Position Title:

Research Associate - Biology

Job Category:

Employees in Training

Employment Type:

Terminal (Fixed Term)

Job Profile:

Research Associate

Job Duties:

Attention:

The Department of Biology in the College of Letters and Sciences at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater seeks a postdoctoral fellow in the area of developmental biology, cell biology, physiology, or molecular genetics beginning August 2026. This is a National Science Foundation funded position with responsibilities for research (75%) and teaching and mentoring undergraduate students (25%). Experience in developmental biology, cell biology, physiology, or molecular genetics is preferred.

Job Details:

This is a National Science Foundation funded postdoctoral position studying circadian gene regulation of metabolism and gene expression during dorsal mesoderm specification in Xenopus laevis  (RUI # 2523434). The project extends preliminary findings that circadian genes (bmal1 and rev-erba) impact the metabolic shift that occurs during dorsal mesoderm specification.  We use a variety of embryological and molecular genetic approaches.  The candidate will be trained in relevant techniques which include genome editing using CRISPR-Cas9, luciferase-based assay systems, RNA-Seq, bioinformatics, microinjection, and microdissection of Xenopus embryos.  The candidate will also receive training in pedagogical techniques by participating in workshops and programs at UWW as well as one on one mentoring by the PI.  The candidate can also expect the PI to support their career goals in the form of publication of results, sharing of reagents and resources, transgenic lines, support for writing grant proposals and attendance at professional meetings.

Responsibilities:

Teaching responsibilities include introductory biology lecture and lab courses and developmental biology. Research expectations include supporting the PI’s grant research, publication of results, mentoring undergraduate research students, and writing grant proposals. All students, faculty, and staff are required to ensure their materials are digitally accessible and utilize standard technology platforms supported by UW-Whitewater. Examples include, but are not limited to, Navigate, Canvas, and Microsoft Office applications – including Outlook, which is essential for university email communications and scheduling.

Department Information:

The Biology department at the University of Wisconsin – Whitewater offers Bachelor’s degrees in Biology, with emphases in five areas: Cell/Physiology; Ecology, Evolution, and Behavior; Honors; Marine Biology and Freshwater Ecology; and Pre-Biomedical Professions. The Biology department has more than 300 majors and ~30 minors. We also serve the University by offering several general education courses and supporting the pre-health professions certificates in dental, medical, physician’s assistant, optometry, and veterinary medicine. Our department is particularly supportive of undergraduate research with dedicated research labs for each of our faculty members, and many of our students have presented their work at national and regional meetings. More information about the College of Letters and Science (https://www.uww.edu/cls) and the Biology department (https://www.uww.edu/cls/departments/biology) may be found at the included links.
 

CONDITIONS OF APPOINTMENT:

University of Wisconsin-Whitewater does not offer H-1B or other work authorization visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain work authorization throughout the employment term. If you have questions regarding this, please contact Human Resources. UW-Whitewater is not an e-verify employer, therefore STEM extensions are not options for work authorization.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Department:

Biology

Compensation:

Well-qualified candidates can expect a starting annual salary of $45,000 - $50,000 commensurate with the candidate's education, related experience, and qualifications.

UW System employees receive an excellent benefit package. To learn more about the UW System's comprehensive benefit package, review the UW System Employee Benefits Brochure.

Required Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Biology is required. ABD candidates may apply but must have their degree completed by the contract start date in August 2026; if not, they will be hired on a one-year contract with the understanding that their degree will be completed before January 2027.

  • Demonstrated interest in teaching at the undergraduate level, ability to effectively communicate complex information to diverse audiences, both verbally and in writing, and ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively with a team are required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in RNA-Seq, Crispr-Cas9, and bioinformatics is helpful but not required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Ability to interact respectfully with people with diverse socioeconomic, cultural and ethnic backgrounds

  • Willingness and ability to be an active participant in following applicable safety rules and regulations including necessary training and drills.

Only complete application packages will be considered. This includes online submission of the following documents:

  • Cover letter/letter of interest

  • Statement of teaching philosophy

  • Statement outlining experiences working with undergraduate researchers

  • Curriculum Vita

  • Names and contact information for three professional references (letters of recommendation may be solicited at a later time)

  • Copies of unofficial graduate transcripts (Official transcripts will be required if offered the position)

Contact Information:

If you have questions regarding this recruitment or if you are unable to complete the application online due to a disability or system problem, please contact us at (262) 472-1024 or hr@uww.edu.

For questions regarding this position, please contact:

Search Committee Chair, Amber Kammeraad

kammeraa@uww.edu

262.472.1092

Applications received by September 19th, 2026, are ensured full consideration. Applications received after that date may be given consideration at the discretion of the search committee. The most qualified applicants will be invited to participate in the next step of the selection process.

CAMPUS INFORMATION:

UW-Whitewater is a thriving public university located in southeastern Wisconsin. It leads the way in providing world-class, affordable higher education programs to more students than neighboring regional comprehensives in the University of Wisconsin System. A collaborative team of 1,300 faculty and staff are devoted to the success of the university’s 11,500 students at its main and Rock County campuses. The team provides high-impact practices and academic programs — online and in person — from associate to doctoral levels. Recognized nationally for affordability, inclusion, and career development, UWW serves approximately one-third first-generation students and boasts strength in many areas, especially business and education. The campus and community embrace the Warhawk Family spirit, supporting the university’s arts and nationally recognized NCAA Division-III level championship athletics. As a proud institution of access, more than 10 percent of undergraduate students use the acclaimed Center for Students with Disabilities — a priority mission since the 1970s.   

  

UW-Whitewater's campuses are located centrally near Milwaukee, Madison, and Chicago, offering easy access to the cultural and commercial opportunities of major metropolitan areas. Near both Lake Geneva and the Wisconsin Dells, the area attracts numerous visitors from across the country. Whitewater is a vibrant college community near the Kettle Moraine State Forest offering area residents seasonal outdoor enjoyment. The nearby Rock County campus is located in Janesville, a town of 60,000 located on the Rock River and known as Wisconsin’s Park Place.

Position Title:

Instructional Designer

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist II

Position Summary:

The Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (CETL) at the University of Wisconsin–Platteville is accepting applications for an Instructional Designer. This position provides support to instructors and departments in the design and development of courses for all UW-Platteville departments. While the development of online courses for programs in the Distance campus is a large part of this work, the position will also provide design and development support for alternative modality and technology-enhanced courses across the university. The instructional design team collaborates with faculty to create effective, engaging, and inclusive learning experiences that align with educational objectives. As an expert in instructional design, this position will support faculty professional development in teaching and learning, helping faculty to enhance teaching practices, leverage technology effectively, and promote inclusive and engaging learning experiences for students. Working in support of distance and alternative mode courses to create effective and engaging learning environments impacts student learning and retention. As part of the CETL team, this position will work closely with faculty, administrators, and other stakeholders to support and promote online and alternative mode courses across the university in a collaborative environment.

This is a 12-month, full-time, benefit and paid leave eligible position, with a salary of $51,500 per year.

Key Job Responsibilities:


  • Manage multiple course development and revision projects, defining scope and overseeing project timelines.
  • Promote collaboration, partnership and relationships among course authors and stakeholders.
  • Analyze instructional materials to identify strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Provide training and technical support directly to learners in settings such as classrooms, labs, clinics, and distance learning mediums.
  • Collaborate with faculty to provide creative solutions to varied instructional challenges.
  • Develop engaging educational experiences that can be objectively measured for effectiveness through assessments that are align with stated learning outcomes.
  • Build and develop course content in Canvas in collaboration with course authors, including pages, modules, assignments, assessments, and other instructional materials.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret data to identify instructional needs and enhance the effectiveness of learning experiences.
  • Design instructional activities that acknowledge and accommodate the diverse needs of learners, showcasing an awareness of cultural and demographic variations.
  • Provide support and guidance in meeting compliance under the Americans with Disabilities Act, including universal course design, copyright issues, and other accessibility considerations.
  • Collaborate with CETL department members to ensure the successful initiation, planning, execution, and completion of faculty development initiatives.
  • Adhere to and advance university standards and procedures for the creation of quality educational products.
  • Promote the use of research in design practices, training content, and evaluation of the effectiveness of outcomes-based learning experiences.
  • Research, evaluate, and recommend learning resources, technologies, materials, and processes to support effective learning experiences.
  • Analyze, test, troubleshoot, resolve issues, and provide feedback regarding learning technologies.
  • Design, develop, or recommend multimedia learning materials and collaborate with multimedia service providers to ensure instructional needs are met.
  • Demonstrate ability to work effectively with limited direction.
  • Communicate effectively in visual, oral, and written form and deliver engaging presentations.
  • Serve on departmental committees and project teams as assigned.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, educational technology, or a related field.

  • 3-5 years of professional work experience as a full-time instructional designer.

  • 1-2 years teaching and/or online learning experience.

  • Practical knowledge of instructional design methods and practices.

  • Demonstrated ability in interpersonal, verbal, written, and presentation skills.

  • Organizational skills to effectively manage multiple projects simultaneously in various development and implementation stages while meeting corresponding deadlines.

  • Experience working with a Learning Management System (LMS) (e.g., Canvas, Brightspace by Desire2Learn, Blackboard, etc.).

Why It’s Great to be a Pioneer:

The University of Wisconsin-Platteville, founded in 1866, offers associate, baccalaureate, and master’s degree programs in a broad spectrum of disciplines including: science, technology, engineering, and mathematics; criminal justice; education; business; agriculture; and liberal arts. The Platteville campus is located in Southwest Wisconsin's largest community, which has a rich history rooted in mining —particularly lead mining —dating back to the early 19th century. The region offers excellent school systems, high-quality medical and hospital facilities, outstanding recreational opportunities, and vibrant businesses and industries. UW-Platteville serves as a cultural and educational center for the Tri-State region of Illinois, Iowa, and Wisconsin.

Instructional and Media Designer

Job Duties:

The University of Wisconsin Oshkosh is seeking a collaborative and innovative Instructional Designer & Learning Technology Specialist to support the READY RURAL initiative. This position serves as the lead for instructional design, educational technology, digital learning, and multimedia development, partnering with faculty and subject matter experts to transform content into engaging, accessible, and workforce-focused learning experiences.

In this role, you will design and develop high-quality instructional materials for online, hybrid, face-to-face, simulation, mobile, and partner-based learning environments. You will create innovative learning resources that support rural healthcare education, including topics such as telehealth, virtual care, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health, home-based care, interprofessional practice, care coordination, and workforce readiness. The position also supports the development of stackable credentials, continuing education offerings, faculty development resources, and workforce training programs.

The successful candidate will provide consultation and support to faculty and staff on instructional technologies, digital learning tools, accessibility, and inclusive teaching practices. Responsibilities include developing multimedia resources such as instructional videos, simulations, interactive learning modules, digital toolkits, and tutorials, while ensuring all learning materials meet quality and accessibility standards.

This position also plays a key role in managing instructional design and media development projects by coordinating timelines, maintaining documentation and reusable resources, training faculty and project personnel on educational technologies, and supporting the collection and interpretation of data to continuously improve learning experiences and program effectiveness.

Universities of Wisconsin also offers an extremely competitive benefits package for 2026 that includes:

  • Health plans, currently starting at $45 per month.

  • 176 hours of vacation per year (prorated for start date).

  • 36 hours of personal holiday, and 9 legal holidays (prorated for start date).

  • 176 Hours of sick leave for first 18 months. After this period, employees can earn up to 96 hours per fiscal year. Accumulates without limit and does not expire.

  • Paid parental leave after six months of continuous employment.

  • Wisconsin Retirement System (pension) with 7.2% employer contribution for 2026.

All employment benefits are subject to change. A full list of current benefits and eligibility requirements can be found on our website.

This position is funded through the READY RURAL grant and is initially offered as a one-year fixed-term appointment. The appointment is renewable annually for up to four years, contingent upon continued grant funding, satisfactory performance, and program needs.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Applies project management principles to course or media design such as defining project scope, establishing milestones, and tracking progress
  • Provides pedagogical consultation services for instructors and staff on instructional toolsand technologies, best practices for digital instructional content, and institutional initiatives
  • Establishes and maintains collaborative relationships with instructors and other academic staff to advance excellence in teaching and learning
  • Reviews courses, media, or other learning products for quality using industry standardsand accessibility best practices
  • Trains and supports instructors and staff to leverage technology and teach implement pedagogy effectively
  • Works with campus partners across pre-production, production, and post-production stages of media development for implementation in courses and other campusinitiatives
  • Creates and maintains documentation on pedagogy, course or media design, templates, instructional technologies, and curates a library of shareable resources
  • Designs and develops learning activities and course content using instructional technologies to foster inclusive and equitable student experiences

Department:

College of Nursing, Health Professions and STEM

Starting at $60,000 commensurate with experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Curriculum and Instruction, Learning Design, Media Production, Healthcare Education, or related field

  • Experience designing online, hybrid, technology-enhanced, or multimedia learning experiences.

  • Experience with learning management systems, digital learning tools, instructional technologies, or media production tools.

  • Experience consulting with faculty, instructors, trainers, or subject matter experts.

  • Strong project management, communication, organization, and technical problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in instructional design, educational technology, learning sciences, curriculum and instruction, healthcare education, or related field.

  • Experience supporting healthcare education, simulation-based education, workforce development, continuing education, or academic-practice training.

  • Experience with tools such as Canvas, Articulate 360, Adobe Creative Cloud, Camtasia, H5P, video platforms, virtual simulation tools, or similar systems.

  • Experience with accessibility standards, Universal Design for Learning, inclusive pedagogy, and AI-assisted instructional design.

  • Experience supporting telehealth, digital health, Virtual Care, or simulation learning environments.

Position Title:

Instructional Designer

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Regular

Job Profile:

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III

Job Duties:

The Center for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning (CATL) is searching for an Instructional Designer to help our faculty thrive as educators in the era of AI and other advanced technologies. The successful candidate will work as part of a collaborative and innovative team of other designers and technologists who strive to support educators from their new faculty orientation through communities of practice for highly experienced instructors. The team is committed to student success. Opportunities exist for individual and program consultations on course design and evidence-based teaching, faculty development programming, and more.  A sample of the job responsibilities includes:

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Collects, organizes, interprets, and disseminates data to identify instructional program needs and enhance effectiveness
  • Advises and supports groups working on program-level curricular design and development by facilitating the work, and by contributing expertise in pedagogy/andragogy, instructional design, and learning technology. May also contribute subject matter expertise.

Position Title:

Instructional Designer - College of Business and Economics

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III

Job Duties:

Attention:

The College of Business and Economics at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater seeks an Instructional Designer (Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III, TL009).

Job Details:

The Instructional Designer serves as a strategic partner and expert pedagogical consultant to faculty and academic units within the College of Business and Economics (CoBE). This position applies advanced instructional design principles, learning theories, and user-experience standards to support the design, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of high-quality learning experiences across face-to-face, hyflex, and online modalities. Operating within the CoBE Tech team, the individual in this role acts as a primary pedagogical and educational technology resource, collaborating with instructional staff to implement effective assessment strategies, select appropriate instructional technologies, and ensure compliance with digital accessibility standards. This position reports directly to the Assistant Dean of Online Education & Technology at the College of Business and Economics. This is a full-time, 12-month Academic Staff position.

Key Job Responsibilities:

1. Instructional Design & Pedagogical Consultation

●       Consult with faculty on the application of learning theories, instructional design models, and evidence-based teaching strategies to develop engaging, learner-centered business education courses

●       Guide instructors in aligning measurable learning outcomes with course activities, structural sequencing, and robust, authentic assessment methodologies

●       Consult with faculty on the ethical integration of Generative, Agentic, and other relevant AI tools (e.g., LLMs, specialized business simulators) into coursework, assisting them in developing clear classroom AI policies and innovative, "AI-active" or "AI-resistant" assessment models

●       Use AI-assisted workflows to accelerate course mapping, draft creative case-study scripts, and generate diverse practice question pools aligned with professional accreditation standards

●       Conduct systematic quality reviews of new and existing courses using recognized quality assurance rubrics (e.g., Quality Matters)

●       Ensure all instructional materials, course layouts, and digital media adhere strictly to federal, state, and institutional accessibility guidelines (ADA, Section 508, and Universal Design for Learning principles)


2. Multimedia Production & Technology Integration

●       Collaborate directly with the CoBE Tech media production team to coordinate the design and seamless integration of high-quality visual graphics, animations, podcast setups, and broadcast-quality video/audio components into course environments

●       Utilize course authoring tools and the institutional Learning Management System (LMS) to build interactive, visually engaging learning modules

●       Evaluate emerging instructional innovations, educational applications, and AI-driven workflow solutions, recommending strategic equipment or software implementation to the Assistant Dean

●       Provide advanced troubleshooting and technical consultation for instructional technology platforms utilized within the college


3. Faculty Training & Support

●       Develop, coordinate, and deliver comprehensive training programs, workshops, and documentation for faculty and staff regarding instructional design best practices and LMS functionality

●       Provide supportive, client-focused technical assistance to educators across a wide spectrum of technical comfort and experience levels

●       As operationally feasible and approved by leadership, this position may include opportunities to teach courses within the college


4. Strategic Alignment & Administrative Support

●       Represent CoBE Tech on campus-wide committees and cross-functional initiatives related to institutional teaching, learning, and digital learning strategies

●       Assist the Assistant Dean with regular technology needs assessments to inform future resource and equipment planning

Department:

College of Business and Economics

Compensation:

Well-qualified candidates can expect a starting annual salary within a range of $65,000 – $75,000.

UW System employees receive an excellent benefit package. To learn more about the UW System’s comprehensive benefit package, review the UW System Employee Benefits Brochure.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Education, or a closely related field

  • Minimum of 2 years of professional experience designing and developing courses within an education environment across multiple modalities (online, hyflex, face-to-face)

  • Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise-level Learning Management Systems (such as Canvas)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior teaching or instructional facilitation experience in a Higher Education setting, with eligibility/desire to teach business-related courses

  • Quality Matters (QM) Peer Reviewer certification

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Autonomy & Initiative: Strong ability to self-motivate, take initiative, prioritize projects, and work highly independently in a fast-paced environment

  • Consultative Communication: Exceptional active listening, written, and oral communication skills, with a proven passion for assisting users of varying technical skill and comfort levels

  • AI Literacy & Tool Fluency: Practical understanding of Generative AI platforms and prompt-engineering frameworks (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot) and how to apply them responsibly to course creation, writing assistance, and workflow automation

  • Design Frameworks: Deep knowledge of adult learning principles, modern assessment strategies, and quality assurance frameworks

  • Accessibility & Compliance: Thorough understanding of digital accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1, ADA, Section 508) and student data privacy regulations (FERPA)

  • Collaborative Mindset: Strong ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, media production specialists, and campus IT partners to achieve unified project goals

  • Ability to interact respectfully with people with diverse socioeconomic, cultural and ethnic backgrounds

  • Willingness and ability to be an active participant in following applicable safety rules and regulations including necessary training and drills

CAMPUS INFORMATION:

UW-Whitewater is a thriving public university located in southeastern Wisconsin. It leads the way in providing world-class, affordable higher education programs to more students than neighboring regional comprehensives in the University of Wisconsin System. A collaborative team of 1,300 faculty and staff are devoted to the success of the university’s 11,500 students at its main and Rock County campuses. The team provides high-impact practices and academic programs — online and in person — from associate to doctoral levels. Recognized nationally for affordability, inclusion, and career development, UWW serves approximately one-third first-generation students and boasts strength in many areas, especially business and education. The campus and community embrace the Warhawk Family spirit, supporting the university’s arts and nationally recognized NCAA Division-III level championship athletics. As a proud institution of access, more than 10 percent of undergraduate students use the acclaimed Center for Students with Disabilities — a priority mission since the 1970s.   

  

UW-Whitewater's campuses are located centrally near Milwaukee, Madison, and Chicago, offering easy access to the cultural and commercial opportunities of major metropolitan areas. Near both Lake Geneva and the Wisconsin Dells, the area attracts numerous visitors from across the country. Whitewater is a vibrant college community near the Kettle Moraine State Forest offering area residents seasonal outdoor enjoyment. The nearby Rock County campus is located in Janesville, a town of 60,000 located on the Rock River and known as Wisconsin’s Park Place.

Position Title:

Instructional Designer and Artificial Intelligence Coordinator

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III

Position Summary:

The University of Wisconsin–Platteville is seeking an Instructional Designer and Artificial Intelligence Coordinator to support innovative teaching and learning initiatives across the institution. This role will design, develop, and enhance instructional activities, programs, and curricula while partnering with faculty to apply evidence-based learning theory, instructional design models, and emerging educational technologies. You will also lead efforts to support the effective and responsible use of Generative AI in higher education by providing consultation, developing resources, and delivering professional development for faculty and students.

This is a full-time, 12-month, benefit and paid leave eligible position with a starting salary of $60,000 per year, commensurate with experience.

Key Job Responsibilities:


AI professional and instructional development support


  • Plan, develop and implement faculty development initiatives and professional engagement activities related to Generative AI in Higher Education.
  • Provide accessible and individualized mentorship and consultation to faculty on pedagogical approaches, learning assessment strategies, and instructional challenges related to Generative AI.
  • Continuously monitor and evaluate current research, trends and best practices related to online learning and AI in order to ensure programs and consultations reflect effective approaches to teaching and learning.
  • Design and curate just-in-time online resources related to Generative AI and AI literacy, including tutorials, templates, asynchronous book groups, and guides, that provide faculty and students with immediate, self-directed support for course development, teaching and learning needs.
  • Help integrate AI tools into institutional operations while ensuring alignment with the UW System strategic priorities, data governance policies, and academic mission.
  • Collaborate with librarians and faculty to design AI literacy instruction and resources for students in order to promote baseline critical thinking around the use, evaluation, and ethics of AI.
  • Assist in developing guidance and instructional best practices for the responsible use of AI in teaching and learning, including considerations related to bias, privacy concerns, and appropriate data use.
  • Partner with the Provost’s Office to translate the University’s AI vision into actionable faculty development.
  • Provide feedback to leadership on trends, risks, and emerging opportunities in AI.
  • Work with ITS to facilitate a collaborative process to communicate and align AI adoption with institutional security and compliance requirements, including data protection and responsible use.

Instructional design in support of alternative delivery courses in UW-Platteville online programs


  • Organize, design, and develop online course developments and revisions in consultation with faculty.
  • Mentor faculty in evidence-based instructional design principles and best practices for online learning while collaborating on course development, building their capacity for effective course design and delivery.
  • Partner with program coordinators to ensure alignment of course development timelines, deliverables, and quality standards, facilitating clear communication and project completion across all stakeholders.
  • Actively engage with the instructional design team through regular communication, resource sharing, and collaborative problem-solving to leverage collective expertise and maintain consistency across course development projects.
  • Pursue continuous improvement through data collection, stakeholder feedback, and professional development opportunities, iteratively enhancing design processes and outcomes based on learner success metrics and evolving practices.

University Support


  • Serve as a member of the Division (CETL, Library, Textbook Center) team, participating in staff meetings, projects and initiatives.
  • Represent CETL on appropriate governance and UW System committees, as requested.
  • Collaborate with Division colleagues on cross-functional initiatives.
  • Develop sufficient knowledge in the functional areas of CETL to be able to provide backup support, as needed.

Other duties, as assigned

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, educational or communication technology, or a related field.

  • 3 years of professional work experience in Instructional Design or AI coordination

  •  Experience working in higher education

  • 1-2 years teaching and/or online learning experience

  •  Experience working with AI

  • Demonstrated ability in interpersonal, verbal, written, and presentation skills.

  •  Organizational skills to effectively manage multiple projects simultaneously in various development and implementation stages while meeting corresponding deadlines.

  • Experience working with a Learning Management System (LMS) (e.g., Brightspace by Desire2Learn, Canvas, Blackboard, etc.).

Why It’s Great to be a Pioneer:

The University of Wisconsin-Platteville, founded in 1866, offers associate, baccalaureate, and master’s degree programs in a broad spectrum of disciplines including: science, technology, engineering, and mathematics; criminal justice; education; business; agriculture; and liberal arts. The Platteville campus is located in Southwest Wisconsin's largest community, which has a rich history rooted in mining —particularly lead mining —dating back to the early 19th century. The region offers excellent school systems, high-quality medical and hospital facilities, outstanding recreational opportunities, and vibrant businesses and industries. UW-Platteville serves as a cultural and educational center for the Tri-State region of Illinois, Iowa, and Wisconsin.

The office location is located at 660 West Washington, Madison, WI. An in-office requirement is expected three (3) days per week, and two days may be worked off-site/remote.  Telecommuting agreements are subject to change at any time.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Major responsibilities of the position include but are not limited to:

·       Assist in developing objectives for learning and ensure they are aligned with business documentation and end-user business processes

·       Assist in facilitating professional development courses including activities and guides learning to align with existing curriculum

·       Assist subject matter experts in developing content, prepare and update specialized instructional materials and assessment tools to align with unit objectives and strategy

·       Assist with needs assessments and evaluations to support ongoing development and improvement of learning experiences for customers

·       Assist in reviewing and analyzing course evaluation data and determine appropriate action to incorporate feedback

·       Assist in measuring participant performance and progress utilizing assessment tools to align with established mission and philosophy

·       Assist others to serve as a subject matter expert, point of contact, and communicates with program affiliates, audiences, and stakeholders providing information and guidance on adult learning materials and standards

Department:

UW-Shared Services provides payroll, benefits, business services, and reporting services to UW employees and universities.  UW-Shared Services exists to standardize processes, consolidate operations, and streamline administrative practices to provide high quality services while improving administrative efficiency and effectiveness. In addition to providing high quality services, Service Operations brings value to UW institutions by reducing administrative burden and cost, thereby allowing them to invest time and resources into activities which are more central to their mission.

Compensation:

The Instructional Designer - Assistant (Official Job Title: Training & Organizational Development Specialist I) is a full-time, salaried (exempt), academic staff, position. Well-qualified candidates can expect a starting annual salary within a range of $50,000. - $65,000. commensurate with the candidate’s education, related experience, and qualifications.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in instructional design or related field OR one (1) year of related working experience in a business setting
  • Knowledge of adult learning theories and instructional design principles in a professional work environment to develop and deliver in-person, virtual and asynchronous learning.
  • Knowledge of or ability to learn complex business processing to design and develop learning experiences
  • Effective written and oral communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Demonstrated skill and experience providing excellent customer service to internal and external customers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) or more years of technical training course development and training for employees
  • Experience in instructional design using Articulate 360,  Captivate or similar tools to design and creating interactive eLearning content
  • Experience with a variety of learning technology including learning management systems, and online conference technology, such as Zoom and Microsoft Teams
  • Basic knowledge of graphic design elements and techniques to create useful and meaningful visuals 
  • Planning, organization, and project management skills
  • Knowledge of Workday or other ERP application fundamentals
  • Experience working in the public sector or higher education

POSITION SPECIFICS​

We are searching for a highly motivated and self-starting Systems Engineer to join our Mission Systems (MS) Department at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State and serve as a Systems Engineer and System Architect. The MS Department mission is to serve as the nexus between technology and operations, leading multidisciplinary initiatives that transform operational capabilities. Through strong partnerships and trusted stakeholder relationships, we facilitate the delivery of integrated solutions to complex, real-world challenges.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

  • Define and develop system architectures for complex, multi-domain defense systems using systems engineering principles

  • Apply modular design approaches to decompose complex systems into manageable, interoperable subsystems and components

  • Develop architectural frameworks, interface definitions, and integration strategies

  • Lead requirements analysis, functional decomposition, and allocation across system hierarchies

  • Conduct trade studies and alternatives analysis to evaluate architectural approaches

  • Create and maintain system architecture documentation including block diagrams, interface control documents, and design specifications

  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams to ensure architectural integrity throughout system development

  • Support verification and validation planning to ensure system architecture meets operational requirements

  • Communicate architectural concepts and technical recommendations to stakeholders and project sponsors

Additional responsibilities for higher-level position includes:

  • Indirect supervision and mentorship of other engineers

  • Monitoring and tracking of funding and budgets

  • Work independently on complex assignments, review progress, and evaluate results

  • Lead communications with external audiences for scheduling, coordination, and business purposes

  • Represent the organization in technical exchanges and program reviews

Required skills/experience areas include:

  • Technical background in Electrical, Systems Engineering, or related engineering discipline

  • 5+ years of experience designing and developing complex systems

  • Past success with systems engineering approaches to system architecture and modular design

  • System decomposition, functional analysis, and interface management

  • System architectures for hardware/software integrated systems (not IT network or enterprise architecture)

  • Understanding of systems engineering principles, processes, and lifecycle management

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work across engineering disciplines

  • Ability to express ideas successfully to drive understanding

  • Past success in writing white papers or report

Preferred skills/experience areas include:

  • Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) training and experience with tools such as Cameo, MagicDraw, or similar

  • Department of Defense or Navy systems development programs

  • Defense system architectures and standards (e.g., DoDAF, UAF, MODAF)

  • Digital engineering practices and tools

  • Requirements management tools (e.g., DOORS, Jama, Innoslate)

  • Open systems architectures and modular open systems approach (MOSA)

  • MATLAB, Simulink, or other system modeling and simulation tools

  • Previous success in a multidisciplinary, team-oriented culture

  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility, if required

Your working location will be on-site in State College, PA, . but options exist for hybrid of on-site/work from home based on project-dependent ability.  Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process. This role requires periodic travel to remote locations.

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Frogs and Salamanders are threatened around the world from infectious diseases, particularly fungal diseases. We work to understand these diseases, how they move around the world, and how to treat them. To accomplish this, we have established a colony of frogs and salamanders. Currently, we are working to develop effective ways to captively-breed selected species to be more resistant to disease. By producing additional individuals, we can also conduct experimental work to identify effective treatments for amphibians threatened by disease. In addition, The Bletz has multiple on-going projects at the intersection of amphibians, disease and the pet trade where sampling preparation and processing are needed using microbiological and molecular techniques.

The Bletz Lab is seeking a part time worker to assist with multiple aspects off this work. The opening is for the Fall 2026 Semester with future semester as a possibility.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

We are seeking a Principal Electro-Optic and Infrared (EO/IR) Systems Engineer to join our Sensors, Signals, and Software Department in the Electro-Optics and Electronics division located in Freeport PA. This department supports DoD acquisitions through electro-optics, electronics, and software trade space definition, exploration, and reduction to inform next generation DoD architectures and capabilities. This spans research in the form of modeling, extensive prototyping, and both functional and environmental test.

You Will:

  • Take on challenges where the path the research may take is not clear, and the outcome is not known or guaranteed

  • Be part of the team leadership that operates in this ambiguous space and develops the executable plan for the rest of the team

  • Perform physics-based modeling to predict the performance of imaging system concepts and designs, such as through the use of the Night Vision Integrated Performance Model (NV-IPM) and MODTRAN.  Execution of these analyses are supported by a deep understanding of the underlying environmental, atmospheric, optics, imager, and human components that the model represents

  • Experience within an organization responsible for manufacturing EO/IR systems

  • Drive system level trade studies to develop architectures and allocate system level requirements across subsystems and engineering disciplines

  • Be heavily involved in camera selection and evaluation covering the full spectrum of visible, shortwave (SWIR), midwave (MWIR), and longwave (LWIR) infrared

  • Lead a team on all aspects of system test (lab, environmental, and field testing) including authoring test plans, identification of the appropriate test equipment, and execution of the tests themselves

  • Leverage prior first-hand experience with building and testing imaging systems to help the team avoid the traditional pitfalls in imaging designs and instead focus that energy towards the high-risk research components

  • Routinely interface with sponsors, customers, and end-users to understand their problems, brainstorm solutions, scope research, communicate the technical aspects of research execution, and convey the significance of results.

  • Track the latest developments in imaging cameras, physics-based modeling, and imaging improvement / enhancement techniques and advise on how and when to integrate them into on-going and future research opportunities

  • Devise, plan, and lead projects solving extremely complex problems that impact the design success of current products or address broad design issues of future products or technologies

  • Coordinate research and development activities between disciplines involving exploration of subject area, definition of scope and selection of problems for investigation, and development of novel concepts and approaches

  • Plan and direct research projects that have substantial impact that extends knowledge and understanding; plan, organize, mentor and advise the work of staff scientists, engineers and technicians

  • Provide input to the strategic direction of the division’s research pursuits by helping to establish the appropriate core competencies and evaluating where our capabilities best align with a sponsor’s needs

  • Perform project planning, budgeting, and scheduling

  • Manage vendors and suppliers, from purchase orders through statements of work

  • Lead other engineers in day-to-day tasking to satisfy stakeholder’s requirements and expectations

  • Provide technical leadership within the department for imaging and EO/IR programs and initiatives

  • Independently manage multiple and/or large electro-optic projects

  • Develop and propose solutions for new applications

  • Perform the role of Trusted Agent to the government to assess and validate state-of-the art imaging systems and solutions from the Defense Industrial Base

  • Propose and lead new initiatives, guide programs of national or international significance, identify future problems, research trends and opportunities, and direct and/or participate in major proposal preparation and presentation

Required skills and experience include:

  • Past success with the design, analysis, procurement, assembly and test of complete electro-optic and infrared (EO/IR) imaging systems for military applications

  • Infrared imaging system experience is a must

  • Radiometry (analysis and laboratory measurements), development of link budgets, prediction of sensor response, and image quality metrics

  • Software tools for instrument control, data analysis, and image processing (LabVIEW, MATLAB, ImageJ, Python, Open CV, etc.)

  • Real-time image processing

  • Laser Range Finders, LiDAR, and other laser systems

  • Specification and use of optical components such as dichroic filters, polarizers, beam splitters, lasers, fast steering mirrors, and shutters

  • Proficient in a discipline core to the design and development of imaging systems prior to transitioning to a system role

  • Operating as a systems engineer for imaging systems

  • Knowledge of various focal plane arrays types, imaging sensors, camera specifications, and video interfaces

  • Past success with visible and infrared imaging system design and characterization

  • Strong knowledge of electro-optical assembly methods including tolerancing and alignments

  • Good working knowledge of physics, electro-mechanical devices and imaging sensors

  • Familiarity with lab instrumentation and tools such as oscilloscopes, integrating spheres, spectroradiometers, interferometers, light sources, motion stages

Preferred skills and experience include:

  • Skills in the use of requirements management tools such as DOORS or Jama

  • Experience with statistical analysis tools and methods to establish measurement uncertainty

  • Familiarity with opto-mechanical design techniques leveraging mechanical design tools such as SOLIDWORKS

  • Familiarity with sensors for the measurement of physical properties (IMUs, ultrasonic, proximity, photoelectric, temperature, etc.) and signal conditioning methods

  • Knowledge of machine vision algorithms and image processing techniques

  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility, if required

This position will be located fully on-site located in Freeport, PA.

 

MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS

Bachelor's Degree - Engineering or Science
19+ years of relevant experience
Required Certifications:
None

ARL operates in a secure information environment involving Unclassified, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and Classified information. Personal electronic devices brought onsite must be registered and may be restricted from certain areas. You must be a U.S. citizen to apply.

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

The Penn State Department of Family and Community Medicine is seeking a part-time (up to 24 hours/week) Research Assistant to support our community-engaged, dynamic, fast-paced Food as Medicine and SNAP-Ed initiatives during the summer months.

This is a summer appointment with the possibility of extension beyond the summer if funding is available. Our team’s goal is to realize a future where everyone can identify, access, prepare, and eat high-quality, culturally appropriate food to achieve optimal health. We develop, test, and implement evidence-based nutrition education and culinary medicine programming for diverse populations in community and clinical settings.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-moving, community-based environment and is deeply passionate about nutrition education, food access, gardening, and health equity. Candidates must be adaptable, energetic, and committed to delivering high-quality programming while supporting evaluation and reporting efforts.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Deliver SNAP-Ed and Food as Medicine programming in low-income community settings, including:
    • Community gardens
    • Food pantries
    • Boys & Girls Clubs
    • Senior centers
    • Other community partner sites
  • Conduct engaging nutrition education sessions, food tastings, and cooking demonstrations
  • Adapt programming for diverse audiences (children, adults, families), including potential digital or social media engagement
  • Support garden-based education and seasonal food programming
  • Collect, manage, and report evaluation data to assess individual- and community-level impact
  • Contribute to continuous quality improvement of programming

Qualifications

  • Exceptional interpersonal skills and strong oral and written communication abilities
  • Strong culinary skills and foundational nutrition knowledge
  • Passion for community nutrition, SNAP-Ed programming, gardening, and health equity
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative team
  • Flexibility and willingness to work in varied community settings
  • Reliable transportation for local travel to partner sites
  • Availability for occasional evening and weekend community events

Preferred Qualifications

  • Fluency in Spanish
  • Experience with SNAP-Ed or other community-based nutrition education programs
  • Experience with gardening or garden-based education
  • Experience with data management and analysis tools (e.g., REDCap, Excel)
  • Background in community nutrition, public health, dietetics, or a related field

To apply, candidates should upload a cover letter with a summary of relevant skills, statement of research interests and goals, current resume, and contact information (name, position title, institution, e-mail address) for at least two professional references. The successful candidate must pass a background check. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is closed.

The FCM Research Division has a dynamic team of researchers involved in diverse, collaborative, primary care-based research, including cancer prevention and survivorship, healthy lifestyles, disease prevention, mental health, pain, substance use, health disparities, and more. Our campus is located in the beautiful town of Hershey, which features a high quality of life including excellent schools, numerous venues for indoor and outdoor activities, and proximity to major metropolitan centers.

The Healthy Environments Action Lab (HEAL) within the Hamer Center for Community Design at Penn State University is dedicated to addressing the intersection of the built environment, community resilience, and human health. We are currently seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Part-Time Research Assistant to join our team and support ongoing research initiatives.

Position Summary

The Part-Time Research Assistant will support various phases of the research lifecycle, from securing funding to publishing results. The ideal candidate will bring a strong foundation in mixed-methods research and possess specific subject matter expertise in climate change, public health, and emergency preparedness.

Key Responsibilities

  • Grant Preparation: Assist in the research, drafting, and assembly of grant proposals and funding applications.
  • Manuscript Preparation & Editing: Draft, review, edit, and format manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed academic journals.
  • Qualitative Analysis: Conduct qualitative data analysis, including coding, thematic analysis, and synthesizing qualitative data.
  • Literature Reviews: Perform comprehensive, systematic literature searches and synthesize findings to support grant proposals, manuscripts, and project development.
  • Project Assistance: Provide general administrative and logistical support for ongoing research projects to ensure milestones are met; other research and administrative tasks as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in psychology, Global Health, or a related field. Current enrollment in or recent completion of a Master’s degree program in Epidemiology, Public Health, or a closely related discipline.
  • Research Experience: Proven experience in manuscript preparation, literature reviews, conducting qualitative interviews, and large-scale cohort analysis.
  • Technical & Methodological Expertise: High proficiency in statistical programming (R, RStudio, SPSS). Experience with epidemiologic methods (e.g., regression modeling, survival analysis, causal inference) and survey design.
  • Subject Matter Knowledge: Strong understanding of concepts related to climate change, community health impacts, and the social determinants of health. Experience in crisis counseling or community resource navigation is highly desirable.
  • Work Ethic: Highly self-motivated, disciplined, and capable of working independently with minimal supervision.
  • Communication: Excellent written and oral communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex health data into reproducible research outputs.
  • Attention to Detail: Exceptional organizational skills and a meticulous approach to data cleaning, editing, and maintaining confidentiality protocols.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with international research fellowships or global health fieldwork.
  • Demonstrated experience in interdisciplinary teamwork and student/stakeholder consulting.
  • Familiarity with additional tools such as Canva, Adobe Photoshop, or Unity/C#.

We are searching for a talented, experienced, organized, detail-oriented, and highly motivated AI/ML Engineer to join our Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) and Data Curation Center of Excellence in the Information Science Division within the All-Domain Analytics and Signatures Office (A2SO) at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL).  This team serves as the foundation for effective machine learning—building, curating, and governing the data that directly determines whether AI/ML models succeed in operationally relevant environments.  You will focus on hands-on work with classified multi-modal data, including imagery/FMV, geospatial and AIS tracks, signals and sensor data, and text-based intelligence reports and develop pipelines, annotation frameworks, and quality assurance processes while gaining deep exposure to state-of-the-art AI/ML research.

ARL is an authorized DoD Skillbridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

  • Label, annotate, and curate multi-modal datasets (imagery/FMV, geospatial, signals, text/documents) to support AI/ML model development and evaluation
  • Design and implement data pipelines for ingestion, transformation, quality control, and cataloging of classified and open-source data
  • Develop and maintain annotation standards, labeling guidelines, and data governance processes to ensure consistency and reproducibility across projects
  • Conduct IV&V of datasets and model outputs to ensure data integrity, label accuracy, and fitness for intended use
  • Collaborate with research scientists, algorithm developers, and program stakeholders to identify, acquire, and prioritize data requirements for specific AI/ML projects
  • Build and maintain data catalogs, metadata schemas, and access-controlled repositories that make curated datasets discoverable and accessible to the broader research team
  • Employ Python, SQL, and annotation platforms (e.g., CVAT, Label Studio) to automate labeling workflows, perform exploratory data analysis, and develop quality metrics
  • Document data provenance, lineage, and known limitations to support model evaluation, reproducibility, and responsible AI practices
  • Collaborate within an Agile development environment as part of a large research team

Required Skills/Experience areas include:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Science, Engineering, or a related technical field
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL for data manipulation, analysis, and pipeline development
  • Familiarity with data annotation tools and workflows (e.g., CVAT, Label Studio, or equivalent)
  • Understanding of machine learning concepts, including how data quality impacts model training, evaluation, and deployment

Preferred Skills/Experience areas include:

  • Experience working with DoD or Intelligence Community data, workflows, or operational environments
  • Familiarity with geospatial data formats (shapefiles, GeoJSON, AIS), imagery/FMV exploitation, or signals data processing
  • Experience with data versioning tools (e.g., DVC, LakeFS) or data catalog platforms
  • Knowledge of IV&V methodologies and quality assurance practices for data-driven systems
  • Exposure to containerized development environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure)
  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the TS/SCI level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility, if required

Your working location will be fully on-site, located in State College, PA or Reston, VA.  Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process.

The College of Information Sciences and Technology (IST) at Penn State is seeking an Instructional Designer to join the Office of Learning Design.

Our college fosters an inclusive and diverse community engaged in innovative interdisciplinary education, research, and service. We prepare leading professionals and scholars who leverage technology and critical thinking to address the complex challenges of an information society. IST is a destination for those who want to advance inclusive, ethical, and value-based discovery at the intersection of people, information, and technology while creatively developing solutions for a sustainable future.

The Office of Learning Design provides services for courses delivered in-residence, online, and in other formats. Our instructional designers collaborate with faculty on the design, revision, and delivery of courses across multiple modalities. We offer faculty development in a variety of formats and venues. Our team contributes to the larger community at Penn State and beyond through developing strategic partnerships and leading critical projects and committees.

  • Develop and integrate instructional media and technology to enhance teaching and learning and ensure their effective use.

  • Design and evaluate assessments and learning experiences that measure student achievement, inform course improvement, and incorporate feedback.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Learning Design team within the College of the Liberal Arts is seeking an Instructional Designer to oversee all aspects of designing, developing, and managing online course portfolios.

This position is not focused on technical support. Instead, the key responsibilities of the Instructional Designer are centered on collaborating closely with faculty authors to ensure course content and assessments enhance learning and support student success.

This involves the evaluation of online lesson content and assessments using knowledge of online pedagogy, interdisciplinary research, and evidence-based best practices.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Meeting with faculty authors to design and develop content for asynchronous online courses, including those that enroll adult learners.

  • Providing guidance to faculty authors based on established learning frameworks.

  • Reviewing faculty-created course content and assessments and providing research-based recommendations to enhance student learning.

  • Acting as the project manager for courses in development to monitor progress; determine, set, and ensure others on the team adhere to schedules and deadlines.

  • Collaborating with multimedia specialists in the creation of course-related multimedia elements (animations, illustrations, videos, virtual environments) and managing the completion of these elements within an established timeframe.

  • Overseeing the work of Instructional Design Assistants for the setup and maintenance of approximately 35 courses each semester.

  • Ensuring that all course content follows copyright and accessibility standards.

  • Researching and promoting innovative trends and technologies that impact online learning in higher education.

Qualifications:

  • Advanced knowledge of learning theories, best practices for online learning, and current research in the field

  • Ability to draw from the above knowledge in their course design, reviews, and recommendations

  • Outstanding project management skills

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication (written and verbal) skills

  • Ability to work collaboratively with team members and faculty partners, as well as being comfortable delegating work to others

  • Experience with Canvas or another learning management system

POSITION SPECIFICS​

We are searching for highly motivated Systems Engineers to join our Systems Engineering Department in the Undersea Systems Office at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State.  This role will support the development of complex physical undersea systems, including advanced vehicles, sensors, and integrated hardware/software technologies for undersea applications. This is not an IT, cloud, or enterprise systems position. This role focuses on traditional systems engineering for defense hardware, spanning concept development, system architecture, subsystem integration, test, and transition to fielded military systems. This department's focus is on tailoring and on applying rigor using the systems engineering process.  You will have the opportunity to contribute heavily to physical systems development, from conceptual definition into design, test, then transition into production. USO designs, develops, validates, and maintains a suite of large-scale undersea warfare models and simulations used by technology developers, analysts, the Navy, and its allies. We serve as a research center of excellence in undersea weapons, unmanned undersea vehicles, and advanced sonars. We support our national security and undersea warfare sponsors through the development and demonstration of science and technology with the expertise, tools, and processes to take concepts from the early developmental phase through transition to industry and the fleet.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

  • Translate stakeholder needs into system-level requirements and architectures

  • Perform analysis of alternatives and develop system concepts for hardware‑centric undersea platforms and payloads

  • Conduct system and requirements decomposition, interface definition, and integration planning

  • Support model-based systems engineering (MBSE), system modeling, and hardware/software integration

  • Develop verification and validation strategies, test plans, and test procedures for physical prototypes and fielded systems

  • Participate in and support lab, dockside, and at-sea test events

  • Collaborate regularly with engineering teams, program sponsors, Navy partners, and program management

  • Identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and support lifecycle decision-making

Additional responsibilities for higher level positions includes:

  • Organize and direct a multi-disciplinary and diverse engineering team

  • Provide technical leadership within the division programs

  • Plan and direct research projects that have substantial impact that extends knowledge and understanding

  • Propose and lead new initiatives; guide programs of national or international significance; identify future problems, research trends, and opportunities

Required skills/experience areas include:

  • Applying systems engineering to complex physical systems, preferably in defense, aerospace, maritime, or robotics domains

  • Experience collaborating in multi-disciplinary, team-oriented cultures

  • Ability to express ideas successfully to drive understanding

  • Past success in writing white papers or reports

  • Past success in a lead role, organizing, managing, and directing, multi-disciplinary teams, while contributing and assisting in project management

  • Past success while leading or contributing to technical proposals and white papers

Preferred skills/experience areas include:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Computer, Systems Engineering or related engineering discipline.

  • Unmanned underwater systems development

  • Hardware integration, prototype testing, or system-level test events

  • Past success using requirements and MBSE tools (Cameo, DOORS, Jama, etc.)

  • Working knowledge of DoD acquisition, especially Department of the Navy systems engineering processes

  • Exposure to environmental qualification, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or embedded system integration

  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility, if required

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Position Summary

The Penn State College of Medicine, Department of Molecular and Precision Medicine and Department of Medicine, seek a PhD-trained Senior Bioinformatician / Research Data Scientist to support an expanding portfolio of translational and precision health research programs. The successful candidate will develop, implement, and evaluate advanced computational and statistical approaches to analyze high-dimensional biological data, including multi-omics datasets. This role will collaborate closely with faculty investigators across disciplines—including aging biology, infectious diseases, cancer biology, and mucosal immunology—to integrate genomics, transcriptomics (including single-cell), proteomics, and related datasets into mechanistic and translational insights.

The Senior Bioinformatician will serve as a key computational partner across multiple projects, contributing to study design, data analysis, visualization, and interpretation while helping to build sustainable computational infrastructure within the department.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, select, and apply advanced computational and statistical methods to analyze complex biological datasets
  • Perform integrative multi-omics analyses (e.g., genomics, transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq, proteomics, epigenomics)
  • Utilize and implement tools such as Scanpy and other single-cell analysis frameworks
  • Develop and maintain reproducible workflows in Python and related programming environments
  • Collaborate with faculty to design computational strategies aligned with research aims
  • Develop novel algorithms, software tools, and analytical pipelines to address emerging research questions
  • Generate high-quality visualizations and analytical summaries for manuscripts, grant applications, and presentations
  • Contribute to interpretation of results and development of new hypotheses
  • Support training of trainees and junior investigators in data analysis best practices
  • Ensure data management, documentation, and reproducibility standards are maintained

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Biology, Biomedical Sciences, Biostatistics, Computer Science, or related field
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing high-dimensional biological or omics datasets
  • Strong programming skills in Python (required) and familiarity with data science frameworks
  • Experience with single-cell data analysis tools (e.g., Scanpy or similar platforms)
  • Experience integrating multi-omics datasets
  • Ability to work collaboratively across interdisciplinary research teams
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Background in biology, immunology, cancer biology, infectious diseases, aging, or related biomedical fields
  • Experience working in an academic medical center environment
  • Familiarity with high-performance computing environments and cloud-based analysis
  • Track record of contribution to peer-reviewed publications

Impact of the Role

This position will serve as the senior bioinformatics lead across multiple translational research initiatives, enabling integration of large-scale datasets into biologically meaningful discoveries. The role is central to advancing precision health initiatives and strengthening the department’s computational research capacity.

Master's Degree

We are searching for a Division Head for the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) Division in the Fluid Dynamics and Acoustics Office (FDAO) at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. The CFD Division Head will lead a premier group of approximately fifteen of engineers and research faculty in meeting the mission of bringing state-of-the-technology tools, talent and leading-edge computational fluid dynamics to our DoD and industrial sponsors. The Division Head, along with immediate reports, will develop and mature business relationships and programs with other ARL offices, industry, and government sponsors.   • Lead technical developments and improvements in field of Computational Fluid Dynamics including but limited to code development, V&V, and applications in new and evolving tools and methodologies to solve complex flows.   • Provide technical oversight of complex simulations and interface across the organization to ensure high quality research output

  • Perform organizational leadership to the CFD Division, to include personnel management, recruitment, development, and retention of employees

  • Past success as a Principal Investigator in this field

  • Strong research track record of computational fluid dynamics with a focus in hydromechanics, hydroacoustics, maneuvering and controls, propulsion systems or related discipline

  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Top Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility

  • Successful history of proposed and awarded research projects evidenced through securing external research funding

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Join Penn State IT’s innovative Data Empowered Learning team, dedicated to enhancing student success through cutting-edge learning analytics tools like Course Insights and Elevate. We are seeking a skilled Front-End Developer to design, build, and maintain intuitive and impactful user interfaces for our next generation of learning analytics applications. 
 

The successful candidate will bring strong front-end engineering skills together with sound systems thinking, product-minded design judgment, and the ability to work in a dynamic team based environment. This role requires an engineer who can translate educational use cases and analytics into reliable, user-centered software solutions, while thoughtfully incorporating AI-assisted features where appropriate. 


This is not a prompt-only prototyping role. We are seeking an engineer who can pair thoughtful product and systems design with disciplined implementation, testing, and evaluation. Candidates should be able to communicate effectively with technical stakeholders, articulate architectural decisions and tradeoffs, discuss code and data flows in depth, and demonstrate a strong understanding of software quality.


Responsibilities:

  • Develop, test, and deploy high-quality, responsive, and accessible user interfaces for learning analytics applications using Angular.

  • Collaborate closely with backend developers, data scientists, and educational stakeholders to implement application features.  

  • Work within our established NX monorepo structure and NodeJS development environment.

  • Maintain and enhance existing Angular applications, ensuring performance, scalability, accessibility, and long-term maintainability.

  • Troubleshoot and debug front-end and integration issues across application layers 

  • Apply sound software engineering and design patterns when integrating AI-assisted capabilities, including human-in-the-loop workflows, fallback behaviors, logging, and monitoring.

  • Research and integrate advancements in front-end technologies, AI application development practices, and responsible engineering best practices.
     

Required Qualifications:

  • Proven experience as an Applications Developer, Front-End Developer, or similar role.

  • Strong proficiency in modern Angular framework, TypeScript, HTML5, and CSS3/SCSS.

  • Experience working within a NodeJS environment for development workflows, including build tools and package management.

  • Experience consuming RESTful APIs and integrating front-end applications with backend services.

  • Proficiency with version control systems, particularly Git.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and commitment to producing maintainable, production-quality software.

  • Demonstrated ability to think beyond feature delivery and contribute to application architecture, technical design, and system reliability.

  • Familiarity with user-centered design, design thinking, or related approaches for translating stakeholder needs into effective software solutions.

  • Ability to evaluate technical tradeoffs and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical partners.

  • U.S Citizenship - sponsored VISAs are unavailable for this position.

Bachelor's Degree
3+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted

None

 

Desired Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Science, or a related field.

  • Familiarity with NX monorepos or similar monorepo management tools.

  • Experience with data visualization libraries (e.g., D3.js, Chart.js).

  • Understanding of UI/UX principles and accessibility standards (WCAG).

  • Experience working in Higher Education or EdTech environments.

  • Familiarity with Python for backend development.

  • Familiarity with AI-enabled application development, including prompt orchestration, retrieval-augmented workflows, agent-based patterns, or integration with LLM-powered services.

  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools productively while maintaining engineering rigor, code quality, and accountability.

The Data Empowered Learning team is primarily located on campus at University Park, and this position requires a partial in-person presence of at least 1–2 days in the office per week to drive collaborative success. While local hybrid presence is required for the role, the team offers flexibility regarding daily work hours to accommodate individual schedules.

  • Configure and manage operating systems (Windows and Linux), applications (commercial and government), networks (IPs, subnets, etc.), and network equipment (switches)
