title: Post Doc Res Assoc
description: The Ho lab at the University of Utah is launching an ambitious program to systematically discover, map, and therapeutically harness mitochondrial microproteins to reverse mitochondrial dysfunction in rare and common disease. Microproteins encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs) are an enormous, largely uncharted space of short proteins that regulate core aspects of mitochondrial metabolism, import, and stress responses, and represent a new class of therapeutic targets. Building on our leadership in microprotein discovery and function, we are now expanding in Utah to recruit multiple postdoctoral fellows to apply high throughput methods and machine/deep learning to unlock the full potential of the dark proteome.

title: Lab Technician
description: The Luo Lab at The University of Utah is seeking a full-time Lab Technician to join our team investigating the neural circuits underlying decision-making and attention. We combine sophisticated behavioral paradigms in rats with large-scale in vivo electrophysiological recordings and causal circuit manipulations using optogenetics. The successful candidate will be an integral member of our research group, providing technical support for ongoing projects and contributing to the lab's vibrant scientific environment.

title: REFRAME Platform Architect
description: This is a repost; previous applicants need not reapply. This position supports the REFRAME project, a multi-year, externally funded research initiative led by NC State University. The project aims to deliver a modular, AI-enabled, open-source platform for feedstock-agnostic evaluation of future biomass. It will integrate legacy open-source models, novel surrogates, shared metadata schemas, and a large language model (LLM) to enhance accessibility for varied stakeholders. Leveraging well-characterized agricultural and food processing residues, REFRAME will generate insights into historically underfunded circular biomass streams and provide deployment-ready tools for end-to-end scenario analysis, counterfactual modeling, and decision support across the value chain. The Platform Architect will play a central role in designing and operationalizing the technical backbone of this platform in close collaboration with faculty, research staff, and external partners. The Platform Architect is a senior technical leadership role that will lead the software and infrastructure development for the digital backbone for the REFRAME project. This digital backbone is the central nervous system for developing, deploying, monitoring, and governing all machine learning models related to the project. The platform architect will be responsible for strategic roadmapping of infrastructure, system design, tech-stack selection, devOps, security & compliance, workflow integration, and process optimization, ensuring the platform’s scalability, reliability, and efficiency. The architect will also work closely with the project manager and software development personnel, bridging gaps between project personnel and development personnel to ensure that ML models can transition from research workflows to scalable, secure, and reliable production environments efficiently. The Platform Architect is a senior technical leadership role responsible for defining the strategy, design, and implementation of our solution-specific Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) platform. This platform is the central nervous system for developing, deploying, monitoring, and governing all machine learning models related to the project. The Architect bridges the gap between data science experimentation and production engineering rigor, ensuring that ML models can transition from research workflows to scalable, secure, and reliable production environments efficiently. Platform Vision and Architecture : Strategic Roadmapping: Define the technical vision and multi-year roadmap for the end-to-end ML platform, aligning it with project and research objectives and data science needs (including GenAI/LLM capabilities). System Design: Architect, design, and document a robust, scalable, and cost-efficient platform covering the entire ML lifecycle: Data Ingestion, Feature Store, Model Training, Model Registry, Model Serving/Inference, and Monitoring. Technology Selection: Evaluate, select, and integrate appropriate cloud-native services (AWS, Azure, or GCP), hybrid and on-prem computing resources, and open-source MLOps tools (e.g., Kubeflow, MLflow, Airflow) to build a cohesive ecosystem. MLOps and Delivery Excellence : Automation: Lead the implementation of MLOps pipelines using CI/CD practices to automate model training, testing, validation, deployment, and automated retraining workflows. Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Design and enforce IaC standards (Terraform/CloudFormation) for provisioning and managing all underlying compute, networking, and storage resources (e.g., Kubernetes clusters, GPU instances). Feature Engineering: Define shared data and feature management patterns to ensure consistency and reuse across model training and inference workflows. Governance, Security, and Compliance: Model Governance: Implement standards for model versioning, lineage tracking, and compliance to ensure models are traceable, reproducible, and meet ethical AI principles. Security: Architect security measures, including network segmentation, access control (IAM/RBAC), and data encryption across the entire ML pipeline. Performance & Cost Optimization: Establish comprehensive monitoring and alerting for model performance (drift, bias) and infrastructure metrics, driving continuous optimization for performance and cloud costs (FinOps). Technical Leadership and Collaboration: Cross-Functional Partnership: Act as the primary technical point of contact, collaborating closely with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Software Engineers, Product Managers, domain scientists, industry partners, process engineering and systems modeling experts. Documentation: Create and maintain high-quality architectural diagrams, reference implementations, and technical documentation.

title: TRIO Upward Bound Instructor
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Upward Bound Program is an early intervention pre-college program that helps students prepare for higher education. Upward Bound brings high school students to college campuses after school, on the weekends, and during the summer to receive instruction in mathematics, laboratory sciences, composition, literature, and foreign languages. Tutoring, counseling, mentoring, cultural enrichment, and work-study programs are additional components to the Upward Bound Program. The NC State University Program serves five high schools (Vance County HS, Louisburg HS, Bunn HS, Franklinton HS, and East Wake HS). The Program has been a part of the University since 1978 and has assisted hundreds of students to enroll in college and gain a college degree. The Upward Bound Program is looking for Instructors that will be responsible for: Developing and executing lesson plans in assigned curriculum courses in the following areas: High School Mathematics High School English High School Science, including physical science and chemistry Computer Science, especially AI Providing written evaluations on each program participant

title: Assistant Professor of Linguistics
description: The Department of English at North Carolina State University invites applications for one full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Linguistics. As a faculty member, you will contribute to our undergraduate major and M.A. concentration through teaching, research, and service. The area of specialization is open; however, we are particularly interested in candidates specializing in either: corpus linguistics, with a focus on syntax, morphology, or the lexicon; or experimental sociolinguistics and/or experimental psycholinguistics. If you are passionate about advancing linguistic research, committed to excellence in teaching and mentorship, and eager to contribute to a collaborative academic community, we encourage you to apply.

title: County Extension Director
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Working for NC State Extension allows you to teach without being tied to a classroom and school bell. While our employees are located in NC County offices, they reap the benefits of employment at NC State University. Some of our benefits include: Paid time off Paid tuition Health Insurance Flexible Scheduling Retirement Savings Supplemental Benefits Programs WolfPerks! You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. The County Extension Director is a leadership position with Cooperative Extension at North Carolina State University. The major responsibility of the job is to provide leadership for and coordinate the efforts of the county Extension staff in developing an effective total county Extension educational program in cooperation with North Carolina A&T State University’s Cooperative Extension Program . The position requires a dynamic individual to provide visionary leadership for a comprehensive Extension program to meet the needs of all segments of the population. The County Extension Director serves as the County Extension administrative leader with responsibilities for administration, public policy issues, and community/leadership development. The County Extension Director is responsible for maintaining an effective advisory leadership system representative of all program areas. The County Extension Director provides leadership and expertise in coordinating/securing resource development for all program areas. Responsibilities include marketing Extension programs and impacts. The County Extension Director must maintain a strong, collaborative relationship in assisting the staff in delivering educational programs with county government input and support. Also, to meet the needs of county citizens, the position must network and collaborate with agencies and organizations, county departments, schools, town officials, area agencies, and University and Extension personnel. The position will be responsible for coordinating staff development, and training. The individual must demonstrate the ability to plan, organize, and work well with people.

title: Assistant Professor - Plant Pathology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor to advance its undergraduate educational mission in plant pathology while developing a complementary research program. This 9-month faculty position provides leadership in delivering and evolving the undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, integrating active learning, case-based instruction, emerging technologies, and innovative approaches to prepare students for careers and continued study in the discipline. The role includes approximately two to three courses annually, spanning foundational plant pathology instruction, team-taught and specialized courses, and the development of undergraduate and distance education offerings. In this role, you will help shape how plant pathology is taught, experienced, and applied across the curriculum while building a research program that complements the department’s strengths. Your scholarship may engage areas such as plant disease diagnostics and management, fungal biology, soilborne pathogens, plant disease ecology, plant–soil–microbe systems, or epidemiology. You will have opportunities to develop innovative teaching and research programs, create meaningful experiential learning experiences, and foster collaboration across disciplines while engaging students in discovery and inquiry. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Teaching and Mentoring: Deliver and modernize core undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, including PP 315 (Principles of Plant Pathology) and its laboratory component, through innovative approaches such as active learning, case studies, emerging technologies, and distance education. Contribute to graduate, team-taught, and specialized courses while helping shape curriculum innovation and assessment across the program. Create meaningful opportunities for students to connect classroom learning with research, discovery, and other experiential learning. Mentor undergraduate researchers, graduate students, and postdoctoral scholars in their academic and professional development. Research and Discovery: Build and sustain an active, externally visible research program that complements departmental strengths and advances knowledge in plant pathology. Develop collaborative research that engages students and connects teaching, discovery, and emerging areas such as soilborne pathogens, fungal biology, and plant–soil–microbe interactions. Pursue scholarly work, external support, and partnerships that expand the reach and impact of your research. Contribute to a culture of inquiry and discovery across the department and broader scientific community. Department Service and Professional Engagement: Contribute to department, college, and university priorities through service, faculty governance, and academic leadership. Foster interdisciplinary collaborations and professional partnerships that strengthen teaching, research, and engagement. Engage with the broader scientific community through professional leadership, manuscript and grant review, and scholarly activities. Support outreach and initiatives that enhance the visibility and impact of the department and university while fostering a collegial, inclusive, and productive academic environment. If you are an innovative educator, collaborative researcher, and engaged academic who is passionate about advancing plant pathology education and discovery, we encourage you to apply.

title: Shipping & Receiving Assistant
description: Join our team as a Shipping and Receiving Assistant , a vital role supporting faculty, staff, and students across the Centennial Biomedical Campus. In this hands-on position, you will support daily receiving, asset tracking, mail runs, event setup, fleet care, and heavy equipment operation. You will also safely handle specialized items, including refrigerated supplies, controlled substances, anatomy specimens, and hazardous diagnostic samples. Key Responsibilities: This position plays a crucial role in supporting the sponsored activities of faculty, staff, and students within the College by performing a variety of tasks and responsibilities across different areas: Sign for and inventory all packages received daily from delivery trucks, confirming their accuracy against delivery manifests, including perishable, infectious, controlled substances, and valuable items. Conduct detailed inventories of all packages delivered to the Centennial Biomedical Campus, including various buildings and units within the college. Deliver packages to designated locations within the college campus, obtaining recipient signatures and recording delivery dates, especially for perishable items requiring refrigerated storage. Assist with the annual inventory of assets spread across multiple campuses and locations, including locating items, recording their details, and updating the university asset management system. Assist the Mail Room Manager with mail operations, including operation of the mail machine, deliveries and pickups from the local post office, courier runs, and retrieving pathology samples from the NC Department of Agriculture Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory. Transport veterinary diagnostic samples to and from diagnostic laboratories, ensuring proper handling of infectious materials. Handle formaldehyde-preserved large and small animal cadavers for the Anatomy Lab, including transportation and use of protective equipment. Receive, document, and transport infectious disease samples for the Vector Born Laboratory to avoid public health risks. Locate and tag new purchases made by the college, documenting their details and entering them into the inventory database. Assist in documenting, tagging, and removing surplus items for disposal, adhering to safety procedures, and maintaining accurate inventory records. Assist with setting up and logistics for special events at the college, including deliveries, setup, and furniture rearrangement. Operate heavy equipment such as forklifts, pallet jacks, backhoes, dump trucks, and box trucks, ensuring proper safety training and certification. Assist with light maintenance on departmental vehicles, including fueling, cleaning, and scheduling maintenance and repairs. Assist with various moves within the college, including office and laboratory moves, and transporting heavy or delicate equipment. Provide customer service throughout the college and the College of Engineering Biomedical Engineering department, assisting customers with their needs. Demonstrate knowledge of various programs administered by Shipping and Receiving and explain them to others. Address various requests from customers across campus, ensuring policies and procedures are communicated and followed. Abilities Necessary to Perform Job Duties: Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations, on a frequent basis.

title: Transportation Supervisor
description: Are you a logistical mastermind who loves the fast-paced world of catering and events? We are seeking a dynamic and organized Catering Driver Supervisor to lead our transportation and beverage/equipment teams. In this role, you will be the backbone of our event execution, ensuring that all catering equipment, beverages, and supplies are delivered safely, efficiently, and on schedule. Beyond driving, you will manage our vehicle fleet, oversee inventory, and lead a dedicated team to deliver outstanding service across the University. If you are a proactive leader with a knack for logistics and a commitment to excellence, we want you on our team! Key Responsibilities Team Leadership & Scheduling Supervise & Support: Lead, motivate, and manage the catering transportation and beverage/equipment teams. Staff Scheduling: Utilize specialized departmental software to create, distribute, and monitor employee schedules. Clear Communication: Foster a collaborative team environment and maintain professional communication with multiple levels of University employees, peers, and customers. Logistics, Driving & Event Execution Delivery Operations: Develop, distribute, and monitor the daily delivery and transportation schedules. Behind the Wheel: Drive various delivery trucks and vehicles to execute catering and dining deliveries safely. Event Support: Load and unload cargo at each location; actively assist with event setup and breakdown. Fast-Paced Adaptability: Thrive and maintain professionalism under pressure in a high-energy, fast-moving environment. Fleet Management & Safety Fleet Care: Ensure a well-maintained, clean, and safe fleet of catering and dining vehicles. Training & Records: Establish and maintain a driver training program and a comprehensive fleet service record-keeping system. Preventative Maintenance: Oversee routine inspections, fueling, and preventative maintenance schedules in strict accordance with the NCSU Motor Pool guidelines. Inventory & Supply Control Inventory Management: Oversee inventory control, receipt, storage, and issuance of a wide variety of catering supplies, materials, and equipment. Physical Stamina: Ability to handle physical demands including bending, twisting, pulling, pushing, and standing for extended periods. Lifting Capability: Must be able to lift 30 pounds above the head, and up to 60 pounds on rare occasions (with or without reasonable accommodation). We offer a collaborative, team-oriented workspace where your leadership directly impacts the success of major University events. If you are ready to drive your career forward, apply today!

title: Landscape Construction Project Manager
description: Do you have a passion for landscape construction and enjoy turning plans into well-executed projects? NC State University is seeking a Landscape Construction Project Manager to help shape and improve the campus landscape through thoughtful planning, strong project management, and a commitment to quality. In this role, you will manage landscape construction projects from planning and design through construction and final closeout. You’ll collaborate with University project managers, designers, consultants, contractors, and Facilities leadership to keep projects on schedule, within budget, and aligned with university standards. Your expertise in landscape construction, horticulture, hardscaping, irrigation, and stormwater systems will help ensure projects are built to last and successfully transition into ongoing campus maintenance. This is an opportunity to see your work become part of the NC State campus while working with a collaborative team dedicated to creating safe, functional, beautiful, and sustainable outdoor spaces. If you’re ready to bring your landscape construction expertise to projects that have a lasting impact on the NC State campus, we encourage you to apply! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Manage landscape construction projects from planning and design through construction and final closeout, monitoring scope, schedules, budgets, milestones, and overall project progress . Use AiM, shared documentation, and team collaboration tools to track project information and maintain accurate project records. Identify and resolve project challenges and operational roadblocks while adapting project scope to meet university priorities. Develop, review, and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to promote consistent and efficient project delivery. Manage project documentation, including contracts, competitive bids, product warranties, project records, and final closeout materials. Serve as the primary point of contact for project-related communication and provide timely, clear updates to stakeholders and leadership. Collaborate with University Project and Design Managers, designers, consultants, contractors, and internal Facilities teams throughout planning, design, and construction. Provide concise project status, milestone, and issue updates during weekly leadership meetings. Build strong working relationships with Grounds Leadership, Landscape Construction Services, Waste Reduction and Recycling, Grounds Planning, and other campus partners. Participate in design reviews and evaluate project plans to ensure alignment with university standards and industry best practices. Apply knowledge of landscape construction, plant and tree identification, hardscape construction, commercial irrigation systems, and stormwater control measures (SCMs) . Conduct project site inspections to verify construction meets approved designs, specifications, quality standards, and campus expectations. Identify construction issues and coordinate solutions with project partners to maintain quality and project objectives. Lead project closeout activities, including final inspections and walk-throughs, verification and filing of as-built drawings, and transition of completed projects to the Grounds Maintenance team.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: This position will support an ongoing project with the NCDOT to evaluate road ripples and the position may generally involve supporting other short duration experimental mechanical evaluations of asphalt concrete mixtures. The position will also provide some laboratory and project management support. The main duties and responsibilities include: Conduct and synthesize literature and agency-practice reviews related to road ripples, including potential formation mechanisms, diagnostic methods, contributing factors, and pavement-performance implications. Coordinate and participate in field and forensic evaluations of North Carolina pavements exhibiting road ripples, including site selection, records and data compilation, field testing, sample collection, laboratory evaluation, and comparative analysis. Plan, conduct, and analyze laboratory and modeling studies to evaluate residual moisture in asphalt mixtures and the potential short- and long-term effects of road ripples on pavement performance. Draft quarterly reports and monthly reports to support the aforementioned research project and/or similar project. May be asked to participate in other research projects related to aforementioned topic as projects are awarded. Coordinate laboratory management activities in support of the asphalt mixture analysis group tasks. This may include coordinating graduate students for cleaning, ensuring PPE is appropriately worn, ensuring supplies are ordered, and coordinating on calibrations.

title: Accounting Technician
description: The Accounting Technician for the Department of Clinical Sciences (DoCS) is responsible for providing financial and administrative support for departmental operations, including state-appropriated funds, discretionary funds, foundation/gift funds, grants, and sales and service center receipts. This position supports the department through financial reconciliation, procurement processing, travel management, reimbursement processing, and compliance monitoring. The role works closely with faculty, staff, the Department Accountant, and the CVM Business Office (CVMBO) to ensure accurate financial management and adherence to university policies and state regulations. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, customer service, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines are essential for success in this position.

title: Assistant Director, Facilities HR Programs
description: The Assistant Director of Facilities Human Resources (FHR) serves as a key member of the Facilities Human Resources leadership team and provides strategic direction, oversight, and continuous improvement for a comprehensive portfolio of HR programs that support the employee lifecycle across the Facilities Division. Reporting directly to the Director of Facilities Human Resources, this position leads a team of 3-4 HR professionals and is responsible for advancing division-wide initiatives related to talent acquisition, onboarding, training and development, engagement and recognition . As a trusted HR leader and consultant, the Assistant Director works collaboratively with Facilities executives, managers, supervisors, employees, and University Human Resources to ensure the delivery of responsive, consistent, and high-quality HR services that support the division's operational goals and NC State University's strategic priorities. The position plays a critical role in fostering a positive workplace culture by developing programs and practices that enhance employee engagement, strengthen workforce capability, promote employee success, and support long-term talent retention. This role combines strategic program leadership, staff supervision, workforce analytics, change management, and process improvement . The Assistant Director evaluates organizational needs, identifies emerging workforce trends, and implements innovative solutions designed to improve the employee experience and operational effectiveness. The position also serves as a senior HR advisor on complex employee and organizational issues, providing guidance that balances business needs, policy compliance, legal requirements, and employee well-being. This position offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on the Facilities Division by shaping HR programs, developing talent, improving organizational processes, and ensuring employees have the resources and support necessary to thrive and contribute to the University's mission. Individuals who are passionate about building innovative HR programs, developing people, leading teams, solving complex organizational challenges, and creating meaningful workplace improvements are encouraged to apply and join the Facilities Human Resources team at NC State University. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Provide strategic leadership and oversight for division-wide programs related to recruitment, onboarding, employee development, engagement and recognition . Lead the design, implementation, assessment, and continuous improvement of HR initiatives that enhance the employee experience and support Facilities Division goals. Oversee recruitment and talent acquisition strategies , partnering with leaders and hiring managers to strengthen hiring practices and improve the attraction, selection, and retention of high-quality talent. Oversee onboarding programs that ensure a welcoming, informative, and consistent experience for new employees while supporting successful integration into the organization. Assess organizational and workforce development needs and implement training, leadership development, mentoring, e-learning, and professional growth opportunities for employees and supervisors. Develop and execute employee engagement initiatives by analyzing survey results, feedback, workforce trends, and organizational data to identify opportunities for improvement. Manage employee recognition programs that celebrate achievements, reinforce organizational values, and promote a culture of appreciation and belonging. Supervise, coach, mentor, and evaluate a team of HR professionals , establishing performance expectations and ensuring high-quality, customer-focused service delivery. Research and analyze complex HR issues and develop practical, compliant, and business-focused solutions aligned with University policies, employment regulations, and organizational priorities. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with Facilities leadership, University Human Resources, and campus partners to ensure consistent application of HR practices and successful implementation of initiatives. Utilize workforce data, operational metrics, and employee feedback to evaluate program effectiveness, identify trends, and support strategic decision-making. Develop and deliver presentations, training programs, communications, reports, and recommendations to a variety of stakeholders, including senior leadership. Oversee HR records, reporting processes, and data management activities while ensuring confidentiality, data integrity, and compliance with applicable requirements. Monitor changes in HR best practices, employment law, higher education trends, and workforce strategies and recommend program enhancements as appropriate. Lead HR technology initiatives and process improvement efforts, including collaboration on the continued enhancement and utilization of AiM and other HR systems to improve data management, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Support organizational change initiatives and special projects that advance Facilities Division and University objectives.

About the Department: North Carolina State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine (NC State CVM ) is a dynamic community whose members are dedicated to preparing veterinarians, veterinarian scientists, and biomedical scientists while advancing animal and human health from the cellular level through entire ecosystems. The Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences at the NC State CVM trains veterinarians, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows in research-based careers focused on discovering new information about animal and human health and disease and using those findings to enhance animal and human health and wellbeing.

Essential Job Duties: The Burclaff Lab is interested in better understanding how metabolism and cellular energetics are regulated within intestinal stem cells and how dynamic regulation underlies the intestine’s ability to maintain itself at homeostasis and following injuries or disease. Our major focus is on the stem cell compartment, studying how the intestinal stem cells maintain their identity, undergo fate decisions, regulate cell cycle, and the dynamic plasticity that occurs within crypt populations following injury. We use a mix of animal and human models, including cutting-edge genetically modified primary human intestinal stem cell cultures, to advance our understanding of the mammalian intestine. Position Overview We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented team member to support research operations, assisting with experiments, and assist with lab management. This role combines hands-on scientific research with core lab oversight in a collaborative environment. Key Responsibilities & Qualifications Research & Lab Work: Execute experiments using animal models (mouse line maintenance/tissue collection), cell lines, and primary cultures. Perform molecular biology techniques ( RNA /protein work, staining, tissue sectioning, live-image analysis). Lab Management: Oversee day-to-day operations, manage equipment and inventory, and coordinate multiple concurrent projects. Data & Documentation: Maintain accurate records, manage scientific data, and contribute to publications, grant applications, and presentations. Technical & Problem-Solving Skills: Prior research experience required. Proficient in standard lab equipment, troubleshooting, computers, and data management tools. Work Ethic & Soft Skills: Self-motivated, highly organized, and able to work independently while fostering a collaborative, supportive team environment.
Other Responsibilities: In addition to the core responsibilities of this role, there may be occasional opportunities to take on additional duties. This offers an opportunity to build on your skills, explore new areas, and gain a deeper understanding of the department’s operations.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Experience working in a research lab Experience in mammalian primary cell culture (establishment and maintenance) Experience in molecular biology and biochemistry techniques ( PCR ; RT-qPCR; gel electrophoresis, DNA , RNA , and protein extraction; immunofluorescence; immunohistochemistry) Experience in mouse colony management (animal handling, breeding, weaning, genotyping, etc) and in vivo experimentation

title: Director of Gifts and Records Management
description: The Director of Gifts & Records Management (GRM) is a key leader within Advancement Services at NC State, responsible for ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and effectiveness of the university’s gift processing and constituent data operations. This role oversees the recording and stewardship of nearly 60,000 gifts annually and the maintenance of more than 900,000 constituent records, forming the operational backbone that supports fundraising, donor engagement, and institutional decision-making. Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Advancement Services, the Director leads a high-performing team responsible for the full lifecycle of gift administration and biographical data management. The Director sets standards, establishes processes, and ensures compliance with IRS, CASE, FASB, and institutional policies while delivering accurate, timely, and service-oriented operations. The position also plays a key role in the ongoing enhancement and optimization of the university’s CRM platform, supporting the continued evolution of advancement operations following implementation. This role requires a leader who can balance precision with judgment, apply policies thoughtfully, navigate complex and nuanced situations, and partner effectively with fundraisers and campus stakeholders. The Director is expected to continuously improve and modernize operations by strategically leveraging data, technology, automation, and artificial intelligence, ensuring that Gifts & Records Management remains efficient, scalable, and responsive to the university’s evolving needs.

About the Department: North Carolina State University (NC State) was founded in 1887 with the purpose of creating economic, societal, and intellectual prosperity for the people of North Carolina. Today it is the largest university in North Carolina with more than 34,000 high-performing students, 8,000 pre-eminent faculty and staff and 300,000 alumni. NC State is known for its leadership in research, education, and service and as a research extensive university, is recognized for its strengths in science, engineering, and technology. The University consistently ranks among the top public national universities and one of the best values in higher education. University Advancement amplifies NC State’s local and global impact by nurturing lifelong relationships, championing philanthropy and strengthening the Wolfpack community. Led by Vice Chancellor Brian Sischo, UA fulfills its mission through the operations of four main units: University Development, which seeks and obtains philanthropic support; Alumni Engagement and Annual Giving, which builds and fosters relationships and a culture of philanthropy with alumni and other constituencies; University Communications and Marketing, NC State’s dedicated communications agency; and Advancement Services, which provides information management and other key support functions to all University Advancement units. Advancement Services plays a vital role in advancing NC State University’s fundraising and engagement efforts through accurate data, innovative technology and exceptional service. The department delivers the systems, tools and insights that help the university build stronger relationships with alumni, donors and friends, ensuring every gift is managed with integrity and care. Comprising the offices of Advancement Information and Technology, Gifts and Records Management, and Donor Services, the Advancement Services oversees application development, reporting and analytics, gift acceptance and processing, donor records management, gift agreements, endowment reports and naming opportunities. It also manages the university’s advancement systems and data, including Kindsight Ascend on Salesforce CRM . Advancement Services works closely with Alumni Engagement and Annual Giving, University Development, University Communications and the college and unit advancement offices to provide reliable information and forward-looking solutions that strengthen philanthropy and engagement across the university. Advancement Services also leads data and systems governance for University Advancement, promoting the ethical, consistent and secure use of information in all fundraising and engagement activities. By combining operational excellence with a culture of collaboration and innovation, Advancement Services helps NC State make data-informed decisions that drive meaningful and lasting impact.

Essential Job Duties: The Salesforce Developer is responsible for designing, building, and maintaining solutions across University Advancement’s Salesforce ecosystem centered around Kindsight’s ascend managed package. The role combines strong hands-on software development, thoughtful technical design, adherence to best practices, and stewardship of code quality. The Salesforce Developer manages the full application development lifecycle, working with cross-functional teams in the design, development, testing, and deployment of solutions. The ideal candidate brings their expertise to ensure solutions are reliable, secure, performant, and aligned with business and architectural standards. This role reports directly to the Director of Application Services within Advancements Services.
Other Responsibilities: Key responsibilities will include, but not limited to the following: Architecture and Design Assess business requirements to drive architectural decisions, balancing Salesforce out-of-the-box features, third-party AgentExchange products, and custom programmatic solutions. Translate business requirements into scalable technical designs, specifications, and data flow diagrams using Salesforce best practices. Participate in design reviews and user story scoping sessions to provide guidance on solution patterns and platform capabilities. Work closely with administrators, solution/product owners, cross-functional teams, business analysts, and other technical leads to refine requirements. Development & Customization Develop and maintain scalable solutions using Apex, Lightning Web components ( LWC ), and advanced flow orchestration. Maximize the use of low-code/no-code capabilities to build a robust framework designed for sustainable scalability. Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to analyze complex system logs, trace execution paths, and resolve platform exceptions efficiently. Proven track record of delivering hands-on Salesforce integration solutions, with deep technical proficiency in RESTful and SOAP web services. Build reusable components, utilities, and frameworks to accelerate development across the team. Monitor Apex jobs, integrations, and platform events for failures or performance issues. Stay updated with Salesforce platform releases and industry trends to recommend best practices and improvements. Release Management & DevOps Participate in structured release processes using tools such as VS Code, GitHub, and Gearset CI/CD pipelines. Data Modeling, Mapping, and Transformation Design and maintenance of custom objects, fields, relationship, and record types. Ensure the data model supports scalability, reporting needs, and integration patterns. Implement sharing rules, permission sets, and role hierarchy strategies aligned with security requirements. Evaluate the impacts of scheme changes across automation, interactions, and UI components. Testing and Quality Assurance Write comprehensive unit tests with meaningful assertions and required code coverage. Support integration testing, regression testing, and UAT cycles. Validate performance, scalability, and error handling behavior to complex flows and Apex logic. Conducts bulk data testing and governor limits analysis to ensure code performs under the high-load periods. Participate in peer code reviews and enforce coding standards. Compliance and Governance Adhere to enterprise security, data governance, data retention policies, and other compliance standards, Ensure all development follows established coding conventions and architectural guidelines. Maintain auditability through documentation, version control, and traceable deployment practices.
Minimum Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree with preference in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field/discipline. 5+ years of hands-on experience in Salesforce development and configuration. Salesforce Certified Platform Developer
Other Required Qualifications: High proficiency in Apex developments, including classes, triggers, asynchronous processing, and integration callouts. Advanced experience in building Lightning Web Components ( LWC ) with reusable, modular design patterns. Demonstrated experience designing and implementing Salesforce data models, including objects, relationships, and security controls. Experience integrating Salesforce with external systems using REST / SOAP APIs, platform events, and middleware tools within a hybrid cloud ecosystem. Experience with DevOps and source control solutions.
Preferred Qualifications: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II Familiarity with advancement/fundraising data sets, including biographic data workflows and fundraising-related transactions. Familiarity with Kindsight ascend or AdvancementRM managed package. Experience in working within a hybrid ecosystem (cloud and on-premise platforms). Experience in higher education and/or not-for-profit industry.

title: CLAWS Lithography Engineer
description: We are seeking a highly-skilled lithography engineer to join our team and contribute to the ownership for NNF’s suite of lithography capabilities. The ideal candidate will have deep, hands-on experience in all lithographic processes; including contact lithography tools, stepper/projection lithography tools, automated wafer coat/develop stations, and e-beam/laser direct-write systems. Process Research & Development Advanced Development: Lead the design and optimization of cutting-edge photolithography processes tailored for next-generation applications, specifically targeting wide-bandgap devices for RF, power electronics, and photonics. Technical Consultation: Provide expert-level process integration support to internal and external users, translating complex device requirements into repeatable lithographic workflows. Service Excellence: Execute high-precision service work for external customers, ensuring all deliverables meet rigorous industry standards for semiconductor fabrication. Equipment Engineering & Maintenance Serve as the primary technical lead for lithography toolsets, ensuring maximum uptime and process stability through regular baseline monitoring. Maintenance & Repair: Independently perform scheduled preventative maintenance and diagnose/repair unscheduled hardware failures to minimize facility downtime. Vendor Management: Manage relationships with equipment manufacturers; coordinate complex service visits, manage service contracts, and oversee major tool overhauls. User Training & Technical Communication Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs for students and researchers, certifying users on tool operation, chemical safety, and lithographic theory. Act as the central communication hub for the lithography area, providing timely updates to management and users regarding tool status, process drifts, or facility interruptions. Facility Operations & Compliance Actively participate in facility safety audits and uphold strict cleanroom protocols to ensure a safe working environment for all personnel. Maintain meticulous records including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), maintenance logs, user databases, and training certifications. Oversee the lithography supply chain, managing the inventory of specialized chemicals, resists, and critical spare parts to ensure uninterrupted lab operations.

description: In this role you will assist the Director of Recruiting with coordinating and executing the day to day player acquisition plan in the recruiting department.
