title: UTS - Temporary Recycling Collections Operator at NC State
description: Bulk Waste and Electronics Collections – scheduled route collections average of 180 sites per week for materials and electronics not accepted in the automated or recycling collection system. Related transport and sorting into appropriate materials bins at the Dearstyne Rolloff Site. Bulk material collections include items such as pallets, crates, discarded furniture, scrap metal, electronics, etc. Recycling and Reuse Collections – customer requested collections of reuse, recycling and unwanted building items and hauling to Dearstyne for recycling or disposal. This is on demand service for campus customers and response time is offered within 1-2 business days of the initial request. Common requests include delivery and pick up of carts for office clean outs, pick up and signature collections of confidential recycling, preparing and distributing materials for reuse in other areas or departments. Events and Projects – Field support to provide special waste/recycling/compost service for campus events and support major activities on campus such as residence hall move in and move out where additional services, monitoring and staff support are needed for collections. Repair, Maintenance, Safety – provide inspection and maintenance of containers related to the collection of waste and recycling on campus. Includes cleaning, proper labeling, delivery, distribution and placement of containers inside and outside of buildings. Inspection and maintenance of assigned trucks and equipment used daily to complete duties and assignments. Perform all work assignments and duties in compliance with established safe work practices. Follow safety and health regulations, policies and procedures. Identifies and resolves potential safety concerns or violations.

title: Research Administrator
description: Essential Job Duties As part of the College’s research administration team, The Research Administrator plays an important role in supporting faculty and ensuring the effective management of sponsored projects. The position provides financial and administrative support throughout the full award lifecycle, from proposal development and submission through award management, reporting, and closeout. By partnering with faculty and university stakeholders, this role helps ensure sponsored projects are managed effectively and in compliance with university, state, federal, and sponsor requirements. Proposal Development and Submission Prepare, compile, and submit grant and contract proposals for assigned faculty through NC State University systems, including RED, and sponsor electronic submission portals such as Grants.gov, Research.gov, and EERE Exchange. Collaborate with Principal Investigators (PIs) to develop proposal budgets, budget justifications, and other required documents in accordance with university and sponsor requirements. Create and maintain RED records for faculty and coordinate with campus offices to facilitate timely and accurate proposal submissions. Provide guidance and training to faculty within the assigned portfolio regarding NC State business processes and requirements for proposal development and submission. Review proposal documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable university and sponsor guidelines. Serve as a resource to faculty throughout the proposal process, identifying potential issues and coordinating resolutions with appropriate university offices. Award Management Manage an assigned portfolio of sponsored projects by monitoring financial activity, expenditures, budgets, and projections and providing Principal Investigators (PIs) with timely information to support effective project and financial decision-making. Provide financial guidance and oversight by applying accounting principles, sponsor requirements, and university policies to budgeting, forecasting, personnel expenses, cost allocations, and other fiscal activities. Partner with PIs throughout the award lifecycle by conducting regular financial reviews, discussing project spending and future plans, identifying potential issues, and recommending appropriate actions to keep projects on track. Coordinate award modifications and approvals by preparing and managing project modification requests, including rebudgeting, no-cost extensions, changes in PI, equipment purchases, travel, pre-award costs, and other actions requiring university or sponsor approval. Manage subcontracts and subawards throughout their lifecycle, including setup, monitoring, reporting, compliance, and closeout, while coordinating with PIs, university offices, and sponsoring agencies as needed. Ensure financial and regulatory compliance by monitoring sponsored project activity, reviewing personnel and financial expenditures, supporting effort certification, and addressing issues in accordance with federal, state, university, and sponsor requirements. Coordinate sponsored project closeout by resolving outstanding financial and administrative matters, completing final reconciliations, obtaining required approvals, maintaining project records, and coordinating timely submission of final reports and documentation. Grant Reporting Provide financial reports, budget analysis, and consultation to PIs to support effective fiscal management of sponsored projects. Assist PIs and project teams with sponsor-required financial and progress reporting, ensuring reports are accurate, complete, and submitted by established deadlines. Monitor and manage cost-share commitments and reporting, including maintaining appropriate supporting documentation and ensuring expenditures are accurately tracked and reported. Reconcile project financial activity and provide supporting documentation for sponsor and university reporting requirements. Respond to questions from faculty and project stakeholders regarding project financial status, reporting requirements, and allowable expenditures. Maintain accurate and complete financial records and documentation to support reporting, audits, and compliance requirements. If you are a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working with faculty, managing complex projects, and using financial expertise to support research, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Environmental Services Technician I - 40324
description: Are you looking for a fulfilling career where you can make a tangible difference in creating a clean and welcoming environment? We are seeking a passionate and detail-oriented Environmental Services Technician to join our exceptional Environmental Services team at NC State’s Facilities Division . In this vital role, you will help maintain over 10 million square feet of campus space, ensuring a safe and inviting atmosphere for students, staff, and visitors. With the support of a dynamic team of over 320 professionals, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and take pride in your work while contributing to our vibrant campus community. Join us and be a part of a team that takes pride in delivering exceptional service to one of the most prestigious campuses in the region. Apply today and help us keep NC State shining bright! Working Hours: 8:30 am - 5:00 pm, Monday – Friday Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Clean and sanitize designated areas using standard cleaning assignments to maintain a safe and hygienic environment Report any discrepancies, damages, or maintenance needs within buildings and promptly respond to emergencies and inclement weather Operate housekeeping equipment such as vacuums, mops, and scrubbers to complete tasks like dusting, disinfecting, and replenishing supplies Periodically strip and refinish floors, shampoo and extract carpets, and perform pressure washing of entrances, exterior walls, and windows Remove and manage recycling from centralized indoor recycling sites Assist with window washing and other seasonal cleaning tasks as needed Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs. Perform lifting duties up to 30 pounds frequently and 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations, and perform physical tasks such as grasping, pushing, and pulling cleaning equipment; reaching overhead; bending, squatting, climbing, and maintaining balance.

title: Student Employee Program Specialist
description: The Student Employment Program Specialist plays a key role in supporting the university's federal work-study and non-federal undergraduate student employment programs. In this position, you will help ensure students have a positive employment experience by administering student employment processes, supporting supervisors and employers, ensuring compliance with employment requirements, and enhancing programs that prepare students for future academic and career success. Key Responsibilities: Administer Student Employment Programs: Coordinate the university's federal work-study and non-federal student employment programs, ensuring compliance with applicable regulations, policies, and procedures. Support Student Employment Processes: Verify student employment eligibility, oversee employment documentation, and help ensure student employees are paid accurately and on time. Partner with Campus and Community Employers: Build and maintain collaborative relationships with on-campus departments and approved off-campus employers to support successful student employment experiences. Deliver Training and Program Support: Develop and facilitate workshops, training sessions, and guidance for student employment supervisors while serving as a resource on student employment policies and best practices. Enhance Programs Through Assessment: Monitor program effectiveness, prepare reports, analyze trends, and recommend improvements that strengthen student employment opportunities and support student professional development. If you enjoy building relationships, improving processes, and creating meaningful employment experiences that help students develop professionally while supporting the university's mission, we encourage you to apply.

title: UTS - Temporary Advancement Learning Specialist at NC State
description: This position is responsible for assisting with administration and coordination of training programs, including providing logistical support for training processes, systems, reporting, and services of the department. The position will assist with the process to onboard new employees as well as offboard employees leaving the university. Additionally, this person will serve in a help-desk role to answer questions regarding the department's systems, and assist with system access for all the department's related systems and resources, including data usage and confidentiality compliance.

title: COSS Support Specialist, Gaston County
description: The County Support Specialist is a member of the staff of the North Carolina Cooperative Extension Service (NCCES). The full-time County Support Specialist’s primary responsibility is to provide specialized office support for staff and volunteers, program marketing assistance, and some administrative support duties for Extension program areas. The position duties reflect a relatively high degree of independence and accountability. Requires fluent computer and marketing skills, excellent customer service, and basic accounting skills.

title: UTS - Temporary Front Desk Concierge at UNC
description: Serve as the primary point of contact for members and guests, delivering exceptional service through warm welcomes, personalized interactions, and proactive relationship-building. Assist with dining reservations and seating, promote club amenities, services, and events, and coordinate member communications and engagement initiatives. Manage member requests from start to finish and create memorable experiences that enhance member satisfaction and loyalty. Maintain a professional, welcoming club environment, uphold company standards and policies, respond effectively to member concerns using service recovery procedures, and remain adaptable to meet the evolving needs of members, guests, and club operations.

title: Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect
description: The Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect , provides leadership for planning and strategic investment within the Facilities Division. This position leads university-wide planning initiatives that guide the long-term development, stewardship, and strategic investment of NC State’s physical environment, aligned with the university’s mission and strategic plan and serves as or supervises the university architect. The position is responsible for the development, implementation, and ongoing stewardship of the university’s Physical Master Plan , which serves as the framework for campus growth, land use, infrastructure investment, sustainability, and design decision-making across NC State’s campuses and research properties, including the Raleigh campus precincts, Lake Wheeler Field Laboratory, and Reedy Creek Field Laboratory. Reporting to senior Facilities Division leadership, the Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect provides leadership for campus planning, infrastructure planning, facilities information systems, and sustainability initiatives. The position collaborates extensively with university leadership, the UNC System, local and regional governments, faculty, staff, students, and community stakeholders to ensure the university’s physical environment supports teaching, research, outreach, student success, and operational excellence. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Strategic Campus Planning Lead the development, implementation, and periodic updates of the university’s Physical Master Plan and Campus Development Process, including the 6-Year Capital Plan and capital budget development. Ensure campus planning and capital development initiatives align with the university’s strategic priorities, long-range vision, and design principles. Chair the Campus Design Review Panel and provide architectural leadership for campus design standards, aesthetics, development guidelines, wayfinding, and signage systems. Collaborate with Design and Construction to guide capital project planning, programming, scope development, and design review. Lead site planning, landscape planning, space programming, architectural studies, and environmental planning efforts, including the Urban Forest Management Plan and stewardship of Lake Raleigh Woods. Coordinate university engagement with municipal, regional, and community planning initiatives. Present planning recommendations and master plan updates to university leadership, the Board of Trustees, and the Buildings and Property Committee. Infrastructure Planning Lead long-range infrastructure planning, capital renewal strategies, and lifecycle management of university facilities, utilities, and major building systems. Direct the assessment, prioritization, and development of data-driven capital renewal plans, investment strategies, dashboards, and reporting tools that support institutional decision-making. Coordinate Facilities Division Capital Needs Requests and support development of biennial and long-range capital plans. Ensure infrastructure investments support institutional growth, operational reliability, risk mitigation, financial stewardship, and the strategic use of utility and asset information systems. Facilities Information Systems and Space Management Oversee campus GIS programs, mapping systems, and maintenance of the official University Campus Map. Manage building information, floor plans, room inventories, and space data systems to ensure accurate records, reporting, and strategic planning. Direct management of Facilities’ physical and digital plan room, including project documentation, as-built drawings, O&M manuals, specifications, real estate records, and hazardous materials reports. Provide analytics, reporting, and business intelligence to support space utilization, capital planning, utilities management, research administration, and university operations. Maintain building records, digital archives, and campus addressing standards. Sustainability Leadership Provide leadership for the Sustainability Office and implementation of the university’s Sustainability Strategic Plan. Advance sustainability initiatives that promote student engagement, applied learning, climate action, resource stewardship, and environmentally responsible operations. Integrate sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental stewardship into campus planning, design, construction, renovation, and operational practices. Champion partnerships and solutions that improve building performance, reduce lifecycle costs, and support institutional sustainability goals. Governance and Committee Leadership Chair the Campus Planning Subcommittee, Space Working Group, and Campus Design Review Panel. Advise and support the Campus Development Committee on capital planning, land use, design, and space allocation decisions. Support the Board of Trustees Buildings and Property Committee on matters related to the Physical Master Plan and campus development. Serve on university committees and advisory groups related to sustainability, environmental stewardship, stormwater management, GIS, public art, and urban forestry. Support the NC State Sustainability Council and serve as an ex officio member of capital project building committees.

title: Journey Utilities Plant Operator - Nightshift
description: Behind every class, laboratory, residence hall, and campus event is a team making sure NC State has the reliable utilities it needs to operate. As a Utility Plant Operator , you’ll play a critical role in keeping the university running by operating and monitoring the central utility systems that provide electricity, steam, hot water, and chilled water across campus. This is an opportunity to work with a variety of utility equipment and gain valuable experience in a central utility environment. You’ll work alongside experienced utility professionals to monitor plant operations, troubleshoot equipment, perform inspections, and help maintain safe, efficient, and reliable service. If you're dependable, safety-minded, mechanically inclined, and interested in learning how large-scale utility systems work, we want to hear from you. Please apply today! Working Hours: 12 hr shift, 3-4 days a week, 6:00 PM - 6:00 AM. Hours may adjust to meet the needs of the organization. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Assist in the control and monitoring of steam boilers, chillers, cogeneration equipment, and auxiliary systems to ensure continuous utility services. Maintain safe and efficient operations of steam, hot water, and chilled water production systems. Conduct real-time monitoring, make necessary adjustments, and ensure compliance with emissions and regulatory standards. Inspect plant equipment, including fuel gas compressors, air filters, pumps, and cooling towers. Work under the guidance of a shift supervisor to optimize plant performance and address operational challenges. Support the operation of the Cates and Centennial Cogeneration Facilities to produce electricity and steam for the campus. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform a wide range of physically demanding tasks in varied outdoor environments, ensuring safe handling practices and maintaining productivity in varying weather and terrain conditions. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Journey Utilities Plant Operator - Dayshift
description: Behind every class, laboratory, residence hall, and campus event is a team making sure NC State has the reliable utilities it needs to operate. As a Utility Plant Operator , you’ll play a critical role in keeping the university running by operating and monitoring the central utility systems that provide electricity, steam, hot water, and chilled water across campus. This is an opportunity to work with a variety of utility equipment and gain valuable experience in a central utility environment. You’ll work alongside experienced utility professionals to monitor plant operations, troubleshoot equipment, perform inspections, and help maintain safe, efficient, and reliable service. If you’re dependable, safety-minded, mechanically inclined, and interested in learning how large-scale utility systems work, we want to hear from you. Please apply today! Working Hours: 12 hr. shift, 3-4 days a week, 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM. Working hours may change to meet the needs of the University. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Assist in the control and monitoring of steam boilers, chillers, cogeneration equipment, and auxiliary systems to ensure continuous utility services. Maintain safe and efficient operations of steam, hot water, and chilled water production systems. Conduct real-time monitoring, make necessary adjustments, and ensure compliance with emissions and regulatory standards. Inspect plant equipment, including fuel gas compressors, air filters, pumps, and cooling towers. Work under the guidance of a shift supervisor to optimize plant performance and address operational challenges. Support the operation of the Cates and Centennial Cogeneration Facilities to produce electricity and steam for the campus. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform a wide range of physically demanding tasks in varied outdoor environments, ensuring safe handling practices and maintaining productivity in varying weather and terrain conditions. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Assistant Women's Tennis Coach
description: The Assistant Women’s Tennis coach will assist the Head Women’s Tennis Coach in the organization of all aspects of a Division I Women’s Tennis Program to include recruiting, player development, practices, and administration. Responsibilities will include, but will not be limited to: Assisting the head coach in administrative functions for the team. Promoting student-athlete welfare by fostering an environment that prioritizes personal growth, leadership development, mental well-being, and academic achievement. Collaborating in the design and implementation of practice plans, individual training sessions, match preparation, and competitive strategies. Identifying, evaluating, and recruiting prospective student-athletes who demonstrate the athletic, academic, and personal characteristics necessary for success at NC State University. Building and maintaining positive relationships with prospective student-athletes, families, coaches, and recruiting networks while ensuring compliance with NCAA, conference, and institutional recruiting regulations. Assisting with scheduling and management of practice facilities, match preparations, equipment, and other program resources. Supporting the administration and execution of home competitions, tournaments, camps, clinics, and special events hosted by the Women's Tennis program. Assisting the head coach in the coaching of technical and mental aspects of the game. Supporting fundraising, alumni engagement, community outreach, and promotional activities that enhance the visibility and success of the Women's Tennis program. Ensure adherence to all NCAA, ACC, and University rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.

title: Agriculture Marketing & Content Creator Internship
description: Capture,edit, prepare and upload agricultural educational content from small grains and Official Variety Trial programs to multi-media platforms. These may include NC State University web portals, social media accounts associated with the program including but not limited to facebook, X and Instagram. Content creation will be both short and long form. Short form to include images with written captions or short video clips with closed captioning. Long form will include 2 to 5 minute video content describing an agricultural concept with closed captioning. Development of written and visual program marketing materials will also be required, along with attendance at grower meetings and larger industry events to deliver those materials to stakeholders.

title: Landscape Maintenance Technician
description: Do you enjoy working outdoors and taking pride in creating beautiful, healthy landscapes? Join NC State University’s Landscape Maintenance and Operations team as a Landscape Maintenance Technician and help shape the campus environment that students, faculty, staff, and visitors experience every day. In this hands-on role, you’ll provide professional landscape care across NC State’s campus, using your knowledge of horticulture, turf management, and landscape maintenance to keep our grounds safe, attractive, and sustainable. You’ll work as part of a dedicated team that takes pride in maintaining one of the university’s most visible and important assets, its campus landscape. If you’re dependable, enjoy hands-on work, and want to see the results of your work make a difference every day, we invite you to apply and join the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform routine landscape maintenance, including mowing, edging, trimming, blowing, mulching, leaf collection, and general debris removal. Install and maintain plant materials including annuals, perennials, trees, shrubs, bulbs, and sod. Apply herbicides, pesticides, and insecticides safely and in accordance with all regulatory and product guidelines. Prune shrubs, trees, and ornamental plants to promote plant health, structure, and seasonal bloom. Monitor turf and plant health, identify pests, diseases, and soil deficiencies, and report concerns promptly. Operate and perform basic maintenance on landscape equipment such as trimmers, mowers, chainsaws, blowers, and utility vehicles. Assist with turf care through soil testing, seeding, fertilization, irrigation support, and sod installation. Collaborate with the irrigation team by monitoring system performance and assisting with repairs when needed. Maintain clean, organized, and safe worksites, vehicles, and storage areas. Respond to customer and field concerns professionally, escalating issues to Field Leads or Zone Managers when appropriate. Complete daily work logs, timesheets, and records with accuracy and attention to detail. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform physically demanding outdoor tasks safely in various weather and terrain conditions. Ability to verbally communicate effectively with supervisors and the general public and understand verbal and written instructions and other communications regarding work assignments and other matters.

title: Bezos Center Operations & Partnerships Manager
description: The Bezos Center Operations Manager will collaborate with faculty, researchers, and industry partners to ensure the smooth operation of the Center’s programs while fostering partnerships that drive innovation in sustainable protein technologies. This role supports the Center’s leadership team in implementing operational strategies, managing resources, and optimizing workflows to enhance productivity and collaboration. The Operations Manager will also support the Center’s research, workforce development, and capacity-building activities, develop and maintain relationships with partners, and facilitate technology transfer. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Strategic Planning & Operational Leadership: Devise and implement short- and long-term operational strategies and processes in collaboration with the Director. Ensure operational efficiency, compliance, and risk management. Develop and refine workflows to support program growth and sustainability. Program & Partnership Management: Implement and oversee the Center’s research, workforce development, and outreach programs. Manage partnerships and stakeholder consortia, identifying opportunities for collaboration with academic, industry, non-profit, and government partners. Support technology transfer initiatives and facilitate partnerships that advance sustainable protein innovation. Manage projects that contribute to the growth and expansion of the Center’s initiatives. Staff Leadership & Development: Manage Center staff, including hiring, onboarding, performance evaluations, and professional development. Provide guidance to staff on project execution and program priorities. Foster a collaborative work environment by supporting team development, engagement, and growth. Market Research & Strategic Recommendations: Conduct market research on emerging trends in sustainable protein technologies. Provide strategic recommendations to inform the Center’s work agenda, program development, and partnership strategy. Offer subject matter expertise when relevant to initiatives and collaborations. Reporting & Documentation: Support annual reporting requirements by collecting, organizing, and drafting information for internal and external stakeholders. Maintain documentation for operational processes, programs, and partnerships. This role offers the opportunity to shape the operations of a leading Center advancing sustainable protein technologies. If you are a highly organized, strategic, and collaborative professional with experience managing programs, partnerships, and staff in a research or innovation environment we encourage you to apply.

title: Associate Director of Autonomous Science
description: The Associate Director of Autonomous Science will contribute to advancement of the scientific and engineering vision for SPEED’s autonomous laboratories, helping transform how experiments are designed, executed, analyzed, and optimized. This is a highly collaborative leadership role at the intersection of science, robotics, artificial intelligence, and advanced laboratory automation. The Associate Director will coordinate the translation of complex scientific questions into closed-loop autonomous experiments that combine AI-driven planning, robotic experimentation, multimodal characterization, data analysis, and scientific reasoning. Working with SPEED scientists, engineers, researchers, and external users, the position will shape new capabilities, guide high-impact research programs, and ensure that autonomous experiments deliver rigorous, reproducible, and scientifically meaningful results. Primary Responsibilities: Autonomous Science and Engineering Leadership Lead design and operation of end-to-end autonomous experimentation workflows across SPEED’s robotic laboratories. Translate scientific goals into closed-loop systems spanning experimental design, robotic execution, measurement, analysis, interpretation, and AI-guided experiment selection. Define requirements for integrating synthesis, processing, characterization, optimization, and autonomous decision-making. Advance Bayesian optimization, active learning, machine learning, scientific models, genetic algorithms, and AI agents in physical laboratory systems. Establish standards for controls, validation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility, metadata, and experimental provenance. Evaluate AI-generated recommendations for scientific validity, feasibility, safety, and alignment with research objectives. Drive improvements in SPEED’s reliability, throughput, autonomy, and scientific capabilities. Scientific Program and User Engagement Serve as scientific leader and primary point of contact for researchers using SPEED’s autonomous experimentation capabilities. Translate user questions into defined experimental objectives, strategies, and success criteria. Assess project feasibility and develop experimental plans, autonomous campaigns, analysis strategies, and validation approaches. Partner with researchers and engineers to execute projects, interpret results, and resolve scientific and technical challenges. Lead reviews of experimental results, AI recommendations, uncertainty, emerging hypotheses, and next steps. Develop sustained research partnerships with academic, government, national laboratory, and industry organizations. Expansion of SPEED Scientific Capabilities Lead development and integration of new autonomous laboratory capabilities, methods, and application areas. Identify opportunities to expand SPEED across chemistry, materials science, catalysis, molecular discovery, formulation, process development, and related fields. Define requirements for robotic platforms, analytical systems, sensors, AI tools, and integrated workflows. Guide new capabilities from concept and prototyping through commissioning, validation, and deployment. Establish benchmarks to evaluate performance, reproducibility, and transferability. Evaluate emerging technologies in laboratory robotics, scientific AI, multimodal characterization, digital twins, agentic systems, and autonomous decision-making. Develop strategies to transfer methods, models, and experimental knowledge across SPEED platforms and partner laboratories. Contribute to strategic planning, equipment investments, partnerships, proposals, publications, and initiatives advancing SPEED’s scientific mission. Research Team Leadership and Technical Coordination Provide scientific direction and mentorship to researchers, platform scientists, and engineering personnel. Coordinate multidisciplinary teams spanning science, robotics, automation, software, data, AI, and facility operations. Set project priorities, milestones, deliverables, and performance expectations. Review experimental plans, autonomous workflows, technical documentation, data products, and scientific conclusions. Lead technical discussions to resolve integration challenges and align scientific and engineering efforts. Establish consistent scientific, software, data, and documentation practices across SPEED platforms. Develop training, workshops, and technical demonstrations for researchers, users, and partners. Represent SPEED at scientific meetings, sponsor reviews, user workshops, advisory activities, and external collaborations.

title: Student Success Navigators for Elevate (IPSE)
description: Note: This position is open only to currently enrolled NC State students who are in good academic standing. Primary purpose of this position: NC State’s inclusive postsecondary education program for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities, Elevate is seeking a motivated and reliable Student Success Navigator to support in study halls, courses to promote self-determined learning among Elevate students. This role provides the opportunity to support students individually and in small groups in developing skills such as time management, navigation, and assignment completion. Job Responsibilities: Provide 5 to 15 hours per week of support, including academic and social mentoring responsibilities Provide individualized academic support in study sessions and Elevate program or inclusive Courses Provide individualized support during Elevate’s Living Learning class or workshops Assist students with navigation, assignment planning, and time management, including use of Google Suite tools and other mobile applications Support Elevate students with independent living, social goal, and academic goal attainment including attending events/ activities and facilitating event/ activity registration Document activities completed with Elevate students, as instructed by Elevate staff Participate in trainings led by Social or Academic Peer Coaches or Elevate program staff Clearly communicate availability and provide adequate notice if scheduling conflicts arise Opportunities to serve as a job coach for on campus student employment internship(s) Eligibility Requirements: Must be an undergraduate or graduate student currently enrolled at NC State University Strong academic, organizational, and interpersonal skills Must have a passion for inclusion Proficiency with Google Suite tools and digital scheduling and communication mechanisms used by the Elevate program

title: Temporary Research Technician
description:
Posting Number: PG196158TM
Position Number: 11ASO3746
Position Type: Temporary
Essential Job Duties: Duties include: Processing large numbers of arthropod samples under the stereoscope. Identifying and recording numbers of major insect and mite pests of small fruit crops. Labeling and organizing arthropod samples. Assisting with greenhouse and field collection of arthropod samples. Experience using a stereoscope is preferred. Experience with arthropod identification is preferred but is not required; training can be provided. Assisting with fieldwork involving the excavation and uprooting of blueberry plants from research plots approximately 2–3 times per month, primarily under outdoor field conditions and direct sunlight. Performing physically demanding field work that requires prolonged standing, bending, kneeling, digging, and working in variable weather conditions. Safely operating heavy-duty hand tools and field equipment, including shovels, hammers, axes, pruning shears, heavy-duty scissors, sharpened cutting tools, and chainsaws, while following all laboratory and field safety procedures. Opening and processing plant root masses in the laboratory to extract, collect, and document beetle larvae using hand tools and following established laboratory protocols. Schedule: 35-40 hours per week, 8 am-5 pm with 1 hour lunch break. Fieldworkdays may be longer 10-11-hour days (1-3 days per week, 1-2 times per month).
Is Time Limited: No

title: CaSA Temporary Administrative Support Associate
description: The Administrative Associate provides office support, under supervision, to the Climate and Sustainability Academy faculty and staff, focused on essential operational, logistical, and clerical support to the Academy team. The candidate will ensure compliance with university policies and procedures while providing exceptional customer service.

title: Business Officer
description: The Business Officer will perform a variety of administrative, fiscal, HR, and operational functions for OIT and Business Services, providing support to serve nearly 300 employees within OIT. This position will report directly to the Director of Business Services, in coordination with the Manager of Human Resources, and serve as the point of contact for other operational needs within Business Services and OIT. As the Business Officer, your work will have a direct impact on the department's success by supporting efficient operations and delivering exceptional service to campus partners. You'll work alongside a collaborative team in an environment that encourages professional growth and fosters a rewarding workplace experience. Key responsibilities will fall within the functional areas outlined below: Financial Management: Initiate and process a variety of financial transactions, including purchase requisitions, purchase orders, voucher payments, reimbursements, interdepartmental transactions, Marketplace orders, and related fiscal activities. Support the financial management of OIT budgets by monitoring expenditures, processing budget adjustments, reconciling financial transactions, and ensuring compliance with university policies and accounting guidelines. Appropriates spending and the allocation of funds by processing budget journals and other financial actions during the university’s fiscal year end closeout period Serves as the point of contact with college departments that partner with OIT on technology projects that are grant-funded, to manage pre- and post-award processes (budget preparation, no-cost extensions, reporting, budget closeout) Process and reconcile procurement card transactions, travel authorizations and reimbursements, insurance payments, and other assigned financial activities. Human Resources: Initiate and process employment actions for student, temporary, and other designated employee groups, including personnel transactions and employment changes. Maintain personnel records and organizational information by managing electronic personnel files, updating organizational charts, and supporting the accuracy of HR documentation. Partner with the OIT Human Resources team to support recruitment activities, ensure compliance with university policies, and assist with HR projects and operational initiatives. Business Services Operations: Coordinate business services operations by serving as the primary contact for building access, key management, office equipment, surplus property, permits, and office supply procurement. Support departmental operations by coordinating meeting and event logistics, assisting with asset management activities, and providing administrative support for Business Services initiatives. If you're a detail-oriented professional who enjoys balancing financial management, human resources, and business operations while building strong partnerships across campus, we invite you to apply and become an integral member of our Business Services team.

title: Budget Specialist & Accounts Receivable Accountant
description: The Budget and Accounting position provides financial and budgetary support to departments within the College of Veterinary Medicine. Reporting to the Assistant Dean of Finance and Business, this role is an important part of the business office team and supports a range of accounting, budgeting, reporting, and auditing activities that help ensure the effective management of university resources. In this role, you will work with a variety of funding sources, including state, federal, F&A, receipts, trusts, contracts and grants, gifts, and foundation funds. You will process journal entries, prepare financial reports, review revenue, expenses, and payroll transactions, and develop ad hoc reports to support financial analysis and decision-making. This position offers the opportunity to expand your knowledge across multiple areas of university financial operations while applying your skills in financial analysis, reporting, reconciliation, and compliance. Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, sound financial judgment, and the ability to interpret and apply university, college, state, federal, and UNC System policies and procedures. Key Responsibilities Payroll & Position Control Management Monitor and process monthly and biweekly salary redistributions for the College of Veterinary Medicine, including temporary, graduate, and employee appointments. Review complex salary distribution worksheets and analyze funding changes across multiple sources while ensuring accuracy and compliance with fiscal and federal deadlines. Partner with the CVM Grants Office and Departmental Accountants to process release time, 90-day retroactive requests, and other salary-related transactions. Monitor labor encumbrances and projected salary commitments to identify and address potential funding deficits. Provide guidance on funding strategies for new hires, reappointments, salary changes, and legislative increases. Apply university finance and HR systems, policies, and funding requirements to process transactions and advise departments. Manage payroll workflows in alignment with university calendars and support year-end processing, including back-to-base transactions, fiscal year cleanup, payroll suspense accounts, and leave payouts. Ensure salary actions comply with sponsor guidelines, Uniform Guidance, and institutional effort reporting requirements. Budget Analysis & Financial Planning Conduct budget analysis across state appropriations, F&A receipts, trust funds, contracts and grants, gifts, and foundation funds. Monitor fund balances and financial trends to identify potential deficits, surpluses, and areas requiring attention. Prepare budget projections and forecasts to support financial planning and decision-making. Assist with course and teaching budgets and support departments in developing spending plans. Analyze historical spending patterns and provide recommendations to support effective fiscal management. Complete quarterly budget-to-actual reconciliations and provide variance analysis to leadership. Support fiscal year-end closeout activities and develop financial dashboards and reporting tools to support data-driven decisions. Accounts Receivable Complete monthly, quarterly, and annual billing activities using the university's Express Billing system. Monitor outstanding receivables and aging reports and follow up on past-due accounts to support timely collection. Record and reconcile incoming payments, ensuring accurate posting to appropriate fund sources and project phases. Collaborate with the University Controller's Office on delinquent accounts and applicable write-off procedures. Maintain documentation supporting receivable balances and compliance with university policies. Assist Accounts Payable with reimbursement and payment requests. Departmental Support & Compliance Ensure financial activities comply with State spending guidelines, Uniform Guidance, Contracts and Grants requirements, and foundation policies. Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and desk manuals to support consistent financial practices. Provide training and proactive financial guidance to CVM units. Maintain collaborative relationships with CVM units and central university offices to support effective financial operations. If you are a detail-oriented financial professional who enjoys analyzing financial information, solving problems, and supporting effective financial operations, we encourage you to apply. This is an opportunity to bring your financial expertise to a collaborative business office environment while supporting the College of Veterinary Medicine's financial goals.

title: Pastry Sous Chef
description: NC State Dining is seeking a passionate Pastry Sous Chef to join our team! The Pastry Sous Chef position will provide day-to-day oversight of the baking production staff for NC State Dining. This position works closely with the Executive Pastry Chef to provide a high-quality baking department. This position will be responsible for maintaining the highest culinary standards and works directly with the bakery staff to provide training, supervision, quality control, and excellent customer service. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Operational Compliance — Train staff on NC State Dining guidelines, procedures, food safety, and sanitation standards. title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
department: 134001 - Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research
description: About the NC State College of Education As one of the nation’s top-ranked colleges of education, NC State’s College of Education leads the way in North Carolina in preparing extraordinary educators, conducting transformational research, and engaging communities where they are to improve the educational outcomes of all learners and advance the greater good. The college’s faculty are widely-recognized thought leaders who use their research to transform the practice of teaching, learning, and leading. They have particular strengths in improving technology-enhanced learning and teaching; fostering community-based learning and PK-16 partnerships; and innovating leadership and workforce development, educational policy, and evaluation. About two-thirds of the faculty are grant active. They are engaged in over 225 active projects totaling $151 million, making them the most productive in terms of research activity compared with other colleges of education in North Carolina and among the Top 5% in the nation. In FY24, the college’s research expenditures exceeded $20 million. The college has over 1,600 students studying across five graduate certificates, seven undergraduate majors, two undergraduate minors, 13 master’s degrees, three Ph.D., and two Ed.D. programs housed in three academic departments: Educational Leadership, Policy, and Human Development; Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Education; and Teacher Education and Learning Sciences, with approximately 130 tenure-track and professional-track faculty, 110 support and professional staff, and about 160 graduate and teaching assistants. The College of Education is also home to the Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research, the Friday Institute for Educational Innovation, and Elevate, NC State’s inclusive postsecondary education program for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The college has over 18,000 living alumni, with over 6,000 working in public schools in every county in North Carolina. Those who are teachers rate among the highest in effectiveness on surveys of school employers in North Carolina. NC State promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interest and experience would enable them to support the university. About the Belk Center: The Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research develops and sustains exceptional community college leaders who are committed to advancing college access and student success, the social and economic mobility of their colleges’ students, and the economic competitiveness of their regions. The center provides professional development and research related to current and emerging student success opportunities and challenges facing community college leaders and policymakers in North Carolina and the nation. Primary Purpose of Position The Senior Research Associate (Postdoctoral Scholar) serves as a researcher supporting applied research initiatives within the Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research. This position designs, implements, and evaluates mixed-methods research projects focused on improving outcomes for adult learners, student parents, and community colleges. The position is responsible for leading quantitative and qualitative research activities, producing evidence-based recommendations, disseminating research findings through publications and presentations, and supporting statewide leadership development and institutional improvement efforts. The Senior Research Associate will also mentor graduate student researchers and collaborate with community college leaders, policymakers, and other stakeholders to advance the Belk Center's mission of improving student success through applied research. Primary Duties and Responsibilities: Research Design, Implementation, and Analysis (40%) Lead the design, implementation, and analysis of mixed-methods research studies. Design, administer, and analyze large-scale statewide surveys, including the Student Parent Survey. Conduct quantitative modeling, policy analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and other statistical evaluations to assess program effectiveness and student outcomes. Develop research methodologies and evaluation plans that produce rigorous, actionable findings. Ensure research quality through reproducible analytical methods and sound data management practices. Data Collection, Reporting, and Dissemination (25%) Conduct quantitative analyses using statistical software such as Stata, SPSS, R, or Python. Support qualitative research through the design, facilitation, coding, and analysis of interviews and focus groups using software such as NVivo or Dedoose. Integrate qualitative and quantitative findings into comprehensive reports and recommendations. Prepare executive summaries, technical reports, scholarly manuscripts, practice briefs, guidebooks, and other research products. Present research findings to institutional leaders, policymakers, statewide partners, and professional organizations at local, state, regional, and national conferences. Stakeholder Engagement and Program Support (20%) Facilitate the Student Parent Advisory Council. Support curriculum development for statewide communities of practice by contributing research findings, metrics, and evidence-based recommendations. Collaborate with community colleges, tribal colleges, state agencies, and external partners to support project implementation and continuous improvement. Engage with stakeholders to support study design, data collection, interpretation of findings, and dissemination of results. Professional Scholarship and Mentorship (15%) Mentor and advise graduate student researchers and research assistants engaged in Belk Center projects. Publish and co-author peer-reviewed manuscripts and other scholarly publications. Present research at regional and national conferences. Participate in professional development and contribute to advancing the Belk Center's research agenda.

The position supports externally funded research and Extension programming by coordinating field trials, evaluating research data, maintaining research operations, and contributing to the communication and dissemination of findings. Collect, validate, organize, and interpret research data; perform preliminary statistical analyses and recommend modifications to improve research quality and methodology. Serve as the primary field coordinator for multiple concurrent research projects, ensuring timely implementation of experiments and resolving novel research challenges. title: Biotechnology Program Coordinator
description: In this role, you will play a central role in advancing the Biotechnology (BIT) Program and supporting the students, faculty, and partners who make it successful. You will serve as the program expert and a trusted advisor to students, helping them navigate their academic programs, connect with opportunities, and achieve their educational and professional goals. You will work closely with BIT leadership, faculty, university offices, students, and external sponsors to coordinate courses, monitor student progress, lead communications and events, and support program reporting. You will also lead data analysis and reporting for externally funded training programs, including NSF REU and NIH T32 grants, helping demonstrate program impact and support continuous improvement. This position offers an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful program activities, build relationships across the university and beyond, and directly shape the student experience and continued growth of a dynamic biotechnology education and training program. This role focuses specifically on BIT program operations and does not oversee ISI-wide education or partnership initiatives. Key Responsibilities: Academic Program Leadership Advise BIT undergraduate and graduate students on degree requirements, course planning, enrollment, and academic progression. Coordinate courses, instructors, classrooms, catalog updates, and graduate program activities. Maintain accurate student records and monitor enrollment, progression, and completion. Data, Reporting & Program Operations Manage program records, databases, calendars, and operational resources. Lead data analysis, longitudinal tracking, and sponsor reporting for BIT programs, including NSF REU and NIH T32 Monitor program and budget information and provide leadership with insights to support planning and decision-making. Communications, Outreach & Events Lead BIT communications, website content, marketing, and outreach to showcase program opportunities. Coordinate seminars, workshops, recruitment activities, visitors, and other program events. Manage announcements, calendars, and communication channels to keep students and stakeholders informed and engaged. Program Coordination & Support Serve as a primary resource for BIT students, faculty, staff, and partners, helping them navigate program processes and university systems. Coordinate meetings, schedules, presentations, reports, and other activities that support effective program operations. Take ownership of day-to-day program needs, solve problems, and help advance the BIT program's goals and student experience. This is a visible, multifaceted position that combines student advising, academic program management, data and reporting, communications, and event coordination . The role is well suited to a proactive, organized professional who enjoys managing varied responsibilities, solving problems independently, and serving as a trusted resource to students, faculty, leadership, and university partners. Success in this role requires strong communication and organizational skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high level of service and accuracy.

title: Sponsored Research Administrator
description: The College of Engineering is looking to hire multiple Sponsored Research Administrators (SRA) within the newly established college-managed operating model, responsible for orchestrating both pre-award and post-award lifecycles for an assigned departmental faculty portfolio. While the incumbent is physically co-located within a department to provide high-touch, localized customer service, the position is an integral part of the centralized College ORA team. The primary purpose of this role is to apply advanced accounting principles, federal/state regulations, and university guidelines to ensure the fiscal and administrative integrity of all sponsored projects. Operating under this modernized model, the incumbent must balance localized portfolio execution with central compliance directives, actively participating in college-wide resource-sharing and standardized service-level agreements (SLAs). Detailed Description of Core Responsibilities Pre-Award Portfolio Management & Proposal Development Localized Faculty Consultation: Partner directly with PIs in the embedded unit to develop accurate, compliant proposal budgets and detailed justifications from initial concept through final submission. Standardized Regulatory Screening: Analyze complex agency Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs) to ensure strict alignment with F&A rules, cost-sharing restrictions, budget caps, and direct cost allowability, reducing front-end submission errors. Institutional System Management: Fully execute and route records within institutional software suites, including RED Proposal Development, ensuring data integrity is validated at the departmental level before final central routing. Electronic Research Administration (eRA): Build, format, and package proposal submissions within varied sponsor portals (Research.gov, GRANTS.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST), acting as the localized technical expert for the department's faculty. Post-Award Financial Management, Forecasting & Closeout Award Onboarding & Budget Translation: Review select incoming award notices alongside the PI to establish accurate internal ledger setups, ensuring F&A is calculated correctly based on MTDC or TDC parameters. Compliance Monitoring & Risk Mitigation: Perform continuous financial analysis of active grant ledgers. Monitor expenditures for accuracy, allowability, and strict compliance with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), Uniform Guidance, state rules, and university policies. Projections & Planning Models: Build multi-year spending projections and variance analysis models for faculty to optimize fund utilization, prevent over-expenditures, and manage labor distributions/personnel charges. Reconciliations & Cost-Share Tracking: Audit human resource expenditures, travel vouchers, and procurement charges against grant terms. Track, document, and report mandatory or voluntary committed cost-sharing obligations. Lifecycle Closeouts: Execute comprehensive closeouts for expiring grant segments. Prepare and process Project Modification Requests (PMRs) for budget modifications, no-cost extensions, or residual balance distributions, ensuring audit-ready documentation is permanently archived. Model Alignment, Cross-Coverage & Leadership Matrixed Team Collaboration: Actively participate in the broader College ORA network to ensure alignment with university-wide research administration standards. Navigate the dual priorities of central College compliance policy and local departmental workflow. Cross-College Workload Balancing: Participate in the new model's agile resource framework, willingly stepping in to provide temporary pre- or post-award coverage for other COE departments during peak submission cycles or staff absences to maintain college-wide continuity. Faculty Onboarding & Training: Develop and deliver targeted resources, onboarding guides, or info-sessions for new faculty and departmental business officers regarding centralized ORA standard operating procedures and financial management tools.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration (AVC-RA) serves as the university's senior executive leader for sponsored programs and institutional research administration, providing strategic oversight of enterprise-wide pre-award services, sponsored project administration, research contracts, research administration systems, and research administration data governance. Reporting directly to the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation, the AVC leads a high-performing leadership team that includes the Director of Institutional Research Systems & Reporting, the Director of Research Administration & Campus Liaison, and additional OSP directors. Working collaboratively with university leadership, colleges, research centers, faculty, federal sponsors, and administrative partners, the AVC ensures a coordinated, compliant, and service-oriented research administration enterprise that advances NC State's research mission while strengthening institutional stewardship and operational excellence. As the AVC RA, you will shape the future of research administration at one of the nation's leading public research universities. Your leadership will influence how investigators secure external funding, how research operations evolve to meet an increasingly complex regulatory environment, and how institutional systems, data, and policies support innovation at scale. Success in this position comes from balancing strategic vision with collaborative leadership—building trusted partnerships across the university, championing continuous improvement, and fostering an environment where faculty and research administrators have the resources, guidance, and infrastructure needed to expand NC State's research impact. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership & Research Administration: Provide strategic leadership for the university's sponsored programs enterprise, aligning research administration priorities with institutional goals and the evolving external funding landscape. Advise the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation and university leadership on research administration strategy, sponsored programs, regulatory compliance, institutional risk, and operational effectiveness. Lead the development and implementation of university-wide policies, governance, and business practices that strengthen research administration and support faculty success. Foster a culture of collaboration, service excellence, continuous improvement, and accountability across the Office of Sponsored Programs and the broader research community. Enterprise Oversight & Risk Management: Provide executive oversight of institutional pre-award operations, research agreements, and sponsored programs administration to ensure consistent, compliant, and customer-focused service delivery. Safeguard the university's legal, financial, and operational interests through effective risk management, contract oversight, and compliance with federal, state, and sponsor requirements. Lead the university's response to significant regulatory changes, audits, investigations, and other matters impacting the research enterprise. Research Systems, Data & Operational Excellence: Provide executive sponsorship for research administration systems, institutional data governance, and modernization initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness and decision-making. Champion technology, process improvement, and analytics strategies that strengthen research administration services and support institutional growth. Ensure research administration infrastructure evolves to meet the changing needs of faculty, sponsors, and the university. University & External Engagement: Build trusted partnerships with university leadership, faculty, colleges, and research administrators to advance the institution's research mission. Represent NC State in relationships with federal agencies, industry, nonprofit organizations, and national research administration associations. Serve as the university's senior institutional representative for complex sponsor negotiations, strategic collaborations, and matters requiring executive-level consultation. If you are a collaborative and strategic leader who is passionate about advancing research, building strong institutional partnerships, and shaping the future of research administration, we encourage you to apply.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Commercialization
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Commercialization (AVC‑RC) provides executive leadership for NC State’s commercialization enterprise, spanning intellectual property management, licensing, startup formation, venture development, and investment programs. The AVC sets university‑wide commercialization strategy, ensures compliance with federal and institutional requirements, and leads programs that accelerate the translation of research into societal and economic impact. As the AVC-RC, you will have the opportunity to expand NC State’s innovation ecosystem by connecting researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, and industry partners to accelerate the journey from discovery to impact. You will lead initiatives such as the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and the NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub, while representing NC State within regional and national innovation communities. Through your vision, partnership-building, and strategic leadership, you will help position NC State’s research enterprise for greater economic and societal impact while advancing a culture of innovation across the university. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership for Research Commercialization: Establishes and advances NC State’s research commercialization strategy, aligning innovation priorities with institutional research goals, economic development initiatives, and national R1 expectations. Sets enterprise-level priorities, performance measures, and service standards that strengthen commercialization outcomes across the university. Advises the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation on commercialization policy, innovation strategy, and external engagement. Intellectual Property, Licensing & Commercialization Governance: Provides executive oversight for intellectual property strategy, ensuring effective management, protection, and commercialization of university-developed innovations. Establishes policies, frameworks, and practices that support licensing, agreements, compliance, and responsible stewardship of intellectual assets. Provides university-wide leadership and guidance on intellectual property and commercialization matters. Venture Development & Innovation Funding: Leads NC State’s venture development ecosystem, expanding pathways for research discoveries to advance through startup formation, market validation, and investment opportunities. Provides strategic oversight for the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub activities. Cultivates relationships with investors, entrepreneurs, accelerators, and industry partners to strengthen commercialization opportunities. Innovation Ecosystem & Executive Leadership: Builds strategic partnerships with industry, investors, and innovation organizations to expand research impact and strengthen NC State’s role within regional and national innovation ecosystems. Provides leadership for a multidisciplinary commercialization team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Ensures effective governance, operational excellence, and high-quality services that advance the university’s commercialization mission. This is an opportunity for an accomplished commercialization leader to shape strategy, influence innovation at scale, and build connections that move groundbreaking research from discovery to impact. If you are ready to lead with vision and purpose, we invite you to apply.

title: Program Associate for Doctoral Programs
description: The University Program Associate manages the comprehensive student lifecycle for the Doctoral Programs (PhD and DDes) in the College of Design, providing expert administrative support from recruitment through graduation. Serving as the primary liaison between the Graduate School and program, this role oversees admissions compliance, degree milestone tracking, and GSSP contract administration. By coordinating fiscal operations, instructional scheduling, and marquee program events, the Coordinator ensures seamless operational success and policy alignment for both graduate and doctoral students and the college community. Student & Faculty Services Advise doctoral students (DDes and Ph.D.) on course planning, registration, and program requirements. Oversee program communications, including listserv management and timely updates on enrollment, tuition, events and key deadlines. Track student progress and milestones; coordinate with Director of Graduate Programs (DGPs) and the Graduate School; monitor exams, electronic theses and dissertations (ETD) deadlines, and degree audits to ensure compliance. Manage the (student/applicant) application lifecycle, including international requirements (English proficiency), faculty reviews, and enrollment monitoring. Program & Event Coordination Plan, schedule, and execute major graduate and doctoral program events, including Immersion Week, Symposium, defenses, forums, and professional development activities. Manage all logistics to ensure seamless event delivery. Coordinate and manage workshop logistics, guest speakers, and provide virtual event technical support. Oversee communications, registration, and logisitics for co-sponsored lectures and student-focused events. Administration & Technology Maintain accurate, up-to-date records for all active students and faculty. Collaborate with the Finance team and Scheduling Officer on course scheduling, instructional planning, and related administrative tasks. Maintain and update program websites, internal resources (Moodle), and handbooks, and stay current with university tech platforms (Google Drive, Panopto, WolfWare). Provide administrative support for faculty meetings, including scheduling, documenting, and distributing minutes, and maintaining faculty documentation. Budget, Finance & HR Support budget tracking, purchasing, and assist with HR tasks as needed. Reconcile PCards, oversee vendor payments, contracts, and honoraria, and manage purchasing for supplies and student association activities. Administer fellowships, travel awards, and honoraria, ensuring timely processing and compliance with program policies. Assist leadership on assistantship appointments, faculty buyouts and hiring processes, coordinate doctoral contracts with HR and Budget Office, and verify student eligibility for assistantships (TA/RA). Collaborate with the Budget Office and Department Head's suite to manage financial processes, budget tracking, and reporting. Assessment & Reporting Collect and manage program data (student milestones, publications, events). Support university reporting and develop assessment visuals; analyze and report on admissions, retention, and graduation data; communicate policy updates to the college.

description:

About the Department: The Department of Animal Science is the largest academic program in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and provides academic instruction to over 800 undergraduate students and 80 graduate students. The Department also is a leader in extension and engagement programs to farmers, allied industry and the public, and conducts internationally recognized research into the nutrition, genetic reproductive, health and well-being of domesticated animals.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. Essential Job Duties: Support innovative research in reproductive physiology and molecular biology by providing technical expertise and laboratory support for multiple research programs. As a Research Technician, you will play an essential role in maintaining transgenic mouse colonies, conducting molecular biology experiments, and supporting faculty, students, and scientists in advancing high-quality research. This position contributes to the success of the laboratory by ensuring research activities are conducted safely, accurately, and in compliance with institutional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Research & Laboratory Support Perform laboratory experiments and molecular biology procedures, including genotyping assays, to support ongoing research in reproductive physiology and molecular biology. Conduct animal-related procedures, including tail sampling and ear tagging, in accordance with established research protocols. Animal Colony Management Manage the transgenic mouse colony by coordinating breeding, weaning, tissue collection, colony maintenance, and accurate recordkeeping of pedigrees and colony health. Ensure compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements governing the care and use of research animals. Laboratory Operations & Collaboration Collaborate with faculty, graduate students, scientists, and research staff to support multiple research projects and laboratory initiatives. Maintain laboratory organization by managing research supply inventories, supporting laboratory cleanliness, and implementing laboratory safety procedures, including the proper handling and disposal of hazardous, non-hazardous, and radioactive waste in accordance with Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) protocols. If you are a detail-oriented research professional who enjoys working in a collaborative laboratory environment and is eager to contribute to innovative scientific research, we encourage you to apply. If you thrive in a hands-on setting, are committed to laboratory safety and quality, and enjoy learning new techniques while supporting a varied research team, we’d love to have you join us. This is a time-limited position with an expected duration of up to 3 years, depending on funding availability
Other Responsibilities: Other duties as assigned.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Experience working with research animals, preferably mice, in compliance with institutional animal care and use guidelines. Experience managing or maintaining transgenic mouse colonies, including breeding, weaning, genotyping, pedigree tracking, and colony health records. Experience performing molecular biology and cell culture techniques in a research laboratory setting. Experience maintaining laboratory operations, including inventory management, laboratory safety practices, and the handling and disposal of hazardous, non-hazardous, and radioactive waste in accordance with Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) protocols.

description:

Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8 am - 5 pm
Job Location: Raleigh, NC
Department: Horticultural Science
About the Department: Since 1901, the faculty, staff and students of the Department of Horticultural Science have been providing innovative teaching, research and outreach to the citizens of North Carolina, the nation, and the world. Our research and extension programs are recognized worldwide for their contributions to applied horticultural production and to discovery science. We generate and extend knowledge about fruits, vegetables, ornamental plants, and landscape design for the purpose of increasing food security and food safety, sustaining the environment, enhancing economic vitality, and improving the quality of life for individuals and their communities.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being.
