Essential Job Duties: The Department of Horticultural Science is seeking a motivated and experienced professional to support the day-to-day operations of the Horticulture Field Lab ( HFL ), a large-scale outdoor and greenhouse research complex serving faculty, students, researchers, and industry partners across multiple departments. The HFL supports a wide range of field and greenhouse research, teaching, extension, and industry testing activities and is home to the JC Raulston Arboretum. The position provides operational and research support for the HFL and assists with operations at the Fox and HFL Greenhouses. The position works closely with the HFL /Fox Greenhouse Coordinator and HFL Research Operations Coordinator to maintain safe, efficient, and functional research and teaching environments. Responsibilities include coordinating facility maintenance and repairs, managing work requests and equipment resources, supporting irrigation and water systems, maintaining operational and inventory records, assisting with field and greenhouse activities, and coordinating resources to meet the needs of approximately 22–25 active research projects and Principal Investigators. The position serves as a key operational resource for faculty, staff, students, and other facility users and assists with the planning and allocation of facility space, equipment, and other resources. Additional responsibilities include supporting safety and compliance activities, guiding temporary personnel in facility operations, assisting with teaching and extension events, and monitoring facility operations during weekends or other periods when designated coordinators are unavailable. The successful candidate will be expected to independently prioritize competing requests, troubleshoot operational challenges, coordinate resources, and effectively communicate with a varied group of facility users and stakeholders.
Other Responsibilities: Supervise HFL interns and bi-weekly employees. Operate skid-steer loader, Dingo, Ditch-witch, tractor, row mulcher. Teach students how to use machinery and conduct various landscape contracting activities. Install research project plots, apply herbicides, insecticides, fertilizers, and other necessary maintenance chemicals. Repair buildings, greenhouses, polyhouses, irrigation lines, and nursery pads. Repair electrical problems, apply poly to houses. Manufacture and deliver mulch as part of campus closed loop initiative (2500 yards). Assist JCRA with various education projects and construction activities. Host field days.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Plumbing, small equipment use, and mechanical aptitude are not required, but helpful skills for this position.

title: Donor Services Specialist
description: The Donor Services Specialist ensures that all gift agreements and related processes, many of which are legally binding, are developed and managed in compliance with university, foundation, federal, and state policies and practices. Donor Services seeks a candidate who thrives in a fast-paced, innovative team environment. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional writing skills, strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, and the capacity to manage multiple detail-oriented responsibilities simultaneously while collaborating closely with frontline fundraising staff. This position reports to the Associate Director of Donor Services.

title: Employer Relations Coordinator
description: The Employer Relations Coordinator is an external-facing position responsible for advancing employer engagement initiatives, building strategic partnerships, and connecting students and alumni with career opportunities across corporate, nonprofit, and public sector organizations. This includes a broad spectrum of opportunities, including full-time employment, cooperative education placements, and internships for current NC State students and alumni. Reporting to the Director of Employer Relations, the Coordinator plays a pivotal role in fostering connections between employers and the university community, enhancing talent pipelines, and supporting student career success. Duties include: Employer Engagement Develop and maintain relationships with employers through varied channels, including site visits, telephone interactions, and electronic communications. Promote NC State University and the Career Development Center resources to prospective and existing employers. Establish and maintain relationships with employers to support student and alumni recruitment. Provide consultation on recruiting strategies and engagement opportunities at NC State. Facilitate employer campus visits and engagement opportunities. Coordinate and manage mock interview programs for employer and campus partners. Customer Service and Operations Review and approve employer registrations, employer contacts, and job postings within the career management system to ensure compliance with Career Development Center policies and quality standards. Provide customer service and technical support to employers using ePACK and other recruiting systems. Coordinate employer information sessions, on-campus interviews, and recruiting activities. Coordinate and expand experiential learning opportunities with employers for Career Development Center programs. Maintain employer-facing website content. Monitor compliance with recruiting policies and procedures. Manage employer communications and campus recruiting logistics. Event Management and Support Coordinate logistics for career fairs, employer events, externships, and related programs. Represent the Career Development Center at internal and external events. Support marketing, communications, and social media efforts related to employer engagement events. Administrative and Strategic Initiatives Establish and implement campus recruiting policies. Collaborate with campus partners, employer partners, and external stakeholders to advance Career Development Center initiatives. Assist with employer outreach, partnership development, and experiential learning opportunities, including cooperative education and internship programs. Maintain accurate records, reports, and employer engagement data to support strategic decision-making and assessment efforts. Perform other Career Development Center duties as assigned.

title: Student Success Librarian
description: The Student Success Librarian supports the Libraries' mission to empower students for a lifetime of success and impact. As a member of the Teaching, Learning, and Outreach team within LSS, the position works collaboratively with library colleagues and campus partners to develop and deliver outreach, programming, and instruction that connect undergraduate students with the Libraries' people, services, spaces, and expertise. Through these efforts, the position helps students develop the information and digital literacies, critical thinking skills, confidence, and sense of belonging needed to succeed academically and thrive as members of the NC State community. Student Success and Engagement The Student Success Librarian leads the Libraries' engagement with university programs and events that recruit, welcome, orient, and support students throughout their arrival to and experience at NC State. This includes initiatives such as New Student Orientation, Wolfpack Welcome Week, open houses, and other programs that introduce students to the Libraries and engage them with the people, services, spaces, and expertise that support academic success, creativity, and well-being. The position coordinates the Libraries' Personal Librarian Program and works with colleagues across the Libraries and campus to connect students with library services, learning opportunities, and experiential learning environments. Instruction and Public Service As a member of the Teaching, Learning, and Outreach team, the Student Success Librarian contributes to the Libraries' instruction program by teaching library instruction sessions for undergraduate courses such as ENG 101 and COM 110. The position also serves as an Ask Us Service Manager, serving as the staff member responsible for public service operations during assigned shifts at one of the Libraries' primary Ask Us service points, including supervising student employees, making operational decisions, and providing virtual reference services. Service and Professional Responsibilities This position serves on library-wide committees, task forces, and teams. Librarians are expected to engage in professional development, contribute to developments in the field, and participate in service activities. The position reports to the Associate Head, Learning Spaces & Services. This position is based in North Carolina. This position is eligible for flexible hours with a hybrid work environment based on departmental and operational needs. This position will require a majority of onsite work. NC State University promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision, and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interests, and experience would enable them to support the university.

title: UTS-Temporary Event Preparation Staff
description: NC State Continuing and Lifelong Education (NCSCaLE) is a division of the Provost within the Office of the Vice Provost for Continuing Education. The McKimmon Conference and Training Center (MCTC) reports to the Continuing & Professional Education Director. MCTC has 33,000 square feet of meeting space and assists with set-ups, exhibits, educational event gatherings, catering, and printing services which include shipping and receiving, and can provide 650 spaces of free parking. MCTC works with campus partners, private/corporate business industry, and local, state, and federal government. MCTC is dedicated to partnering with our global-class faculty and academic partners, as well as cultivating a culture of continuous lifelong learning by identifying and integrating best practices throughout your journey with us. MCTC can help create a meaningful experience that transforms into a lifelong experience. MCTC strives to enrich the lives of people and stay on the cutting edge of the industry. Primary purpose of the position: The Event Preparation Staff plays a crucial role in ensuring the successful execution of various events, including workshops, conferences, and seminars. For example, the Bar Exam, Cyber Security, Engineering Career Fair, and Global Green Energy. Event Staff responsibilities span before and after an event. Here are the key duties: Planning and Preparation: The Logistics Manager/Co-Crew Leader will provide the Event Prep set-up instructions via Social Tables, clients, or coordinators for each space. Ensure precise collaboration and accuracy in setting up event spaces are complete. Manage all logistics and manage all scheduling concerns Ensure compliance with safety and health regulations. Post-Event: Break down all of the equipment and place the equipment (chairs/tables) in the storage area. Other Work/Responsibilities: Occasional specialized duties may include Audio/Visual technical assistance and operation of specialized equipment as training allows. The Event Preparation Staff contributes to exceptional customer service and ensures that events run smoothly, efficiently, and positively reflect on the brand. Event Staff plays a key role in creating memorable experiences for attendees!

title: Assistant Director, Member Services and Student Employment
description: NC State University is seeking an energetic, innovative, and student-centered leader to serve as the Assistant Director of Member Services and Student Employment. We are looking for a collaborative, proven leader who thrives in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment and is passionate about student success. The ideal candidate will empower both student and professional staff to cultivate world-class wellness and recreation programs, services, and facilities that enrich the student experience inside and outside the classroom. The Assistant Director provides strategic leadership and management for Wellness and Recreation member services, point-of-sale (POS) and facility access software, and the department-wide student employment program. Additionally, the candidate will identify and develop alternative revenue streams while adding value to the student experience through special events and programming. Specific responsibilities include: Staff Supervision and Human Resource Management Direct Supervision: Provide strategic leadership, supervision, and performance management for the Coordinator of Member Services and the Student Employment Specialist. Indirect Supervision: Indirectly oversee approximately 120 student staff, ensuring the team delivers the highest level of customer service to students and members. Department-Wide Student Employment: Manage the comprehensive student employment program (recruitment, hiring, onboarding, orientation, and training) for a department that employs approximately 650 student staff annually. Process Optimization: Evaluate current HR workflows to identify efficiencies, develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and maintain comprehensive training materials for the department. Payroll & Timekeeping: Oversee complex department-wide timekeeping and payroll processes to ensure data integrity and strict deadline compliance. Student Recognition: Spearhead comprehensive student staff appreciation initiatives, including Student Employee Appreciation Week and university Wellness Days; plan, produce, and host the annual end-of-year awards ceremony for over 250 attendees to celebrate student staff achievements. Membership Growth and Marketing Membership Management: Drive the strategic growth, forecasting, and optimization of Wellness and Recreation Member Services, directly overseeing annual membership and auxiliary revenues exceeding $900k. Growth & Retention: Design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive recruitment and retention strategies; establish continuous sales pipelines for alumni, faculty, staff, and external community segments. Community Engagement: Build strong relationships with Centennial Campus affiliates and organize special events to boost member satisfaction. Marketing & Promotions: Develop high-impact marketing materials, targeted digital promotions, programmatic tours, and data-backed incentives to maximize conversion rates for prospective members. Revenue Generation and Partnerships Auxiliary Revenue Streams: Identify and cultivate alternate revenue streams, including the conceptualization and execution of specialized member events, paid programming, and creative retail or facility rentals. Corporate Partnerships: Assist with the design and execution of strategic marketing partnership/sponsorship programs; collaborate with external partners to maximize marketing packages and fundraising opportunities. Financial Oversight: Manage the specific and direct fiscal budgets for Member Services, the student staff training program, and the student professional development fund. Strategic Leadership and Systems Administration Leadership: Provide leadership and direction for Wellness and Recreation member services, point of sale and facility access software and student employment program by implementing goals, expectations and processes for programs and revenues. Systems Administration: Provide strategic direction for the maintenance, upkeep, configuration, communication, and design of InnoSoft Fusion (the department’s POS and facility access software) and FusionGO (the department’s mobile application for program registration and facility access). Compliance: Ensure all operations adhere to University, State, and Federal regulations, as well as specific departmental or governing body requirements. Committee Leadership: Lead the Wellness and Recreation student training and development work team, as well as the Fusion department work team. Data-Driven Evaluation: Serve on the Wellness and Recreation assessment work team; design satisfaction surveys, evaluate program efforts, and develop data-driven recommendations to implement new programs. General Support: Assist as needed with all required departmental functions and university-wide initiatives.

title: Business Officer
description: Reporting to the Director for Student Leadership & Engagement, you will support the financial, administrative, human resources, and operational success of the department. In this highly collaborative role, you will help ensure Student Leadership & Engagement has the resources, processes, and operational support needed to advance student engagement and leadership development initiatives. Working across finance, human resources, office operations, and campus partnerships, you will partner with professional staff, student employees, university departments, and campus stakeholders to maintain efficient operations and provide the administrative infrastructure needed to support the department’s programs and services. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Financial & Business Operations Manage budget and accounting records for Student Leadership & Engagement, supporting an annual budget in excess of $1.5 million. Coordinate financial reconciliation and the distribution of appropriations funding to student organizations each semester, totaling nearly $200,000 annually, as approved by Student Government, the Student Body Treasurer, and their advisors. Oversee monthly financial reconciliation, including PCard management, office projects, accounting activities, and cash assets. Manage PCard purchases, Marketplace orders, vouchers, and other purchasing activities in accordance with University policies and procedures. Prepare and submit quarterly financial reports to the division finance office. Manage departmental deposits and maintain accurate financial records. Communicate financial plans, spending guidelines, and budget strategies to the Student Leadership & Engagement team. Assist staff with contract and vendor processes, ensuring appropriate procedures are followed. Provide ongoing financial training and guidance to professional staff on University purchasing, travel, student employment, and budget planning. Human Resources & Employee Coordination Coordinate required clearances for department staff and student employees. Maintain accurate department rosters and Google Groups to support effective communication and access. Support onboarding and offboarding processes for student and professional staff. Assist with student employee hiring processes, including the annual PEP application process. Communicate HR timelines, requirements, and processes to supervisors. Coordinate with appropriate University partners to support timely completion of employment-related processes. Office Operations & Administrative Coordination Serve as the primary departmental requester for work orders and coordinate facilities-related needs. Assist with developing and maintaining office operations, procedures, and administrative policies. Support departmental workflows, documentation, and internal reporting processes. Manage department storage facilities and ensure resources are organized and maintained. Serve as the department surplus manager, coordinating the disposition of surplus property in accordance with University procedures. Monitor and maintain office supply inventories to support daily operations. Coordinate facility and operational needs with campus partners, including NC Student Centers and DASA Facilities. This role is an opportunity to contribute to a collaborative team while helping ensure Student Leadership & Engagement has the financial and operational foundation needed to support students and advance departmental priorities. If you are an organized, detail-oriented professional who enjoys supporting people, managing resources, and improving administrative processes, we encourage you to apply.

title: Budget Analyst
department: 200101 - Dean's Office - Poole College Of Management
description: The Budget Analyst provides professional budget and financial support to the Poole College Office of Business Services (OBS). Reporting to the Finance Officer, the position assists academic and administrative units with budget development, financial monitoring, and reporting to support effective fiscal management. As, the Budget Analyst you will analyze financial data, prepares budget reports, monitors expenditures, and advises departments on budgetary options and the financial implications of operational decisions. Additionally, you will work collaboratively with college leadership, department administrators, and central university offices to ensure compliance with university policies and funding requirements while supporting responsible stewardship of financial resources. Primary Responsibilities include but aren't limited to: Budget Development and Financial Monitoring Assist in the preparation and maintenance of annual operating, personnel, and departmental budgets. Monitor departmental budgets throughout the fiscal year and identify variances between budgeted and actual expenditures. Review expenditures to ensure compliance with university policies, funding restrictions, and budgetary provisions. Assist departments in evaluating available funding and understanding the budgetary impact of proposed expenditures. Support year-end budget reconciliation and fiscal close activities. Monitor salary funding, labor redistributions, and position funding to ensure accurate financial reporting. Financial Analysis and Reporting Compile financial data and prepare recurring and ad hoc budget and financial reports for college leadership and departmental administrators. Analyze budget activity and financial trends to support operational decision-making. Maintain financial records and reconcile budget information using university financial systems. Assist with financial reporting for operating, trust, grant, and other funding sources as assigned. Provide supporting documentation and analysis for budget requests and financial reviews. Budget Consultation and Customer Service Advise department administrators and staff regarding budget availability, funding options, and budgetary implications of financial transactions. Respond to budget and financial inquiries from faculty, staff, and administrators. Interpret university financial policies and procedures related to budget administration. Build collaborative relationships with academic and administrative units to support effective financial management. Provide guidance on budget processes and financial reporting requirements. Systems, Processes, and Continuous Improvement Assist in developing and maintaining budget tracking tools, spreadsheets, and standard financial reports. Identify opportunities to improve budget processes and reporting efficiency. Support implementation of process improvements and updates to financial systems. Maintain accurate financial documentation and records. If you are a detail-oriented financial professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, solving problems, and partnering with others to support sound financial decisions, we invite you to apply.

title: Research Technician (Lab and Field) - DEPP
description:
Posting Number: PG195167SP
Internal Recruitment: No
Working Title: Research Technician (Lab and Field) - DEPP
Anticipated Hiring Range: $42,971 - $45,000
Work Schedule: Monday – Friday, 6:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.
Job Location: Raleigh, NC
Department: Entomology and Plant Pathology

Essential Job Duties: Join the Cotton Genetics and Breeding Lab and contribute to research that advances cotton genetics, genomics, and plant breeding. As a Research Technician, you will provide essential technical and operational support across field, greenhouse, growth chamber, laboratory, and seed-processing environments. Working alongside faculty, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborators, you will help ensure research activities are conducted safely, accurately, and efficiently while supporting the development and evaluation of improved cotton breeding materials. Key Responsibilities Research Operations & Technical Support Support cotton genetics and breeding research by preparing field plots, greenhouse materials, and controlled-environment facilities for planting, phenotyping, harvesting, and research trials. Perform mechanical and manual planting, harvesting, ginning, acid-delinting, seed processing, and sample preparation while advancing and maintaining breeding populations through controlled crosses and self-pollination activities. Collect, measure, and record phenotypic and experimental data from field, greenhouse, growth chamber, and laboratory studies to support ongoing research projects. Data Management & Research Compliance Maintain accurate electronic records for phenotypic data, seed inventories, experimental documentation, and research activities using tools such as Excel and Google Sheets. Prepare and maintain documentation related to chemical storage, sample tracking, laboratory safety, and equipment use while ensuring compliance with institutional research and Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) requirements. Equipment, Facilities & Resource Management Operate, maintain, and perform basic troubleshooting of field equipment, laboratory instruments, ginning and acid-delinting machinery, irrigation tools, and state vehicles. Manage research resources by organizing seed stocks, supplies, greenhouse and field materials, and laboratory inventories to support efficient research operations. Collaboration & Field Operations Travel to research stations and off-campus facilities to assist with experimental setup, plot layout, planting, crop maintenance, data collection, and harvest activities. Coordinate daily research activities with cooperating scientists, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, research station staff, collaborators, and visiting scientists to support timely project completion and effective program operations.
Other Responsibilities: Conduct ginning and acid-delinting of seed cotton; catalog, store, and prepare seed samples for field, greenhouse, and growth chamber planting. Travel to research stations and off-campus facilities to support field and nursery operations, including experimental design, plot layout, field marking, and planting. Perform mechanical and manual planting, harvesting, and seed processing of cotton in field plots, greenhouses, and controlled environments. Coordinate planting, breeding, harvesting, and seed processing activities with students, postdoctoral researchers, collaborators, and research station personnel. Prepare and maintain field plots and greenhouse materials, including envelopes, stakes, pots, growth media, reagents, and chemical solutions required for experiments. Conduct cotton breeding activities, including making crosses, selfing flowers, phenotyping plants and plots, and preparing samples for analysis. Collect, observe, measure, and record phenotypic and experimental data from field, greenhouse, growth chamber, and laboratory settings. Develop, maintain, catalog, and share digital records (e.g., Excel or Google Sheets) for phenotypic data, seed inventories, supplies, and equipment. Operate, maintain, and perform basic troubleshooting of field equipment, ginning and acid-delinting machinery, laboratory tools, and state vehicles. Prepare and maintain documentation related to chemical storage, sample tracking, laboratory safety, and equipment use. Ensure compliance with environmental health and safety regulations and institutional research compliance guidelines across all facilities. Manage program resources, including seed stocks, supplies, tools, equipment, greenhouse and field materials, and vehicles, following established protocols. Assist and work collaboratively with students, postdocs, visiting scientists, collaborators, and stakeholders to support research activities and compliance at work sites.

Experience coordinating research activities and priorities while working collaboratively with graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, research station personnel, visiting scientists, and other research team members.

title: DRIVES Research Associate
description: The DRIVES Agroecology Research Associate will work under the supervision of the Agroecology Professor to support the growth of the Agroecology Lab’s research program about the impacts of crop diversification. Key responsibilities will include organizing and maintaining the Diverse Rotation Improve Valuable Ecosystem Services (DRIVES) database (drives-network.org) and conducting synthesis research on crop diversification across a range of environmental conditions. The DRIVES database is a network of data from long-term cropping systems experiments. The Associate will be responsible for database expansion and enhancing interoperability using data dictionaries and controlled vocabularies when including additional variables. They will lead database content development and write code to assess the linkages between rotational diversity and economic performance and soil health. They will prepare publications for peer-reviewed journals and develop partnerships across the long-term cropping systems research community. Duties include: Research Data Management & Database Development Organize, maintain, and expand the Diverse Rotation Improve Valuable Ecosystem Services (DRIVES) database. Enhance database interoperability by developing and implementing data dictionaries and controlled vocabularies. Integrate and validate data from long-term cropping systems experiments across multiple research sites. Ensure data quality, consistency, and accessibility to support collaborative agroecology research. Research Analysis & Scholarly Publications Conduct synthesis research evaluating the impacts of crop diversification across diverse environmental conditions. Develop and maintain analytical code to examine relationships between rotational diversity, economic performance, and soil health. Interpret research findings and prepare manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed scientific journals. Present research findings and contribute to reports, publications, and other scholarly products. Collaboration & Research Network Development Develop and maintain partnerships with collaborators across the long-term cropping systems research community. Coordinate with researchers to facilitate data sharing and database expansion. Participate in project meetings and communicate project progress with internal and external stakeholders. Contribute to advancing the Agroecology Lab's research program through collaborative initiatives. Position is contingent on availability of funds, potentially 6 months to 1.5 years

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar - PMB
description: The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology supports teaching, research, and extension programs in fundamental plant biology and microbiology, including basic and applied research, teaching graduate and undergraduate courses, mentoring graduate and undergraduate students, and outreach to state and national clientele. The Postdoctoral Research Scholar is invited to join the Lyu lab and lead cross-boundary microbiology research in one or more research projects depending on mutual interests. Research in the lab receives funding from the NIH, USDA, NC State, industry, and private-public partnership. Current microorganisms of interest include oxygen-sensitive archaea, such as methane producers (methanogens), and bacteria, including syntrophic hydrogen producers (syntrophs), hydrogen sulfide producers (sulfidogens), and fermenters. Candidates are encouraged to fill out the trainee’s interest form ( https://forms.gle/LLSBqrB6p2ZfJqxRA ) before applying to this position. The successful candidate will contribute to our research by: Modernizing classical microbiology approaches to discover and characterize physiology-relevant phenotypes. Integrating omics, genetic, and biochemical approaches to investigate physiology-determining mechanisms. Developing experimental models to evaluate the impact of archaeal and/or bacterial physiology in health, agriculture, environment, or biotechnology.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Crop and Soil Sciences encompasses varied disciplines in research, extension, and teaching. The department’s mission is to develop future leaders in crop, soil and environmental sciences, improve crop plants and products, devise effective and sustainable crop production systems, devise effective and sustainable soil management techniques in both agriculture and urban settings; and disseminate crop, soil, and environmental science, knowledge for the benefit of producers of food, feed, turf, biofuels and fiber in North Carolina. Duties and Responsibilities: The primary responsibilities of this position are to conduct, perform, and execute cotton genetics and breeding research focused on genomic selection (GS), nested association mapping (NAM), and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for important agronomic traits in tetraploid cotton. The candidate is expected to perform cotton genetics and breeding research in the field, greenhouse, and lab-based settings; develop and evaluate genetic, genomic resources, and analysis of genotypic data (GBS, resequencing, array-based and targeted genotyping panel SNPs) and phenotypic data, and use a varied array of statistical, genetics, and bioinformatics tools and methods. This position requires the candidate to summarize results, present them as technical reports and presentations at the meetings, and communicate through peer-reviewed publications. The candidate will have the opportunity to participate and cooperatively work with other lab members in the ongoing trait mapping and breeding projects towards dissecting the genetic architecture of agronomic traits and improving cotton productivity through advanced breeding tools. Further, the candidate is expected to mentor and supervise the students in the cotton program. This position is initially for one year but can be extended based on satisfactory research progress and availability of funds.

title: Director of Industry Research Partnerships
description: The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) at NC State University is seeking a Director of Industry Research Partnerships to lead the development and expansion of strategic collaborations between CALS researchers and industry partners. Reporting to the Associate Dean for Research and Director of the North Carolina Agricultural Research Service (NCARS), this position serves as a key connector between faculty, corporate partners, and university stakeholders to advance research, innovation, and workforce development. In this role, you'll cultivate relationships with organizations ranging from emerging start-ups to global corporations, helping transform groundbreaking research into meaningful partnerships that accelerate discovery and economic impact. You'll work across the university to identify opportunities, strengthen existing collaborations, and create new pathways for research, commercialization, student engagement, and industry investment in one of the nation's leading colleges of agriculture and life sciences. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Strategic Partnership Development: Develop and grow long-term industry partnerships that support research, education, extension, and workforce development initiatives. Identify and cultivate new corporate partnerships, including emerging start-up companies, with an emphasis on opportunities supporting the North Carolina Food Animal Initiative (FAI). Create innovative partnership models, including sponsored research, grants, contracts, research centers, internships, co-location opportunities, and other collaborative initiatives. Stay informed of CALS research strengths and emerging industry priorities to proactively connect faculty with corporate partners. Create opportunities for faculty and students to engage with industry through meaningful collaborations and experiential learning. Corporate Relationship Management: Serve as the primary liaison between corporate partners and CALS, ensuring responsive communication and successful execution of partnership agreements. Build trusted, long-term relationships by delivering exceptional service and identifying opportunities to expand existing collaborations. Maintain a comprehensive inventory of corporate partnerships and establish best practices for partnership management. Collaborate with the Office of Sponsored Programs and Regulatory Compliance Services (SPARCS) to support research agreements and contracting processes. Help safeguard NC State's intellectual property by coordinating with the Office of Research Commercialization throughout partnership development. Campus Collaboration & Research Commercialization: Partner with CALS leadership, University Advancement, and university corporate engagement colleagues to develop coordinated strategies for industry engagement. Connect faculty with commercialization resources and licensing opportunities through the Office of Research Commercialization. Coach faculty and students in communicating the value and real-world applications of their research to industry partners. Plan and lead corporate visits, research showcases, and engagement events that strengthen relationships and promote CALS research excellence. Join a nationally recognized research college where your ability to build strategic partnerships will help accelerate innovation, expand research opportunities, and create lasting impact for agriculture, life sciences, and communities across North Carolina and beyond. If you're a collaborative relationship builder who enjoys connecting people, ideas, and industry to advance meaningful research, we encourage you to apply.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Physics Department provides: (1) High quality Physics instruction to the University community through courses in introductory physics; (2) educational opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students in physics through high quality curricula, faculty, and research facilities; (3) outreach programs that advance scientific knowledge. Our research programs cover a wide spectrum including astrophysics, general relativity, condensed matter theory and experiment, computational physics, biophysics, nanoscale science, physics education, experimental nuclear physics, particle and nuclear theory, experimental optics, and experimental atomic and molecular physics. The department enrolls approximately 120 graduate students and 140 undergrad physics majors. The department size is approximately 56 faculty members. While working in this department, you will be expected to foster a supportive and welcoming environment. NC State promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interest and experience would enable them to support the university. Duties and Responsibilities: Predictive modeling and design of protein–nucleic acid interactions, including protein–DNA recognition, protein–RNA interactions, and protein- or small-molecule binding to oligonucleotide aptamers, in close collaboration with experimental groups Physics-based and AI-enabled modeling of chromatin organization, RNA conformational dynamics, and RNA–protein phase separation. Depending on the scholar’s background, the research may emphasize bimolecular simulation, AI for bimolecular science, or an integrated combination of both. Responsibilities will include computational method development, rigorous validation against experimental data, development of reproducible software and workflows, manuscript preparation, and dissemination of research findings. Conduct independent and collaborative computational research on bimolecular structure, dynamics, interactions, and functions. Develop, implement, and evaluate molecular simulation and/or deep-learning methods; construct and analyze atomistic or coarse-grained models; integrate structural, sequence, thermodynamic, and experimental data; and perform rigorous statistical and mechanistic analyses. Research may address protein–DNA and protein–RNA recognition, aptamer binding and design, RNA conformational ensembles and dynamics, RNA–protein phase separation, and chromatin organization. Maintain reproducible, well-documented software and workflows, communicate findings through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and research software, and collaborate closely with experimental and computational research partners. The Department of Physics and Astronomy at NC State University seeks to fill the position for a Postdoctoral Research Scholar in the Lin Research Group. The scholar will advance computational studies of bimolecular structure, dynamics, interactions, and functions. The initial appointment is for one year, with possible renewal for a second year contingent upon satisfactory performance. In the cover letter, candidates should briefly describe the project that best demonstrates their relevant expertise, their independent contributions to method, algorithm, or software development, and the connection of this work to one or more of the position’s research directions.

title: UTS- Temporary Clinical Research Coordinator at UNC Chapel Hill
description: The UNC Institute for Trauma Recovery within the Department of Psychiatry seeks to advance understanding of trauma recovery and develop interventions that improve recovery. The foundation of our past and current success is our fantastic team of faculty and staff. Our team believes that achieving new discoveries for trauma survivors around the globe, via the conduct of observational studies and randomized controlled trials, is an extremely meaningful and satisfying way to spend one’s professional life. We work to place the trauma survivor at the center of all of our decisions and to serve them through our work. We continuously work to create a community where our team members serve trauma survivors and actualize their career growth and individual leadership potential. The Clinical Research Coordinator will support the Institute’s Better Tomorrow Network (BTN), the first research network in the world dedicated to improving treatments and care for survivors of sexual assault. The mission of the Better Tomorrow Network is to remove barriers to the conduct of high-quality, large-scale research studies that improve the lives of sexual assault survivors. The Network brings together leading sexual assault treatment centers, researchers, community stakeholders, and survivors into a survivor-centered collaborative focused on advancing prevention, early intervention, treatment, and systems-level improvements in care and outcomes for survivors. This position will play an important role in supporting multi-site clinical research studies conducted through the Better Tomorrow Network. The Clinical Research Coordinator will assist with study operations, participant recruitment and retention efforts, regulatory and study documentation, data collection and quality assurance activities, and coordination with collaborating clinical sites and research partners. The position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, professionalism, and the ability to work effectively with interdisciplinary teams in a fast-paced research environment focused on trauma-informed care and survivor-centered research practices. The Clinical Research Coordinator is responsible for the planning, organization, and conduct of multiple clinical research study protocols, including independently collecting and recording data, project administration, and communication with various stakeholders.

description: The Department of Forestry and Environmental Resources has a wide variety of strengths in forestry and natural resources management, policy and economics, environmental science and technology, wildlife and conservation biology, tree improvement, silviculture, forest biotechnology, and international forestry. The Department has over 90 full time faculty and staff, and more than 750 undergraduate and 150 graduate students. We are committed to fostering a collaborative environment where innovation, respect, and excellence in education, extension, and research. Faculty, staff, and students work together with business, industry, government, community groups, and non-government organizations to address a wide range of challenges facing our state and the world. These partnerships facilitate research and discovery, teaching and learning, and outreach and service. Additional information about the department can be found at http://cnr.ncsu.edu/fer. The college’s comprehensive approach to teaching, research, and service encompass the many and varied ways in which people’s physical, economic, and social needs are met through the wise use of natural resources.
