title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology at NC State University is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Scholar to conduct research focused on the isolation, characterization, genomics, and virulence of Orientia spp. bacteria associated with free-living chiggers. The successful candidate will work as part of a collaborative research team investigating Orientia spp. through a combination of bacterial culture, cell-based assays, next-generation sequencing, and genomic bioinformatics. The position will involve laboratory research conducted in a BSL-3 facility, as well as computational analysis of bacterial genomes. Collaborating researchers will collect wild-caught, free-living chiggers in the United States and provide specimens for laboratory analysis. The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will contribute to the culture and characterization of Orientia spp., genomic sequencing and analysis, assessment of bacterial virulence, and preparation of research findings for publication and presentation. Key Responsibilities: Culture Orientia spp. bacteria from specimens collected by collaborating researchers and establish and maintain pure bacterial cultures. Conduct laboratory studies to characterize Orientia spp. and assess bacterial virulence using appropriate human or animal cell lines. Perform bacterial culture and related laboratory research in a BSL-3 facility in accordance with established biosafety and laboratory protocols. Prepare purified bacterial DNA for next-generation sequencing and coordinate genomic sequencing with external sequencing service providers. Use probe-directed genome sequencing approaches, as appropriate, to obtain genomic data from Orientia spp. present in crude bacterial mixtures. Assemble, annotate, and analyze Orientia spp. genome sequences using bioinformatic approaches. Compare newly generated genome sequences with known Orientia spp. genomes to determine species identity and characterize genetic relationships. Conduct genomic analyses to investigate genetic factors associated with bacterial virulence and other relevant biological characteristics. Integrate laboratory and genomic findings to support research objectives. Prepare manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and other scholarly products for dissemination of research findings. Present research findings at scientific meetings and conferences. Contribute to collaborative research activities, grant proposals, and other scholarly activities as appropriate. Maintain accurate records of laboratory experiments, genomic analyses, and research findings. Other Duties and Responsibilities: 1. Culture and characterize Orientia spp. bacteria – 50% Culture Orientia spp. bacteria from wild-caught, free-living chiggers collected in the United States by collaborating researchers. Establish and maintain pure cultures of Orientia spp. bacteria and conduct laboratory studies to characterize bacterial growth and virulence. Perform bacterial culture and related experimental work in a BSL-3 laboratory using established biosafety protocols. Culture Orientia spp. in appropriate animal cell lines and assess the virulence and biological characteristics of isolated bacterial cultures using human or other animal cell lines. Chiggers will be collected and provided by collaborating researchers in culture media and will not be provided as live specimens. 2. Obtain genomic sequence data for Orientia spp. – 10% Obtain genome sequence data from Orientia spp. bacteria using next-generation sequencing approaches. Prepare purified DNA obtained from bacterial cultures for submission to an external DNA sequencing service. As an alternative approach, collaborate with private sequencing service providers to use probe-directed genome sequencing to obtain genomic data from Orientia spp. present in crude bacterial mixtures derived from free-living chiggers. 3. Assemble and analyze Orientia spp. genomes – 30% Assemble and analyze genomic sequence data from Orientia spp. bacteria. Compare newly sequenced genomes with publicly available genomes from known Orientia spp. to determine species identity and characterize genetic relationships. Use genomic and bioinformatic analyses to identify genetic factors associated with bacterial virulence and other relevant biological characteristics. Interpret and integrate genomic findings with laboratory data to support research objectives and prepare results for publication in scientific journals. 4. Research communication and scholarly activities – 10% Analyze, interpret, and document research findings; prepare manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and other scholarly materials; contribute to research proposals and grant applications as appropriate; and present research findings at scientific meetings and conferences. Maintain accurate records of experimental procedures, results, and genomic analyses and contribute to collaborative research activities with internal and external research partners.

title: Radiology Technician
description: Help deliver high-quality diagnostic care to the NC State community by providing professional radiology services in a patient-centered clinical environment. As a Radiology Technician at Campus Health, you will produce high-quality diagnostic images using modern radiology equipment and cloud-based software while supporting providers with timely, accurate imaging that contributes to exceptional patient care. This role combines technical expertise, patient interaction, and a commitment to safety to ensure efficient clinical operations and positive patient experiences. Key Responsibilities Diagnostic Imaging & Patient Care Perform radiographic procedures, including patient positioning and digital image capture, to produce high-quality diagnostic images for Campus Health providers. Apply knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and disease processes to deliver safe, accurate, and compassionate patient care throughout the imaging process. Communicate relevant patient information to clinicians and radiologists, serving as a liaison to support timely diagnosis and treatment. Clinical Operations & Documentation Accurately enter patient information into the electronic health record and communicate effectively with patients, providers, and staff through phone, email, and in-person interactions. Maintain radiology equipment through routine quality control, cleaning, and monitoring to ensure reliable operation and high-quality imaging. Safety & Regulatory Compliance Maintain a clean clinical environment and follow infectious disease protocols to support patient and staff safety. Properly handle medical, biological, and infectious waste while adhering to radiation safety, OSHA, and Environmental Health and Safety standards. Participate in scheduled meetings, drills, training, and other departmental activities to support ongoing operational readiness. If you are a detail-oriented radiology professional who enjoys combining technical expertise with compassionate patient care and thrives in a collaborative healthcare environment, we encourage you to apply. Join Campus Health and play an important role in supporting the health and well-being of the NC State community.

title: Painter
description: Join our passionate Facilities team as a Painter in the Trade Shop, where your skills will help keep our campus vibrant, safe, and inviting. In this role, you’ll use your expertise in painting, finishing, and drywall repair to maintain the beauty and functionality of our buildings and spaces . If you enjoy hands-on work, attention to detail, and seeing the visible results of your craftsmanship, we invite you to apply and be part of the team that helps our campus shine. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Prepare surfaces by cleaning, sanding, patching, priming, and ensuring optimal conditions for painting Paint a variety of surfaces, including walls, ceilings, casework, fixtures, handrails, bollards, and equipment Perform advanced surface preparation, including sanding, applying wood filler, Bondo, caulking, and completing drywall repairs. Match paint colors and finishes to maintain consistency throughout campus facilities. Mix and tint paints accurately using specialized equipment Inspect work areas, materials, and vehicles regularly to ensure safety and compliance with hazardous material regulations Review plans, product specifications, and PPE requirements to ensure proper application and disposal procedures Report safety concerns, infractions, accidents, and injuries promptly in accordance with University policy Assist with power washing and other maintenance projects across campus as needed Collaborate with other Trade Shops units to support broader maintenance and repair initiatives Lift up to 60 pounds frequently and up to 90 plus pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations. Communicate effectively with supervisors and the general public, understand and follow verbal and written instructions and other communications related to work assignments and other matters.

title: Clinical Pathology Residency
department: 196001 - Department of Population Health and Pathobiology
description: The College of Veterinary Medicine at North Carolina State University invites outstanding candidates to apply for a 3-year residency position in veterinary clinical pathology beginning July 2027. The training program focuses on in-depth learning of clinical pathology and ACVP board preparation under the supervision of 4 ACVP board-certified clinical pathologists. The resident will join a busy clinical pathology service and play a role in student education and hospital interactions. In addition, there are local veterinary diagnostic labs and the graduate programs at the CVM draw on abundant resources available in the Research Triangle region (universities, industry, and government) to provide unique research and career opportunities. Applicants must possess a DVM or equivalent degree(s), have an excellent academic record, strong communication skills, and be committed to a career in veterinary clinical pathology. Clinical or a post-DVM experience is desirable. NC State University is near two other major universities (Duke University and the University of North Carolina - Chapel Hill) and the Research Triangle Park, which includes multiple government agencies, non-profit institutes, biotechnology, and large pharmaceutical companies. To view full vacancy announcement, additional requirements, and to apply online, please visit https://jobs.ncsu.edu/ See https://cvm.ncsu.edu/education/residencies/residencies-clinical-pathology/ for program description and additional information. Applications should include (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) statement of career goals, (3) official college and professional school transcripts, and (4) three references (see link to form). We will begin reviewing applications on Oct. 15, 2026, and continue until a suitable candidate is found. The position is available July 15, 2027. The following link is for the reference form which will be in place of traditional letters. Please provide this link to your references https://forms.gle/Mm7Sgb2vBiwhNWZ79 Questions related to the application process can be directed to Caitlin Falls in CVM Human Resources. Reference forms and transcripts can be sent to her via email or regular mail.

title: Associate Director, Prospect Intelligence
description: The Associate Director of Prospect Intelligence leads the research and analytics function within Prospect Development, advancing a sophisticated, data‑informed approach to prospect identification, principal‑gift strategy, and pipeline development. This role manages the philanthropic research team, oversees principal‑level research deliverables, and builds the office’s analytics and predictive modeling infrastructure to support University Advancement’s strategic priorities. Reporting to the Director of Prospect Development, the Associate Director works collaboratively with the Principal Gifts team and college‑ and unit‑based development officers. As a key leader within Prospect Development, they train team members, elevate research standards, and drive innovation through advanced analytics, visualization, and emerging technologies.

title: UTS - Temporary Radiology Technician at NC State
description: The primary duties of this position include the following: Taking X-ray images of the human body per order by provider. Interact with internal staff, patients, and referring providers through email, phone, and in-person communications. Keeping equipment clean and in working order. Responsible for maintaining equipment and quality control. Attend scheduled meetings, drills, and training. Perform technical procedures, including patient positioning for radiographs and digital image capturing. Provide excellent patient care by applying full knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and disease processes. Provide quick and accurate information regarding each patient, acting as a liaison between clinicians and radiologists. Proficiently enter data into the electronic health record. Maintain a clean working environment to ensure standards are followed and infection is not spread. Handle medical, biological, and infectious waste appropriately. Follow all radiation safety, OSHA, and Environmental Health and Safety standards.

title: Equine and Farm Animal Attendant
description: This temporary position will be responsible for maintaining a clean and sanitary hospital through routine stall/cage maintenance, hospital cleaning and disinfection, and waste removal. Restrain and provide basic husbandry for equine and farm animal patients. Small animal hospital backup, same duties.

title: Payroll Tax Accountant
description: Reporting to the Payroll Tax Manager, the Payroll Tax Accountant plays a key role in ensuring accurate, compliant payroll tax operations for one of the nation's leading public research universities. This position is responsible for administering multi-state payroll tax compliance, reconciling payroll tax data, researching and resolving complex tax issues, and ensuring the university remains compliant with federal, state, and local tax regulations. In this role, you'll apply your payroll tax expertise to solve complex compliance challenges, improve payroll tax processes, and help ensure employees across multiple states are paid accurately and taxed correctly. You'll collaborate with partners across Payroll, Accounting, Benefits, Finance, and Human Resources while serving as a trusted resource on payroll tax regulations, reporting requirements, and emerging legislative changes. Your work will directly support the integrity, accuracy, and continuous improvement of the university's payroll operations. Key Responsibilities fall within the following core functional areas : Payroll Tax Compliance: Manage multi-state payroll tax filings, remittances, reconciliations, and reporting to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local tax regulations. Coordinate quarterly and annual payroll tax reporting, including W-2 reconciliations and unemployment insurance filings. Monitor changing tax legislation and implement new payroll tax requirements. Payroll Tax Analysis & Resolution: Research and resolve complex payroll tax discrepancies, withholding issues, and reporting exceptions. Partner with Payroll and HR teams to identify root causes, improve processes, and strengthen payroll tax accuracy. Taxable Compensation Administration: Oversee the payroll taxation of taxable fringe benefits and non-salary compensation, including relocation expenses, tuition waivers, awards, and other taxable payments. Ensure IRS reporting requirements are accurately applied across payroll cycles. Process Improvement & Collaboration: Test payroll tax system updates and validate compliance with new tax rates and reporting requirements. Develop and maintain payroll tax procedures while serving as a trusted resource for internal stakeholders on payroll tax regulations and best practices. Operational Support: Provide backup support for payroll tax operations and contribute to the continued success of the Payroll team. Bring your expertise to a collaborative team where your contributions will influence payroll operations, enhance efficiencies, and make a lasting impact across a large and complex organization. If you are a payroll tax professional with strong analytical skills, a passion for regulatory compliance, and a commitment to delivering exceptional service, we encourage you to apply.

title: Professor of the Practice in Media Arts and Production
description: The Department of Communication is seeking a collaborative scholar-practitioner who is passionate about advancing creative media production through innovative storytelling, emerging technologies, and critical inquiry. In this role, you will help prepare the next generation of media professionals by combining creative practice with meaningful engagement across the social, cultural, political, and technological dimensions of contemporary communication. You will contribute to a forward-thinking academic community by teaching media arts and production courses, helping shape the future of the department's media production curriculum, and fostering connections that extend beyond the classroom. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, partnerships with industry and community organizations, and leadership of shared creative spaces, you will play an important role in expanding the department's strengths in digital media production, creative practice, and critical making. Key Responsibilities: Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in media arts and production, including areas such as film and video production, documentary and nonfiction storytelling, transmedia storytelling, and other emerging forms of creative media. Incorporate innovative approaches to storytelling and media technologies, including audiovisual, interactive, immersive, generative, AI-assisted, mobile, locative, social media, installation, and game-based media, as appropriate to your expertise. Contribute to the continued development and evolution of the department's media production curriculum. Coordinate instructional staffing for media production courses. Provide oversight of the department's media lab and support an engaging learning environment for students and faculty. Develop interdisciplinary collaborations across NC State to expand opportunities for creative scholarship and teaching. Build and maintain partnerships with media industries, arts organizations, and community partners to strengthen experiential learning and public engagement. Advance creative media production that encourages critical reflection, public engagement, and innovative forms of communication. Participate actively in departmental initiatives and contribute to a collaborative and collegial academic community. Join a department where creativity, critical inquiry, and emerging media converge. If you're ready to help students explore new forms of storytelling while contributing to an innovative and collaborative academic community, we encourage you to apply.

title: Zone Manager - 40405
description: Are you a motivated leader with a passion for creating clean, safe, and welcoming environments? Join our team as a Building Environmental Services Supervisor (Zone Manager) and play a vital role in supporting the university community through exceptional environmental services. In this position, you will lead and support a team of Environmental Services Technicians (EVS Techs), ensuring campus facilities are maintained to the highest standards of cleanliness, safety, and sanitation. You will oversee daily operations, coordinate work assignments, manage resources, conduct quality inspections, and ensure efficient service delivery across assigned areas. The Zone Manager is responsible for developing staff schedules, monitoring performance, responding to urgent and emergency situations, and providing training and guidance to team members. Through strong leadership and collaboration, you will help foster a positive work environment while ensuring compliance with health, safety, and operational standards. If you are an organized, customer-focused professional who enjoys leading teams and making a visible impact, we encourage you to apply and become part of a team dedicated to enhancing the campus experience for students, faculty, staff, and visitors. Apply today and help us create a cleaner, safer, and healthier university environment for all. Working Hours will be: Monday through Friday - 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 pm, some weekends may be needed. Key Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Supervise, coach, and assign work to Environmental Services Technicians, ensuring balanced workloads and effective daily operations across academic and research facilities. Lead team meetings, deliver safety briefings, approve timesheets and leave requests, and address personnel matters, including coaching, conflict resolution, and performance management. Develop and maintain cleaning schedules and service plans that support classroom instruction, laboratory operations, dining services, and research activities. Allocate staffing, materials, and equipment to maximize service quality, operational efficiency, and cost effectiveness. Conduct routine quality assurance inspections, document findings, and report results to leadership. Utilize inspection data to support performance evaluations, training needs, and continuous service improvement. Establish and manage emergency response and contingency plans to support academic continuity. Ensure staff complete required safety, compliance, policy, and data security training, and oversee the proper handling and storage of custodial equipment and chemicals. Manage receipts-funded budgets with an understanding of operational and financial impact. Oversee inventory, reporting, and supply usage (including uniforms and equipment) utilizing the AiM system. Research and evaluate tools and materials for economical and environmentally responsible use. Identify building deficiencies and non-functional equipment, submit maintenance work orders, and coordinate corrective actions with facility planning staff and campus partners regarding renovations, closures, and space changes. Maintain familiarity with assigned facility floor plans and communicate regularly with faculty, staff, students, and building liaisons to ensure service expectations are met. Lift, carry, and maneuver materials weighing 30–60 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: ASPSA Academic Mentor
department: 240201 - Academic Support Program for Student Athletes
description: Division of Academic and Student Affairs The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State through three integrated components: academic affairs, student affairs, and University College. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Office of Academic Support Program for Student-Athletes (ASPSA) is a comprehensive support program that strives to meet the academic, personal and professional development needs of all student-athletes, promoting excellence and effectiveness in undergraduate and graduate education as well as leadership and civic engagement. ASPSA is committed to extending the educational experience of its constituency with particular emphasis on empowering student-athletes to become strong self-advocates. We provide specialized initiatives to facilitate a smooth transition from high school to college and from college to professional life while successfully integrating student-athletes into the campus community. We strive to enhance academic skills for all student-athletes and provide personalized academic support to meet the needs of each student-athlete. ASPSA maintains a strong sense of integrity and will continue to strive to be one of the benchmark programs for academic support for all collegiate academic support programs in the nation. Mentor Position The primary role of a mentor is to meet with the assigned student-athlete to develop and improve time management skills and productive study habits. Additional responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Assist student-athletes to set academic goals (short and long term) Assist student-athletes with requesting Disability Services Office (DSO) accommodations, if needed Effectively communicate in a timely manner Participate in group training and supervision meetings

title: Tobacco Extension Agronomist
description: The Department of Crop and Soil Sciences at NC State University invites applications for an Assistant Professor and Crop Production Management Specialist. Supported through the Collins Endowment Distinguished Fellowship, this position will provide statewide leadership in applied tobacco agronomy through an integrated program of Extension, research, and teaching focused on improving the sustainability, productivity, and profitability of North Carolina’s flue-cured and burley tobacco industries. In this role, you will work alongside growers, industry partners, county Extension agents, researchers, and agricultural professionals to address real-world crop production challenges and translate research into practical solutions. You will help shape tobacco production recommendations, support producers through emerging challenges, and strengthen the connection between university research and on-farm practices. This position provides an opportunity to build upon NC State’s longstanding leadership in tobacco agronomy while advancing innovation in crop management, sustainability, and production efficiency. Key Responsibilities fall within three key areas outlined below: Extension: Provide statewide Extension leadership and technical support to tobacco growers, county Extension agents, crop consultants, NCDA&CS regional agronomists, agribusiness partners, and other industry stakeholders. Develop and deliver educational programs through grower meetings, field days, county agent trainings, farm visits, and stakeholder workshops. Translate research findings into practical recommendations that address production challenges and support informed decision-making. Maintain and update the NC Flue-Cured Tobacco Production Guide to ensure producers and agricultural professionals have access to current production recommendations and best management practices. Build and strengthen partnerships with state, regional, and national tobacco organizations to advance the tobacco production industry. Research: Develop an applied research program focused on improving flue-cured and burley tobacco production systems. Evaluate new products, technologies, and production practices, including precision agriculture approaches, to improve crop productivity, sustainability, and profitability. Investigate management strategies related to climate variability, pest management, herbicide-resistant weeds, and other emerging production challenges. Conduct on-farm research and demonstrations to evaluate practical solutions under producer conditions. Collaborate with the Director of the Official Variety Testing Program to evaluate tobacco cultivars across multiple environments. Partner with NC State faculty and external collaborators on research related to pesticide residue expectations and the evaluation of new agricultural chemicals for tobacco production. Teaching: Co-teach the undergraduate course CS 116/216 – Agronomic Crops – Cotton, Peanuts, and Tobacco during the fall semester. Provide approximately five weeks of instruction during the fall and spring semesters and two weeks every other summer. In this role, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact through Extension, research, and teaching while contributing to the continued success of North Carolina agriculture.If you are passionate about applying agricultural research to real-world challenges, building strong relationships with industry and community partners, and preparing the next generation of agricultural professionals, we encourage you to apply.

title: Temporary Genome Editing Associate
description: Duties include: Assisting with wheat and corn transformation pipeline, managing greenhouse and tissue culture work to transform plants, recover edited plants, and sequence edits. Includes protocol optimization and fine tuning on specific genotypes. Assist with vector design and construction. Develop Taqman qPCR platform. This is a sophisticated piece of work to develop a high throughput molecular essay that all of the projects in the lab can use as a routine process linked to our databases and trailing system. Working with a senior research scholar to develop binary vectors for plant transformation Working across the genome sciences, Lab and Genome Editing Center to co-create multiple plant transformation platforms and deliver plants through transformation and genome editing in multiple industry projects, including dealing with multiple stakeholders and presenting results weekly.

title: Extension Program Assistant-4-H Youth Development & Family & Consumer Sciences
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. While our employees are located in NC County offices, they reap the benefits of employment at NC State University. Some of our benefits include: · Paid time off · Paid tuition · Health Insurance · Flexible Scheduling · Retirement Savings · Supplemental Benefits Programs · WolfPerks! You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. Primary Function of Organizational Unit North Carolina Cooperative Extension gives our residents easy access to the resources and expertise of NC State University and NC A&T State University. Through educational programs, publications, and events, Cooperative Extension field faculty deliver unbiased, research-based information to North Carolina citizens. New Hanover County is located in southeastern North Carolina between the Cape Fear River and the Atlantic Ocean. It is the second smallest county in the state but is home to over 238,000 people. Projections predict its population to increase to almost 300,000 by 2040. The City of Wilmington is the county seat and is rich in historical significance and home to many recreational and cultural sites and events. Important contributors to the local economy include the state port, tourism, filmmaking, manufacturing, and financial technology. More information about New Hanover County Extension Center, visit their website: https://newhanover.ces.ncsu.edu Overview This position supports New Hanover County Cooperative Extension programs, specifically focusing on the delivery, administration, and coordination of positive youth development programs through 4-H and community health education through Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Duties and Responsibilities: ● School Enrichment Coordination: Lead the coordination and delivery of 4-H school enrichment programs in local schools, with a primary focus on managing the 4-H Embryology program (including teacher training, classroom presentations, and logistics). ● 4-H Club and Program Support: Assisting the 4-H Agent, providing administrative and programming support to 4-H community clubs, including volunteer management, enrollment tracking, curriculum distribution, and assisting with 4-H Teen Leaders and county, district and state level presentation events. ● Summer Camp Support: Assist with the planning, registration, marketing, and delivery of 4-H summer camps and workshops hosted at the Arboretum or off-site locations. ● Healthy Living Programming: Collaborate with the FCS Agent to deliver educational programs focused on youth healthy living, physical activity, and nutrition. ● FCS Program Support: Provide programming support for the Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) program, assisting with workshop registration, food safety or nutrition class preparation, community health outreach, and resource distribution. ● Database & Reporting: Maintain accurate records of youth enrollment, volunteer hours, and program participation; enter monthly demographic and program impact data into the Extension Reporting System (ERS). ● Communication & Marketing: Draft regular newsletter updates, social media posts, and marketing materials to promote 4-H clubs, summer camps, and upcoming FCS classes to families and schools. ● Customer Service: Provide professional, welcoming customer service by handling inquiries from parents, educators, and the public regarding youth enrollment, program schedules, and class registrations. ● Compliance & Professionalism: Maintain professionalism and confidentiality when handling youth medical forms, volunteer background checks, and program participant records, strictly following North Carolina Cooperative Extension and university policies.

CIPM fosters the development and implementation of pest management programs. CIPM works to support and further Integrated Pest Management through the evaluation of emerging technologies, information management and dissemination, environmental stewardship, estimation of economic consequences, resistance management tools and systems, and integration of disciplinary expertise. Under the direction of the Project Leader, this position provides essential research support through organizing scientific documentation, maintaining quality management records, assisting with data activities, and supporting program processes. Through careful attention to detail and application of basic scientific knowledge, you will help ensure program materials are accurate, current, and aligned with established quality standards. Your work will contribute to the reliability of diagnostic practices and the success of a program that supports plant health and agricultural protection. Key Responsibilities fall within the following four core functional areas: Scientific Documentation & Quality Management Support: Support the review, organization, and maintenance of technical documents, including work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and job aids. Assist with updates to scientific documentation to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with established quality management standards. Maintain organized records and documentation to support program compliance and operational effectiveness. Apply basic knowledge of molecular and serological diagnostic methods to support technical reviews, literature searches, and program activities. Assist with the preparation and organization of reference materials, scientific resources, and program documentation. Data Management & Reporting Support: Maintain accurate research records, laboratory documentation, and electronic data files. Support data entry, organization, and review activities to ensure information is complete and accessible for program needs. Assist with compiling data and reports that support diagnostic certification and quality management activities. Program Coordination & Operational Support: Collaborate with project leaders, quality management staff, and subject matter experts to support program priorities and deliverables. Utilize established systems and tools to manage documents, records, and program resources. Follow laboratory quality, safety, and compliance procedures while contributing to a culture of accuracy and continuous improvement. If you are a detail-oriented researcher who enjoys supporting scientific programs through accurate documentation, data management, and quality-focused processes, we invite you to apply. Join our team and contribute to a program that strengthens plant health protection by supporting reliable diagnostic practices across laboratories.
