title: Sterile Processing Assistant
description: The primary purpose of this position is to support the NC State Veterinary Hospitals by providing sterile processing services for surgical instrumentation and equipment to ensure safe, efficient, and uninterrupted patient care. This position is responsible for the decontamination, inspection, assembly, sterilization, inventory management, and distribution of surgical instruments and supplies while maintaining compliance with hospital policies and regulatory guidelines. The role also serves as a key support resource for clinical teams by delivering exceptional customer service and helping ensure the operational readiness of surgical services throughout the Veterinary Hospital. Sterile Processing & Instrument Reprocessing: Provide sterile processing support for the hospitals through the decontamination, inspection, assembly, sterilization, and distribution of surgical instrumentation and equipment in accordance with hospital and regulatory guidelines. Customer Service & Clinical Support: Deliver exceptional customer service to clinical teams by responding to questions regarding surgical packs, instrumentation availability, equipment operation, and procedural supply needs. Operating Room Coordination: Collaborate closely with Operating Room staff to support surgical scheduling, room turnover, and rapid instrument turnaround to ensure equipment and instrumentation needs are consistently met for procedures. Inventory & Systems Management: Maintain and manage surgical instrumentation, implant inventory, and component lists within ISIP Surgical to ensure accuracy, availability, and operational efficiency. Department Operations & Purchasing: Support departmental operations through coordination of equipment and instrumentation rentals, billing activities, and purchasing of implants and sterile processing supplies to maintain uninterrupted workflow and high-quality service. Professional Standards & Operations Safety & Compliance: Maintain a clean, safe, and functional workspace in accordance with OSHA, EHS, radiation safety, hospital infectious disease policies, and sterile processing standards. Team Collaboration & Communication: Participate actively in problem-solving and team advancement while working independently with sound judgment and seeking assistance when appropriate. Operational Agility & Physical Demands: Demonstrate the ability to lift up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations, work safely around potential hazards including zoonotic diseases, chemicals, and gases, and extend work hours as needed to support patient care and hospital operations.

title: Senior Lab Manager
description: The Senior Lab Manager provides strategic and operational leadership across Zeis Textile Extension’s pilot-scale textile manufacturing, testing and prototyping laboratories. This role oversees laboratory managers and supports the continued growth, modernization, and utilization of ZTE’s facilities to serve industry, research, workforce development and innovation needs. Working closely with the Zeis Director, Wilson faculty and staff as well as industry partners, the Senior Lab Manager helps position ZTE as a nationally recognized resource for applied textile innovation, technical problem solving, pilot-scale manufacturing, and workforce training. The role is responsible for advancing operational excellence, equipment strategy, laboratory safety, client engagement and business development across the organization’s technical service portfolio. Key responsibilities include: Leadership and Personnel Management Supervise all laboratory managers within ZTE (knitting lab, weaving lab, physical testing lab, dying and finishing lab, and testing and fabrication services, prototyping lab). Lead, coach, and develop the site leadership team, building a culture of accountability, responsiveness, collaboration and continuous improvement. Foster a collaborative and service-oriented culture that supports technical excellence, workforce development, and continuous learning. Manage, develop, and provide training for employees. Determine and manage staff assignments, and provide leadership and daily direction of other laboratory personnel. Represent the facility to employees, customers, partners and executives. Operations and Process Excellence Lead ZTE technical operations, including production, maintenance, safety, production quality, delivery and financial performance. Champion a Safety-First culture and ensure all labs maintain a clean and safe work environment. Update the laboratory safety plan with Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S). Serve on the Wilson College Safety Committee. Monitor and improve operational performance across laboratory utilization, project execution timelines, quality, customer responsiveness, and resource allocation. Drive operational excellence by optimizing staffing, scheduling, capacity and workflow to support production goals. Collaborate with teams to implement scalable processes and improve production flow, applying Lean, Kaizen, 5S and visual management to eliminate bottlenecks and raise operational efficiency. Business Development and Client Engagement Identify opportunities to expand technical services, pilot manufacturing capabilities and industry engagement activities. Collaborate with the Zeis Director to grow external funding, technical service revenue and strategic partnerships. Serve as the primary industry liaison for priority projects. Manage multiple laboratory resources and conduct multiple Fabrication Service Agreement (FSA) projects simultaneously, including establishing priorities in the use of laboratory resources. Prepare FSA estimates, write FSAs, coordinate and oversee work associated with the FSAs, and invoice for work performed through the business office in partnership with lab managers. Technical Expertise and Asset Management Oversee the proper and safe use of laboratory equipment and manage preventive equipment maintenance and repairs. Lead acquisitions of new equipment to modernize the laboratory and expand capabilities, soliciting quotes for new and used machinery. Keep up to date on the latest technology in the field through a strong network of machinery manufacturing contacts and by attending trade shows. Manage inventory control. Strategy and Partnership Partner with the Zeis Director and the Assistant Dean of Finance and Operations to develop and drive business planning, ensuring continuous evolution to meet customer needs. Translate the business plan into measurable KPIs and manage actions to achieve overall budget and margin targets with each associated entity ZTE. Ensure lab readiness for new equipment, technologies and capabilities through strong cross-functional alignment and disciplined change management. Collaborate with the Zeis Director, academic departments heads and college faculty to provide appropriate support for academic classes

title: ASPSA Tutor
department: 240201 - Academic Support Program for Student Athletes
description: Division of Academic and Student Affairs The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State through three integrated components: academic affairs, student affairs, and University College. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Office of Academic Support Program for Student-Athletes (ASPSA) is a comprehensive support program that strives to meet the academic, personal and professional development needs of all student-athletes, promoting excellence and effectiveness in undergraduate and graduate education as well as leadership and civic engagement. ASPSA is committed to extending the educational experience of its constituency with particular emphasis on empowering student-athletes to become strong self-advocates. We provide specialized initiatives to facilitate a smooth transition from high school to college and from college to professional life while successfully integrating student-athletes into the campus community. We strive to enhance academic skills for all student-athletes and provide personalized academic support to meet the needs of each student-athlete. ASPSA maintains a strong sense of integrity and will continue to strive to be one of the benchmark programs for academic support for all collegiate academic support programs in the nation. Primary Purpose of Position: Must be willing to learn about and abide by the North Carolina State University, NCAA, and ASPSA rules and regulations. Must be able to teach academic success strategies to a wide range of students in a one-on-one or small group setting. Must have the ability to effectively communicate verbally and have skills to develop written reports. Must be attentive to detail and accurate in record keeping. Ability to work a flexible schedule including nights and weekends. Hours available - All work is 100% IN PERSON: Sundays 12 - 3pm, 5 - 8 pm Monday - Thursdays 8am - 9pm Fridays 8am - 5pm Temporary positions are required to take a 31-day break after working 11 months.

title: Housing Facilities Work Crew
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State through three integrated components: academic affairs, student affairs, and University College. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. University Housing Facilities is seeking to fill several positions to serve as Housing Facilities Work Crew members to begin working mid-May through mid-August. They will be required to assist the General Shop and/or other trades teams by moving furniture, removing carpet, painting, cleaning HVAC units, changing filters, and completing other duties as assigned. Team members will also assist the Conference Services staff with lowering and raising beds in residence halls and delivering/retrieving items from the warehouse.

title: House Director
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State through three integrated components: academic affairs, student affairs, and University College. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life advises recognized fraternities and sororities, their governing councils, and manages Greek Village housing. The Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life prepares students for society through a values-based fraternal experience. Our work impacts the student experience in three ways: Chapter Services, Council and Community Development, and Living and Learning Environments. Fraternity and Sorority Life also provides several programs to enhance leadership development and to educate the Greek Community of over 2,800 students. The House Director will coordinate the student development and administrative functions of an Organization-Owned Fraternity or Sorority House and the community within. This position will be directly responsible for the following: Advising: Create a sense of community by promoting peer accountability among chapter residents. Provide training on university policies reinforcing community standards. Maintain a high level of visibility within the residential community for the purpose of serving as an on-site advisor to chapter residents, including but not limited to regular office hours, chapter programming, and chapter meals. Meet regularly with organization leadership, advisors, and House Corporation volunteers. Advise student residents on the development and implementation of programs, applicable policies and procedures, risk management, issues management, leadership development and organization management. Serve as a mediator to assist residents in addressing community conflicts when they arise. Maintain an environment conducive to student academic success and safety. Leadership: Provide leadership, administrative operations, programming, and facilities management in a residential house composed of about 40 residents with an additional 100 out of house student members. Make informed decisions based on a clear understanding of the impact and consequences involved. Create and maintaining an open community within the house. Serve as a communication link between Fraternity and Sorority Life, House Corporation, and residents. Exercise good judgment and remaining unbiased and impartial while addressing house issues. Participate in department decision-making regarding policies, procedures, programs, and facilities management. Oversee daily operations including facilities, overall resident management, occupancy management, financial budget management to ensure a positive, healthy and safe living-learning environment for our residents. Policy Enforcement: Respond appropriately to student concerns and addressing student issues. Follow all University Policies, Regulations, and Rules, as well as other University/Fraternity and Sorority Life Procedures, and Guidelines including but not limited to those pertaining to safety, civility, information security, and non-discrimination. Consulate with the Associate Director to refer cases to the Organizational Standards Board, Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life, CARES, Bias Incident Response or Behavior Assessment Teams, or the Office of Student Conduct. Crisis Management and On-Call Responsibilities: Make appropriate referrals to University support services ie, Student Health, Counseling Services, Behavior Assessment Team, and/or Student Ombuds. Respond to emergencies and providing leadership in crisis situations, collaborating with campus partners when appropriate. Must be onsite overnight except when prior arrangements have been made for time away. Demonstrate ability to work effectively under pressure. Practice effective communication with University administration, Organizational Leadership, and, if applicable, law enforcement or emergency personnel. Serve as a resource or referral agent for students experiencing personal concerns or crisis. Administration: Coordinate fall and spring student check-in and check-out system. Coordinate and direct the opening and closing of the house, as well as occupancy management of the facility through StarRez. Manage room assignment and room change process for the facility. Initiate change, developing, and implementing new ideas and concepts as appropriate. Participate in departmental and division programs, meetings, and committees as needed. Facilities: Coordinate inspections as required by the University, state, federal, or local agencies. Tour building and grounds on a regular basis to identify facility needs. Solicit building improvement ideas from staff and residents to share with appropriate organizational leadership and House Corporation. Working in conjunction with Fraternity and Sorority Life staff and Organizational Leadership to ensure the community is well maintained and a safe environment for residents. Work with vendors and maintenance workers to promote compliance with written agreements between the chapter and vendor; report issues of concern regarding outsourced services to the House Corporation. Assist the House Corporation representative in locating local vendors and contractors as needed and requested by the House Corporation. Work with organization leadership and meal plan vendor to establish menus for the chapter on a weekly and monthly basis. Consult with University Nutritionist as appropriate. Work with a meal vendor or catering service (when applicable) to promote compliance with written agreement between the organization and the service provider; report issues of concern regarding meal vendor or catering service to the House Corporation. Communicate periodic feedback regarding vendor provided services to the House Corporation Board and/or service vendor liaisons.

title: Grounds Crew
description: The Lonnie Poole Golf Course is seeking reliable and energetic individuals to Join our Pack as a Groundskeeper . Essential Job Duties: Landscaping and sodding Applying fertilizer and pesticides on and around the course under the direct supervision of an employee who is licensed in Ornamental & Turf Pest Control Cutting grass on the tee boxes, fairways, roughs, fringes and greens Golf course upkeep Sprinkler system maintenance, fencing and tree trimming Equipment used includes, but not limited to, walking and riding mowers, tee mowers, fairway mowers, rough mowers, rollers, bunker rakes, carts, push mowers and a variety of powered and non-powered hand tools. As a temporary employee, you are eligible for the following temporary employee perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. This is an hourly position, that includes a State required 32-day break at the end of 11 months. Superior work performance may provide an opportunity to renew employment and/or advance into a benefits eligible permanent position.

title: Accountant II
description: The Accountant II reports to the University Housing Business Officer and plays a central role in managing the financial operations that support Housing Facilities and capital projects. In this role, you will take ownership of purchasing and travel processes, ensuring transactions move smoothly while guiding staff through complex policies and requirements. Your work will directly support both daily operations and long-term planning by maintaining financial accuracy, strengthening processes, and helping the department operate more efficiently. Responsibilities fall within four key functional areas of support outlined below: Financial Operations & Oversight Manage end-to-end purchasing activities, including P-Card, marketplace, invoices, and large requisitions Oversee travel processes, including review and approval of authorizations and reimbursements Ensure accuracy, compliance, and integrity of all financial transactions Lead financial reconciliations and quarterly budget reviews for assigned areas and projects Monitor and manage departmental budgets, including support for annual budget development Procurement, Contracts & Asset Coordination Partner with Procurement to process and track large or complex purchases and contracts Lead University Housing related RFP processes Oversee service agreement renewals and billing tracking Coordinate vehicle fleet management, including registration, inspections, and compliance with Risk Management Serve as liaison for asset-related processes, including coordination with central offices Training, Guidance & Process Improvement Serve as a subject matter expert for purchasing and travel, providing training and ongoing guidance to staff Interpret and apply financial policies, ensuring consistent and compliant practices across the department Identify process gaps and implement improvements to increase efficiency and effectiveness Support development of tools and systems for tracking capital planning and financial activity Financial Analysis & Collaboration Assist with long-term capital planning and financial forecasting Compile and analyze financial data to support decision-making and reporting Partner with internal teams and central offices to resolve complex financial issues Provide support during high-volume periods across the business office, as needed If you are someone who thrives in a role where accuracy, ownership, and continuous improvement matter; who enjoys guiding others through complex processes; and who can balance detailed financial work with a broader operational perspective we encourage you to apply.

title: Plumber II
description: Are you an experienced plumber looking for an opportunity to work on a varied range of facilities while making a lasting impact on a major university campus? As a Plumber II , you will perform skilled installation, repair, maintenance, and modification of complex plumbing and piping systems that support classrooms, laboratories, offices, residence halls, and other critical campus facilities. This journey-level role offers the opportunity to apply advanced plumbing and pipefitting expertise while expanding your knowledge through exposure to secondary electrical and HVAC-related systems. If you take pride in solving complex problems, delivering quality workmanship, and supporting the infrastructure that keeps a campus community running, we encourage you to apply and join our team. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Install, maintain, repair, and modify plumbing and piping systems, including water, waste, steam, gas, chilled water, and compressed air systems. Service domestic, lab, and acid waste drainage systems, building sewers, and associated fixtures and equipment. Perform pipefitting tasks, including cutting, threading, assembling, testing, and installing piping, valves, supports, and fixtures. Conduct scheduled preventive maintenance on plumbing and related air, gas, water, and waste disposal systems. Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair boilers, pumps, steam systems, compressors, water softeners, and related equipment. Apply working knowledge of secondary electrical and HVAC-related systems , controls, and components. Ensure all work complies with Federal, State, OSHA, and Facilities Operations safety policies and procedures. Identify and address safety hazards and properly use required personal protective equipment. Communicate clearly with supervisors, coworkers, and campus customers regarding work assignments and timelines. Perform tasks that involve climbing ladders, accessing confined or elevated spaces, occasional lifting up to 60 lbs, and working in varied conditions, including exposure to areas with insects or small animals. All essential duties must be completed with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Advanced Locksmith Level 1
description: Advanced Locksmith Level 1 position will provide highly skilled technical expertise, project management, and leadership for campus locksmith operations. This role is responsible for ensuring compliance with university standards, accurately scoping projects, and efficiently allocating resources. Key Responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Serve as a technical expert , guiding, training, and coaching journey and contributing level technicians on application and installation techniques. Research critical information, including key bittings array, construction documents, and guidelines . Understand and apply master key database enrollment process and procedures . Demonstrate the ability to review and verify construction plans and hardware specifications according to established specifications and construction guidelines. Proficiently work with hardware specifications . Handle project management tasks with a working knowledge of processes and timelines. Provide cost estimates and proposals for work, which includes evaluating and researching necessary requirements from vendor sources. Monitor and track all work orders to ensure timely completion. Assist the supervisor in developing timelines and milestones by identifying critical and less critical activities. Allocate appropriate resources and time for the completion of own work and that of the team, avoiding scheduling conflicts. Communicate effectively with customers regarding the necessary scope of work . Guide Journey-level technicians, ensuring that both Journey and Contributing level technicians have sufficient resources to complete jobs.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar - DEPP
description: We seek a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Scholar to conduct research in nematode genomics and molecular plant-nematode interactions. The position will focus on both basic and translational research aimed at understanding root-knot nematode (RKN) virulence, host adaptation, and mechanisms associated with resistance breaking in crops. The major focus of the project will be characterizing virulence-associated genes in M. enterolobii and investigating their interactions with crop hosts, including sweet potato. Additional projects will involve the integration of multi-omics datasets to better understand RKN-hosts interactions. The postdoc scholar will lead both laboratory experiments and computational analyses. The work will combine molecular biology, nematology, genomics, bioinformatics, and comparative transcriptomics. Depending on research interests and project needs, the successful candidate may also contribute to functional characterization of candidate nematode genes and host- resistant associated genes. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work closely with collaborators at NC State University and other institutions Duties and Responsibilities: Conduct laboratory and greenhouse experiments related to plant-nematode interactions, nematode virulence, and host resistance Perform molecular biology experiments, including DNA and RNA extractions, PCR, qPCR, preparation of samples for genomics and transcriptomics analyses Conduct bioinformatics analyses using high-performance computing environments Maintain clear research records and contribute to reproducible bioinformatics workflows

title: Temporary Research
department: 196001 - Department of Population Health and Pathobiology
description: A research technician is needed to assist with work on pharmacokinetic and population pharmacokinetic modeling in food animal drug avoidance research.

title: Lifeguard
description: A Lifeguard is a trained and certified safety professional responsible for ensuring the safety and protection of people in and around an aquatic environment. In this role, you will ensure the safety of all users through continuous surveillance of the aquatic area. You will enforce aquatic guidelines to maintain a safe environment and be prepared to implement the Emergency Action Plan when necessary. Join our pack! Contribute Safety and Surveillance: Ensure the safety of users through continuous surveillance. Facility Inspection & Maintenance: Inspect the facility, perform preventative maintenance and report any unsafe conditions or equipment failures. Chemical Testing: Perform regular water chemistry tests and accurately log the readings to maintain water quality and compliance. Event Operations: Assist with the setup and teardown of equipment for various aquatic programs, special events and open recreation activities. Certification and Fitness: Maintain an up-to-date American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification and preserve the required fitness level (swimming skills, strength and endurance) necessary to effectively respond to all aquatic emergencies. Cleanliness: Maintain a clean and inviting aquatic environment.

title: CLAWS Fabrication Technician
description: The CLAWS Fabrication Technician will play a key role in supporting research and development activities related to III-V Power, RF, and Photonics device fabrication. The successful candidate will be responsible for hands-on execution of process flows, process module development, and data collection, contributing to the optimization of fabrication processes. This role requires a combination of practical skills in a cleanroom environment, analytical abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Responsibilities: Device Fabrication: Be responsible for hands-on execution of III-V Power, RF, and Photonics device fabrication, including full process flows, short flows, and unit processes. Process Module Development and Optimization: Work with engineering staff to develop and optimize robust process modules including: Execute Design of Experiments (DOEs) for process optimization. Identify opportunities for continuous improvement in fabrication processes. Fabrication Methods: Establish hands-on proficiency in relevant fabrication methods, including but not limited to: Photolithography Metal and dielectric deposition Etching (wet and dry) Wafer dicing Metrology and Data Analysis: Generate in-line metrology data for Statistical Process Control (SPC). Documentation: Maintain accurate and detailed records of experiments, procedures, and results. Equipment Operation and Maintenance: Operate and maintain process equipment, ensuring proper functionality and adherence to safety protocols. Collaboration: Work closely with engineers, scientists, and other technicians to achieve research objectives.

title: Anesthesia Veterinary Technician
description: Are you ready to elevate your clinical skills in a dynamic, cutting-edge teaching environment? The Anesthesia Department provides advanced anesthetic support to a varied patient population across the hospital campus, including small, large, and exotic species. This role requires advanced veterinary medical knowledge, strong time-management skills, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, teaching-focused clinical environment. The position collaborates closely with specialty services, clinicians, staff, and students to coordinate and deliver high-quality anesthetic and perioperative care. Responsibilities include comprehensive patient assessment, administration of complex anesthetic and medical treatments, continuous monitoring during diagnostic and surgical procedures, post-operative recovery, and strict adherence to infectious disease and safety protocols. This role also supports hospital operations through documentation, workflow coordination, and the training and mentoring of learners and new staff. Key Responsibilities: Advanced Patient Care & Anesthesia Support: Provide comprehensive anesthetic and peri-anesthetic care, including pre-anesthetic assessments, high-risk drug calculations, advanced monitoring, life-saving interventions, pain management, and post-operative recovery for small, large, and exotic species. Requires previous experience in a canine / feline veterinary setting. Monitoring, Equipment & Technical Proficiency: Operate, interpret, and maintain advanced anesthetic and physiologic monitoring equipment and specialized patient care devices to ensure patient safety during surgical, diagnostic, and imaging procedures. Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Coordinate care and communicate effectively with specialty services, clinicians, staff, and students across multiple hospital service areas to support complex medical and surgical cases. Education, Training & Mentorship: Orient, teach, and coach new staff, students, interns, and residents on anesthetic procedures, hospital policies, and patient care standards in a teaching-hospital environment. Documentation, Safety & Compliance: Accurately document patient care and treatments within hospital information systems while maintaining a clean, safe work environment and adhering to infectious disease protocols, OSHA, EHS, and radiation safety standards. Must have the ability to work with or around sick animals, potentially hazardous materials, cleaning chemicals, gas anesthetics, zoonotic diseases, and unpleasant odors. Physical & Operational Requirements: Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations. Ability to work beyond scheduled work hours when needed.

title: Radiation Oncology Anesthesia Technician
description: The Radiation Oncology Department provides advanced oncological support to a varied patient population across the hospital campus, including small, large, and exotic species. This position requires advanced veterinary medical knowledge, strong time-management skills, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, teaching-focused clinical environment. The position collaborates closely with specialty services, clinicians, staff, and students to coordinate and deliver high-quality anesthetic and service specific patient care needs. Responsibilities include comprehensive patient assessment, administration of complex anesthetic and medical treatments, continuous monitoring during diagnostic procedures, post-procedural recovery, and strict adherence to infectious disease and safety protocols. This role also supports hospital operations through documentation, workflow coordination, and the training and mentoring of learners and new staff. Key Responsibilities: Advanced Patient Care & Anesthesia Support Provide comprehensive anesthetic and peri-anesthetic care, including pre-anesthetic assessments, high-risk drug calculations, advanced monitoring, life-saving interventions, pain management, and recovery for small, large, and exotic species. Monitoring, Equipment & Technical Proficiency Operate, interpret, and maintain advanced anesthetic and physiologic monitoring equipment and specialized patient care devices to ensure patient safety during diagnostic, and imaging procedures. Interdisciplinary Collaboration Coordinate care and communicate effectively with specialty services, clinicians, staff, and students across multiple hospital service areas to support complex cases.. Education, Training & Mentorship Orient, teach, and coach new staff, students, interns, and residents on anesthetic procedures, hospital policies, and patient care standards in a teaching-hospital environment. Documentation, Safety & Compliance Accurately document patient care and treatments within hospital information systems while maintaining a clean, safe work environment and adhering to infectious disease protocols, OSHA, EHS, and radiation safety standards. Requires ability to lift up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Assistant Professor
description: North Carolina State University (NC State) is seeking a highly motivated and innovative individual for a tenure-track position at the level of Assistant Professor as part of the FRIB Experimental Bridge program. This unique position provides an exceptional opportunity for a dynamic researcher to thrive in a collaborative environment at the forefront of nuclear science. In this role, your professional efforts will be split between the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB) at Michigan State University (MSU) and the local facilities at NC State and the Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory (TUNL), located in Durham, North Carolina. This dual appointment offers a distinctive platform for cutting-edge research, leveraging the capabilities and resources of both renowned institutions. Key Responsibilities: Conduct cutting-edge research at FRIB, using its state-of-the-art facilities to advance the frontiers of rare isotope science. Lead an independent research program and engage in collaborative research at TUNL, where unique capabilities such as high-intensity particle beams, polarized photon beams, neutron beams, and advanced detection systems support a broad range of nuclear physics investigations. Develop a robust, externally funded research program that integrates work at both FRIB and NC State/TUNL. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses at NC State, demonstrating a commitment to excellence in education and mentorship. If you thrive in collaborative research environments and are excited by the opportunity to work alongside leading researchers while building your own research program, we invite you to apply.

title: ICU Veterinary Assistant
description: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Veterinary Assistant provides advanced nursing care within the 24/7 high-acuity unit of the Randall B. Terry Jr. Companion Animal Medical Center. Operating in a fast-paced teaching environment, this role manages a varied caseload of small animal and exotic patients. The position requires a high level of clinical expertise, professional communication, and the ability to coordinate care seamlessly between specialty services, clinicians, and students. Clinical Excellence & Patient Care Advanced Nursing Interventions: Perform complex medical treatments, including catheter placement (venous, arterial, and central), oxygen therapy (nasal/chest tubes), urinary management, and blood/plasma transfusions. Critical Monitoring & Diagnostics: Monitor vital signs (TPR, BP, ECG), manage ventilator support, and utilize specialized equipment such as pulse oximeters, wound vacuums, and ultrasound machines. Emergency Response: Perform CPR and provide immediate life-saving support for patients in crisis. Pharmacological Management: Calculate and administer high-risk medications, including constant rate infusions (CRI), intravenous fluids, and complex pain management protocols. Specialized Recovery: Manage post-anesthetic and post-surgical recovery for high-risk neurological, soft tissue, trauma, and extracorporeal patients. Infection Control: Maintain rigorous standards for isolation protocols, antibiotic-resistant cases, and infectious disease management. Coordination & Educational Support Clinical Communication: Coordinate patient admissions and care plans by synthesizing information from clinicians and students regarding diagnostics and treatment goals. Instruction & Mentorship: Actively teach, coach, and orient 4th-year veterinary students, interns, residents, and new staff on hospital policies and advanced patient care techniques. Data Management: Accurately record and communicate patient data, diagnostic results, and treatment histories using hospital information systems. Client Relations: Support and facilitate client visitations, maintaining professional empathy in emotionally charged or challenging situations. Professional Standards & Operations Safety & Compliance: Maintain a clean, functional workspace in accordance with OSHA, EHS, radiation safety, and hospital infectious disease policies. Team Collaboration: Participate actively in problem-solving and team advancement, working independently with sound judgment while requesting assistance when necessary. Operational Agility: Demonstrate the physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work around potential hazards (zoonotic diseases, chemicals, gases), and extend work hours as required by patient needs.

title: Environmental Services Technician (Housekeeper)
department: 113804 - Vernon G James Research And Extension Center
description: The primary purpose of this position is to clean and perform routine housekeeping duties at the Vernon James Center. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Clean and sanitize designated areas according to established schedules and safety protocols to ensure a hygienic environment Operate and maintain housekeeping equipment, including vacuums, mops, and scrubbers, to complete tasks Perform window washing and other seasonal cleaning tasks as needed Maintain cleaning supplies inventory and request replenishment when needed. Assist with setting up designated spaces for meetings or events Perform minor maintenance, such as replacing light bulbs and performing paint touch-ups; promptly report damages or major maintenance needs. Provide outstanding customer service, remaining professional and respectful. Lift a minimum of 60 lbs., with or without reasonable accommodations. This position requires a high degree of flexibility to respond to and coordinate with the needs of the faculty, staff, and public. Communication with the team and supervisor is critical for success. This position is located in Plymouth, NC

title: Business Services Coordinator
description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering is seeking a highly organized and customer-focused professional to serve as a key member of its Business Office. In this role, you will support both the department and the Nuclear Reactor Program (NRP) by coordinating business operations, managing financial and administrative processes, and serving as a trusted resource for faculty, staff, students, and external partners. Your work will help ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the department while contributing to an environment that supports teaching, research, and student success. Key Responsibilities: Coordinate administrative and business operations for the Department of Nuclear Engineering and the Nuclear Reactor Program. Manage complex financial transactions, purchasing, reconciliations, and related business processes while ensuring compliance with university policies and procedures. Maintain academic and graduate student records, supporting departmental programs with accuracy and attention to detail. Serve as a primary point of contact for faculty, staff, students, and external vendors by providing timely information, resolving questions, and facilitating effective communication. Support program management activities and departmental initiatives by organizing priorities, tracking deadlines, and ensuring business operations run efficiently. This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys variety, values teamwork, and finds satisfaction in creating efficient, well-organized processes. If you're a dependable professional who communicates effectively, adapts to changing priorities, and is committed to providing exceptional service, we encourage you to apply.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar- Bioelectricity Lab
description: The Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences trains doctors of veterinary medicine, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows interested in research-based careers focused on discovering new information about animal and human health and disease and using those findings to enhance animal and human health and well-being. The Bioelectricity Lab develops next generation technologies for the detection and treatment of diseases using electric field mediated phenomena. Duties and Responsibilities: The candidate for the Bioelectricity Postdoc Research Scholar position will lead large/small animal studies investigating the immunological effects a new pulsed electric field cancer therapy. The candidate will additionally lead with other experiments in the laboratory using in vitro models to investigate the effects of pulsed electric fields on biological tissues.

title: Landscape Architect
description: Campus Planning and Strategic Investment at NC State plays a vital role in optimizing the design and use of campus land, buildings, and infrastructure to support the university’s mission. Through collaboration and data-driven analysis, the team ensures financial and environmental stewardship while planning for both current and future needs. As our next Landscape Architect , you’ll help translate NC State’s strategic vision into the physical spaces that bring it to life. This position offers the opportunity to influence how our campus grows— developing innovative and sustainable solutions that enhance the student experience, foster community, and advance the university’s long-term goals. If you’re passionate about purposeful design, strategic planning, and creating spaces that inspire connection and innovation, please apply. General Scope of Duties Translate the strategic plans of the University into the physical facilities required to support them. Provide solutions for a broad range of landscape architectural and engineering planning issues essential to meeting the campus’s development needs. Provide general project support for physical facilities planning efforts at NC State. Analyze, document, and develop physical planning projects, policies, procedures, and informal project designs aligned with the University’s strategic goals. Consider and evaluate a wide range of multi-disciplinary factors, including social, economic, and environmental impacts, related to the development of the campus’s physical facilities. Coordinate planning efforts with campus design professionals to ensure alignment with long-range physical planning goals. Typical duties include: Developing physical facilities planning and design strategies for exterior campus spaces Conducting comparative studies and facilities program analyses Identifying and developing project alternatives Recommending actions to support implementation of the Physical Master Plan, with a focus on exterior spaces and site design Preparing feasibility studies and physical development plans for campus components such as stormwater management, infrastructure, transportation systems, pedestrian access, and other general planning and development needs Develop, monitor, and update project budgets to ensure alignment with project scope and funding requirements Verify budget adequacy for scope of work and review/approve consultant invoices in accordance with University standards Establish and maintain comprehensive project schedules and documentation, including meeting minutes key stakeholder communications

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: We are a dynamic research team focused on elucidating the molecular mechanisms of plant-virus-vector interactions. Our mission is to develop new foundational knowledge of plant viruses and to translate this information into new control strategies and biotechnology tools for crop improvement. Grapevine red blotch disease has emerged as a major threat to winegrape production throughout North America in recent decades. We aim to develop tools and protocols for grapevine red blotch virus (GRBV) detection in insects and plants. We will integrate these new technologies with established methods to better understand GRBV localization in the insect vector throughout circulative transmission and make strides in understanding GRBV latency in grapevine and experimental plant hosts. The detection tools developed will also have applications for red blotch diagnostics. Duties and Responsibilities: The postdoctoral research scholar will express GRBV proteins in prokaryotic and eukaryotic (insect and plant) cells and purify proteins for antibody production. (50%) Characterize GRBV dissemination and tissue tropism in insect vectors with in situ methods. (50%) Molecular analysis of viral genomes, gene expression, and gene function. Primer design, DNA/RNA handling, protein expression, Western blotting. Develop and test standardized procedures for determining vector competence on candidate vectors.

title: SEVIS Data and Compliance Analyst
description: The SEVIS Data and Compliance Analyst will work to ensure NC State compliance with all the maintenance of F-1 and J-1 records in SEVIS in accordance with federal regulations under the supervision of the Interim SEVIS Systems and Compliance Manager. The SEVIS Data and Compliance Analyst will serve as an authorized school official for student (DSO for F-1) and exchange visitor (ARO for J-1) programs, working individually and with other OIS staff to ensure compliance with immigration regulations and reporting requirements. They will run database queries and reports to support NC State's federally mandated Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) reporting to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and submit event based and periodic reporting to SEVIS as required. Data Management and Regulatory Compliance 60% Act as a Designated School Official (DSO) and Alternate Responsible Officer (ARO) as required to perform event based and periodic reporting. Under the direction of the Interim SEVIS Systems & Compliance Manager, synthesize data from multiple sources to manage the new student registration process, identify potential compliance issues for new students, and generate routine reports on expected arrivals for stakeholders. Perform as delegated the registration process for all returning F-1 and J-1 students. In coordination with the Interim SEVIS Systems and Compliance Manager, review and resolve student & scholar alerts in SEVIS and Sunapsis such as changes of curriculum and level, address changes, or assign to advisor for review Perform delegated SEVIS-related database maintenance and data clean-up services Run queries in SIS and Sunapsis to assist with data compliance and institutional reporting Remain current with SEVIS-related and regulatory updates pertaining to international students and scholars to ensure institutional compliance. Advise international students and scholars to the extent necessary to move them through OIS processes and procedures. Electronic Business Services Maintenance & Development 30% Assist in monitoring the effectiveness of new processes, assisting with technical documentation for end users. Coordinate continual updates and maintenance of standard Sunapsis email texts with advisors. Manage departmental and administrative user access Assist clients and departments with questions related to access to Sunapsis and eForm submission, Sunapsis pin resets, merging records and eForm resets Participate in training OIS staff in use of advisor-related SEVIS and Sunapsis functions. Assist in preparing campus-wide Sunapsis training and on-going production support including documentation to be used for training and on-going reference. Assist with maintenance of campus-wide electronic business process documentation and update as needed due to updates in MyPack, Sunapsis, OnBase, SEVIS and other database systems, as well as changes in internal OIS processes and procedures. Act as University back-up on all topics related to Sunapsis/Global Home. Other duties 10% Back up the Intake Specialist as needed during illness/vacation in assigning cases to advisors Attend and provide technical assistance to policies and procedures discussions with advisors Provide back-up support to the front desk as needed. Assist with communicating process updates and providing training to departments and other campus stakeholders. Attend conferences and give conference presentations when needed. Perform all other duties as assigned. This position is scheduled for 29 hours per week though work outside of standard hours may be required due to business needed.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Community Sport Development
description: The Department of Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management (PRTM) in the College of Natural Resources at North Carolina State University invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor with expertise in community sport development. We are seeking an innovative scholar and educator whose research explores the role of sport in strengthening communities through sustainable development, cultural engagement, health and well-being, youth development, economic impact, or related areas. In this role, you will shape the future of community sport development through impactful research, meaningful teaching, and collaboration with students, colleagues, and community partners. You'll have the opportunity to develop or expand a nationally recognized research program, mentor the next generation of sport leaders, and translate scholarship into practice through partnerships that improve communities across North Carolina and beyond. As part of NC State's land-grant mission, your work will extend beyond the classroom—creating lasting connections between the university, industry, and communities while contributing to innovative solutions with local, national, and global impact. Key responsibilities include: Develop Research by or expanding a high-impact scholarly research program that attracts external funding and contributes to the field of community sport development. Teach and Mentor undergraduate and graduate students through engaging instruction, student mentorship, and supervision of research and scholarly activities. Publish and Disseminate research through peer-reviewed publications, professional presentations, and other scholarly activities that advance knowledge and practice. Collaborate with faculty, community organizations, industry partners, and government agencies to foster interdisciplinary research and strengthen community engagement. Shape Academic Programs by contributing to curriculum development, continuous program improvement, and innovative learning opportunities across the department. Serve the University and Profession through departmental, college, and university committees, professional organizations, and public service activities that support NC State's land-grant mission. If you are an innovative scholar who thrives on collaboration, values student success, and is committed to advancing community sport development through impactful research and engagement, we encourage you to apply.

title: Extension Agent, 4-H Youth Development (Assistant, Associate or Full Agent)
description: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. What we offer: Health Insurance Tuition waiver for university coursework Attend non-revenue generating sporting events for free. Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare discounts , Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community. Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered. The position may be hired at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Agent level if the selected candidate meets the required qualifications. Primary Function of Organizational Unit North Carolina Cooperative Extension gives our residents easy access to the resources and expertise of NC State University and NC A&T State University. Through educational programs, publications, and events, Cooperative Extension field faculty deliver unbiased, research-based information to North Carolina citizens. The 4-H Agent provides leadership for the overall 4-H Youth program, planning, implementing, and evaluating initiatives for youth ages 5 to 19. In this role, the agent establishes and maintains traditional 4-H clubs, school enrichment, summer camps, and after-school programs that engage youth in positive life-skill development. The agent is also responsible for overseeing the mandated 4-H Military Program at Fort Bragg. The position will be responsible for working with adult volunteers to design, develop, implement and evaluate programs that meet the needs and interests of youth ages 5-19 to engage them in positive, informal life-skill development activities using a variety of educational methods such as organized 4-H clubs, school enrichment, 4-H summer programs, and after-school programs. This position also recruits, evaluates, trains and coordinates adult and teen volunteers. In addition, this position will be responsible for supervising the overall 4-H program which includes establishing and maintaining 4-H clubs within Cumberland County, recruiting and training present and potential volunteers, manage clubs and special programs, such as Empowering Youth and Families (EYFP), and identifying resources to assist in conducting the 4-H program. Responsibilities will include supervision of program staff and management of programs funded through grants and fees. Located in southeastern NC, Cumberland County has a strong military presence and a viable agricultural economy. The county includes its seat, the City of Fayetteville, and is home to Fort Bragg—the nation's largest military installation. The local agricultural industry is made up of small family farms producing livestock and crops, including soybeans, corn, tobacco, etc. Additionally, the county is home to the fifth-largest school district in the state, serving approximately 49,000 students across 86 schools. For additional information, visit cumberlandcountync.gov . Duties and Responsibilities: Manage and grow the 4-H Youth Development program through clubs, afterschool programs, school enrichment programs, summer fun day camps and traditional 4-H camps. Assist the Livestock Agent with the annual Cumberland County Livestock show. Seek out sponsorships, grants, and other funding sources to support activities and programs. Ensure the 4-H program is accessible to youth across the county. Duties include developing and maintaining 4-H clubs, special interest youth programs, and school enrichment programs. Responsibilities will include recruiting and managing volunteers as well as evaluating and reporting impacts of program efforts. The successful candidate will have a background in digital skills and STEM to focus on developing those skills in county youth. The applicant must be self-directed and possess a strong work ethic with skills in leadership, communication, grantsmanship, public relations, planning, implementation, and evaluation. As a member of the Cumberland County Extension staff the individual in this position will recognize the importance of teamwork and fully support the total Extension program.

title: Extension Agent, Ag, Field Crops and Dairy (Assistant, Associate or Full Agent)
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Working for NC State Extension allows you to teach without being tied to a classroom and school bell. Check out this video on what it’s like to work for NC State Extension. Some of our benefits include: · Paid time off · Paid tuition · Health Insurance · Flexible Scheduling · Retirement Savings · Supplemental Benefits Programs · WolfPerks! You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. Primary Purpose of Position The agent in this position will provide leadership for field crops and dairy programs in Iredell County and proactively conduct need assessments and program evaluations to provide future direction for the program. The County Extension Agent is a member of the faculty of North Carolina State University. The County Extension Agent has primary responsibility for planning, executing, and evaluating that phase of county Extension programs within assigned areas of program responsibility. This position provides leadership for the development, implementation and evaluation of an effective educational program to meet the needs of the county population in the following areas of responsibility: field crops (corn, small grains, cotton, and soybeans), pesticide education, and dairy producer education. This position will serve as the county pesticide coordinator and assist with educational training opportunities for private operators to obtain and maintain their licenses. The agent will be expected to develop specific educational programs and to collaborate with other Extension staff, agencies, groups, and organizations in order to more effectively reach intended audiences throughout the county. North Carolina Cooperative Extension gives our residents easy access to the resources and expertise of NC State University and NC A&T State University. Through educational programs, publications, and events, Cooperative Extension field faculty deliver unbiased, research-based information to North Carolina citizens. Iredell County is located in the central Piedmont region of North Carolina, just north of Charlotte and bordering Lake Norman, and has a population of approximately 206,000. Agriculture has a significant economic impact on the County, generating an estimated $662 million annually, including over $165 million in cash gate receipts from more than 1,055 farms. Iredell County is the leading county in the state for dairy production and ranks first in all cattle (both beef and dairy) and first in corn silage production, making it a hub for dairy and livestock operations in North Carolina. Field crops including soybeans, wheat, and corn are also widely grown throughout the county, supporting the local dairy and beef cattle industries as well as regional grain markets. Other agricultural commodities include hay (fifth in the state), poultry, cotton, viniferous grapes, strawberries, and nursery and ornamental plant production. With close proximity to Charlotte and Lake Norman, there is a large and growing suburban presence in the southern half of the county, creating unique challenges and opportunities for preserving working farmland alongside nearby quality of life amenities not usually found in a rural area. Duties and Responsibilities: The person selected for this position will be responsible for educational programming and technical assistance related to all phases of field crop production and pesticide education. The person selected will also be expected to conduct on-farm research work in the areas of corn, soybeans, cotton, and wheat production. In addition, the person selected for this role will be responsible for educational programing and technical assistance related to dairy production, animal waste operator certifications, and youth dairy programing.

title: Pharmacist
description: This position works in the Pharmacy service for the Veterinary Hospital. The incumbent ensures safe, effective, and legally compliant drug therapy. Serves as the final check when dispensing inpatient medications, outpatient medications, cytotoxic agents, and compounded preparations to all customers of the VH pharmacy.

title: Executive Director of Gift Planning
description: Reporting to the Assistant Vice Chancellor for University Development, the Executive Director for Gift Planning serves as the university’s senior leader for gift planning, providing strategic direction, oversight, and execution of a comprehensive, campus-wide program. The Executive Director partners across Advancement to integrate gift planning into fundraising strategy, supports complex and deferred gifts, and ensures alignment with institutional priorities and industry best practices.

title: Catering Event Coordinator
description: Rave! Catering is looking for an organized, high-energy Event Coordinator to join our premier catering team. Rave! Catering proudly employs experienced, certified chefs and catering professionals dedicated to delivering the highest level of service. We don't expect you to know everything on day one. Our dedicated, expert team is ready to provide hands-on, on-the-job training to help you thrive, grow, and lead. Key Responsibilities: Mastermind the Logistics : Translate event visions into reality. You will organize staff, equipment, and logistics, utilizing Catertrax to proactively build equipment lists and event floor plans. Ensure Flawless Execution: Stay one step ahead by making sure every linen, fork, and menu item is ordered, on-hand, and ready to go before the guests arrive. Lead and Inspire: Supervise events on-site. On some days, you’ll run lean, independent events; on others, you will lead a large service team to execute a flawless dining experience. Deliver "Rave" Service: Act as the friendly, professional face of Rave! Catering, building relationships with university clients and following up to ensure their expectations were exceeded. Be a Collaborative Pack Member: Support the broader NC State Dining mission by stepping in to assist at other campus dining locations when unique business needs arise. We offer flexible schedules and opportunities for learning, growth, and promotion. Superior work performance may provide an opportunity to renew employment and/or advance into a benefits-eligible permanent position. NC State Dining provides campus-wide food services to students, staff, and faculty on the North Carolina State University Campus. NC State Dining operates 10 cafes, 3 food courts, 6 dining halls, 4 markets, 1 restaurant, vending, a nutritional counseling service, and a catering department. The department employs approximately 1000 temporary and student employees and approximately 180 permanent EHRA and SHRA employees.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology supports teaching, research, and extension programs in fundamental plant biology and microbiology, including basic and applied research, teaching graduate and undergraduate courses, mentoring graduate and undergraduate students, and outreach to state and national clientele. Duties and Responsibilities: The postdoctoral researcher will lead the development and optimization of SCRIBE , a novel programmable reversible transcriptional switch for use in plant systems. The successful candidate will design and generate molecular constructs, optimize transcriptional switch performance using transient expression systems, and implement the technology as a transcriptional recorder of root developmental processes in Arabidopsis . The position involves designing and conducting independent research experiments, analyzing and interpreting experimental data, troubleshooting molecular and genetic approaches, maintaining accurate research documentation, and contributing to manuscripts, grant proposals, and scientific presentations. The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with Drs. Alonso and Stepanova while collaborating with laboratory members and external collaborators to advance project objectives.
